|     Scientific Review Board   |                       |    Core Engineering Team      |
| - Prior-art vetting           |                       | - API architecture            |
| - Statistical evaluation      |                       | - CI/CD & release engineering |
| - Reproducibility checks      |                       | - Performance profiling       |
+-------------------------------+                       +-------------------------------+

docs.title: 3.1 Principal Product Architect
docs.text:
• Responsibilities:
  • Custodian of the overall product vision, API consistency, and roadmap execution.
  • Final authority on scope management, dependency additions, and framework interoperability design.
  • Ensures clean-room engineering standards, licensing hygiene, and developer ergonomic consistency across all pillars.

docs.title: 3.2 Technical Research Lead
docs.text:
• Responsibilities:
  • Guardian of scientific integrity, mathematical correctness, and empirical benchmarking rigor.
  • Approves algorithm designs, prior-art evaluations, and baseline comparison protocols.
  • Enforces negative-result preservation and ensures no premature superiority claims are published.

docs.title: 3.3 Scientific Review Board (Advisory)
docs.text:
• Responsibilities:
  • Independent peer review of proposed algorithmic novelties and benchmark methodologies.
  • Review of mathematical formulations in Phase 6 prior to code implementation in Phases 8–11.
  • Validation of statistical significance testing across benchmark suites.

docs.title: 3.4 Core Maintainers & Contributors
docs.text:
• Responsibilities:
  • Code implementation, unit testing, documentation authoring, and performance optimization.
  • Adherence to the Developer Certificate of Origin (DCO) and coding standards.

docs.title: 4. RFC (Request for Comments) & Design Review Process
docs.text:
To introduce major algorithms, new architectural abstractions, or breaking API changes, contributors must follow the structured RFC process:

  1. RFC Creation:
  2. Author forks the repository and creates an RFC document in docs/rfcs/RFC-YYYYMMDD-title.md detailing:
    • Problem statement and motivation.
    • Mathematical formulation and theoretical guarantees (or limits).
    • Prior-art citations and comparison with existing literature.
    • Proposed API design and signature.
    • Empirical validation plan (datasets, baselines, metrics, compute budgets).
  3. Community & Review Period:
  4. Minimum 14-day open commentary period for community, Core Engineering Team, and Scientific Review Board review.
  5. Formal Decision & Sign-off:
  6. RFC requires unanimous approval from the Principal Product Architect (API & Scope) and the Technical Research Lead (Science & Mathematics).
  7. Decisions are codified in docs/foundation/DECISIONS.md.

docs.title: 5. Engineering Standards & Quality Gates
docs.text:
Every code contribution must pass through four strict validation gates:

+------------------+     +-------------------+     +------------------+     +-------------------+
|  Gate 1: Typing  | --> |  Gate 2: Coverage | --> |  Gate 3: Memory  | --> | Gate 4: Benchmark |
|  mypy --strict   |     |  >= 90% unit test |     |  Valgrind / mprof|     |  Statistical seed |
|  Zero suppress   |     |  clean execution  |     |  no memory leaks |     |  5+ random seeds  |
+------------------+     +-------------------+     +------------------+     +-------------------+
  • Typing Integrity: Full PEP 484 type annotations; no untyped Any without documented architectural rationale.
  • Test Coverage: Comprehensive unit tests covering nominal, edge-case, and corrupted input conditions.
  • Resource Constraints: Unit test suite must execute cleanly on a standard dual-core CPU with \(\le 4\text{ GB}\) RAM in under 10 minutes.
  • Clean Code & Linting: Strict adherence to ruff, black, and zero lint warnings.

docs.title: 6. Financial, Trademark, and Legal Boundaries
docs.text:
• Not-for-Profit Scientific Mission: AdaptiveML is established as a public-good, open-source library.
  • Provisional Trademark Warning: The codename "AdaptiveML" is strictly provisional. No commercial entities or organizations may register this name until formal legal searches (WIPO, USPTO) are completed in Phase 3 and Phase 16.
  • No Cloud Vendor Affiliation: AdaptiveML maintains strict neutrality across cloud providers (AWS, Google Cloud, Microsoft Azure, Oracle Cloud). No vendor-specific SDKs or services will ever be introduced into the core library.

docs.title: 7. Charter Amendments
docs.text: This Charter may only be amended by joint consensus of the Principal Product Architect and Technical Research Lead, documented via a versioned pull request and recorded in docs/foundation/DECISIONS.md.

docs.title: AdaptiveML: Research Governance & Evidence Standards
docs.text: Document Status: Approved Baseline (Phase 0 Deliverable) Working Codename: AdaptiveML (Provisional — Subject to formal legal and trademark clearance) Document Identifier: DOC-FDN-005 Last Updated: 2026-11-01 Target Audience: Researchers, scientific advisory board, core engineers, external scientific contributors

docs.title: 1. Philosophical Foundations & Code of Scientific Integrity
docs.text:
The field of machine learning research is frequently burdened by unverified novelty claims, irreproducible benchmarks, selective data pruning, and exaggerated marketing.

The core mission of AdaptiveML demands uncompromised scientific discipline. Every line of algorithmic code, mathematical formulation, and benchmark report must adhere to rigorous research governance.

docs.title: 2. The Ten Inviolable Research Governance Rules
docs.text: Every contributor, maintainer, and scientific researcher working on AdaptiveML must comply with these ten mandatory rules:

docs.title: Rule 1: Strict Separation of Established Facts from Hypotheses
docs.text:
• Any scientific assertion must be explicitly categorized as an Established Fact (supported by verified peer-reviewed literature or formal mathematical proof) or a Working Hypothesis (an assumption or conjecture currently under empirical investigation).
  • Language in documentation and papers must not conflate theoretical expectations with demonstrated empirical reality.

docs.title: Rule 2: Mandatory Citation of Original Research Sources
docs.text:
• No algorithmic concept, loss formulation, or optimization technique may be introduced into the repository without full bibliographic attribution to its original academic literature.
  • Citations must include: Author(s), Title, Conference/Journal, Year, and DOI / ArXiv identifier. Derivative implementations must explicitly cite the foundational papers (e.g., Robbins-Monro, Polyak, Duchi et al., Kingma & Ba, Kirkpatrick et al., Zhang & Sabuncu, Northcutt et al.).

docs.title: Rule 3: Algorithmic Novelty Claim Restriction
docs.text:
• No author, pull request, or documentation page may claim "algorithmic novelty" without a formal, documented prior-art search across IEEE, ACM, NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, and patent databases.
  • Prior-art investigations are formally conducted during Phase 2 (Novelty & Prior-Art Research) and Phase 4 (Comprehensive Literature Review). Until both phases are completed and signed off by the Technical Research Lead, all proposed algorithms are treated as research hypotheses or engineering adaptations.

docs.title: Rule 4: Algorithmic Superiority Claim Restriction
docs.text:
• No contributor or publication may assert that an AdaptiveML algorithm is "superior", "state-of-the-art", "faster", or "more accurate" than an existing baseline without:
  • A statistically powered benchmark suite across standard public datasets.
  • A minimum of 5 independent randomized seeds with reported standard errors / confidence intervals.
  • Paired two-tailed statistical significance testing (\(\alpha = 0.01\)).
  • Fully reproducible scripts, seeds, and hardware environment specifications documented in benchmarks/.

docs.title: Rule 5: Compulsory Preservation of Negative Experimental Results
docs.text:
• If an algorithm fails to converge, demonstrates inferior sample efficiency, underperforms standard baselines (e.g., standard Adam or standard ERM), or breaks under specific distributional shifts, this outcome must not be suppressed or deleted.
  • Negative results must be cataloged in docs/research/NEGATIVE_RESULTS_REGISTRY.md with detailed analysis of the failure modes. Understanding failure regimes is as scientifically valuable as positive results.

docs.title: Rule 6: Prohibition Against Discarding Rare Samples
docs.text:
• In Pillar 2 (RLA) and Pillar 1 (ALA), algorithms must not treat difficult-to-learn or minority-class samples as "noise" or "outliers" simply because they exhibit high initial training loss.
  • Algorithms must preserve valid tail distributions and extreme minority classes. Filtering mechanisms must be evaluated specifically for class-imbalance bias.

docs.title: Rule 7: Strict Independence of Algorithm Pillars
docs.text:
• Pillar 1 (ALA), Pillar 2 (RLA), and Pillar 3 (RAO) must remain strictly independent and usable in complete isolation.
  • No algorithmic contribution in one pillar may introduce runtime imports, dependencies, or required configurations from another pillar. Synergies between pillars may only be explored through the Unified Learning Controller (ULC).

docs.title: Rule 8: Prohibition Against Mandatory Framework Dependencies
docs.text:
• Core algorithmic implementations must run using only Python standard library and NumPy.
  • PyTorch, scikit-learn, SciPy, or other external frameworks must never be made mandatory runtime dependencies of the core package. Any framework-specific integrations must reside in dedicated optional adapter modules (adaptiveml.integrations.*) guarded by lazy import hooks.

docs.title: Rule 9: Prohibition Against Telemetry, Cloud Lock-In, or Mandatory Remote Services
docs.text:
• The codebase must never introduce phone-home telemetry, usage metrics tracking, remote license verification, or mandatory cloud infrastructure dependencies.
  • Every algorithm must be executable entirely offline in an air-gapped, local-first environment on commodity CPU hardware.

docs.title: Rule 10: Legal, IP, and Trademark Findings Preliminary Disclaimer
docs.text:
• All findings regarding patents, copyright provenance, trademark availability, and licensing compatibility recorded in Phase 0 or subsequent technical documents are preliminary engineering assessments.
  • No legal finding is binding until formally reviewed and ratified by qualified intellectual property legal counsel during Phase 3 and Phase 16.

docs.title: 3. Experimental Reproducibility Protocol
docs.text:
To ensure 100% scientific reproducibility, all experiments conducted in Phase 12 and beyond must adhere to the standardized Reproducibility Checklist:

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       REPRODUCIBILITY ARTIFACT BUNDLE                         |
+---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+
| 1. Exact Environment Lockfile         | poetry.lock / requirements-lock.txt   |
| 2. Seed Specification                 | Array of explicit integer seeds       |
| 3. Raw Data Manifest                  | SHA-256 hashes of input datasets      |
| 4. Hardware & OS Telemetry            | CPU model, RAM, OS kernel, NumPy BLAS |
| 5. Unprocessed Raw Metrics            | JSON / CSV logs of all step metrics   |
| 6. Statistical Analysis Script        | R / Python script computing CI and p  |
+---------------------------------------+---------------------------------------+

docs.title: 3.1 Random Seed Control
docs.text:
• All benchmark drivers must execute across a fixed array of seeds: [42, 1337, 2026, 9999, 88888].
  • No global random.seed() or np.random.seed() pollution is permitted. Benchmarks must pass seed-specific np.random.Generator instances directly to estimators.

docs.title: 3.2 Hardware Environment Logging
docs.text:
• Every benchmark log must automatically record:
  • CPU model string and core count (e.g., Intel Core i7-12700H, 14 cores or Apple M2 Pro, 10 cores).
  • System physical RAM and swap configuration.
  • Operating system release and kernel version.
  • BLAS/LAPACK runtime library linked to NumPy (numpy.show_config()).

docs.title: 4. Enforcement & Review Process
docs.text:
• Any pull request violating these governance rules will be blocked by the Technical Research Lead.
  • Violations of Rule 5 (suppression of negative results) or Rule 4 (unverified superiority claims) represent scientific misconduct under this charter and will require immediate retraction or remediation.

docs.title: AdaptiveML: Comprehensive Risk Register
docs.text: Document Status: Approved Baseline (Phase 0 Deliverable) Working Codename: AdaptiveML (Provisional — Subject to formal legal and trademark clearance) Document Identifier: DOC-FDN-008 Last Updated: 2026-11-01 Target Audience: Project leadership, risk committee, maintainers, legal advisors

docs.title: 1. Risk Management Framework
docs.text: AdaptiveML maintains an active, continuously monitored Risk Register. Risks are evaluated across five critical domains: 1. Technical: Architecture, performance, numerical stability, dependencies, and platform execution. 2. Scientific: Algorithmic convergence, empirical baseline competitiveness, and theoretical validity. 3. Product & DX: API ergonomics, market adoption, user onboarding friction, and documentation clarity. 4. Legal & Intellectual Property: Trademark clearance, patent collision, licensing contamination, and provenance. 5. Operational & Governance: Contributor capacity, maintainer bandwidth, CI/CD infrastructure, and release velocity.

docs.title: 1.1 Severity Assessment Matrix
docs.text: Risk Severity is derived from Probability and Impact: - Critical (Red): High Impact + High Probability (Requires immediate architectural intervention). - High (Orange): High Impact + Med Probability OR Med Impact + High Probability (Requires active mitigation plan). - Medium (Yellow): Med Impact + Med Probability OR High Impact + Low Probability (Continuous monitoring). - Low (Green): Low Impact + Low/Med Probability (Standard operational oversight).

docs.title: 2. Active Risk Register
docs.text: Risk ID Category Risk Description Prob. Impact Severity Mitigation Strategy Contingency Plan Status / Owner RSK-TEC-001 Technical CPU Step Latency Bottlenecks: Python/NumPy execution overhead may cause step latency to exceed acceptable interactive thresholds without C/Rust kernels. Medium High High Profile core loops; utilize vectorized NumPy/BLAS operations; restrict Python object allocation inside hot loops. Introduce optional compiled PyO3/Rust or C extensions via cffi in post-v0.1 phases with pure Python fallbacks. Open / Tech Arch Lead RSK-TEC-002 Technical Numerical Instability in Quantized States: Compressing optimizer state accumulators (RAO) to sub-16-bit may introduce gradient variance and training divergence. High High Critical Implement dynamic stochastic rounding and numerical clamping bounds; validate on standard non-convex loss surfaces. Provide automatic fallback to 32-bit state when gradient norm exceeds numerical safety thresholds. Open / Tech Arch Lead RSK-TEC-003 Technical Framework Coupling Creep: Optional frameworks (PyTorch, scikit-learn) inadvertently leak into core algorithmic modules, breaking minimalist dependency rules. Medium Medium Medium Enforce CI lint rules (import-linter) preventing adaptiveml.core from importing torch or sklearn. Isolate integrations strictly in adaptiveml.integrations.* behind explicit lazy-loading guards. Open / Principal Architect RSK-SCI-001 Scientific Inability to Outperform Baselines: Proposed algorithms fail to show statistically significant improvements over tuned standard baselines (Adam, EWMA, Cleanlab). Medium High High Rigorous baseline tuning in Phase 5 & 6; identify niche Pareto boundaries (e.g., performance per megabyte of RAM rather than pure accuracy). Document negative results transparently in benchmark reports; pivot algorithmic focus to hybrid Pareto efficiency. Open / Tech Research Lead RSK-SCI-002 Scientific Tail Sample Discarding in RLA: Noise detection filters misclassify rare minority-class samples as corrupt labels, degrading fairness and long-tail accuracy. High High Critical Incorporate margin-aware and feature-neighborhood density metrics that protect low-density clusters from noise rejection. Flag high-loss rare samples for human review / fallback weighting rather than hard pruning. Open / Tech Research Lead RSK-PRD-001 Product High Cognitive Friction in API: Combining three pillars (ALA, RLA, RAO) might produce an overly complex, unidiomatic API that confuses developers. Medium High High Adhere strictly to familiar scikit-learn (fit/partial_fit) and PyTorch (Optimizer) API patterns. "5-line quickstart" rule. Conduct UX interviews with external ML engineers during Phase 15 before GA release. Open / Principal Architect RSK-PRD-002 Product Competition from Single-Pillar Tools: Specialized single-purpose tools (e.g., River for streaming, bitsandbytes for quantization) outcompete unbundled pillars. High Medium High Emphasize CPU-first execution, zero GPU kernel compilation requirements, and seamless modularity under ULC. Provide direct benchmark comparisons highlighting deployment simplicity and minimal dependency footprint. Open / Principal Architect RSK-LEG-001 Legal / IP Trademark Collision on "AdaptiveML": Prior existence of companies or trademarks (e.g., Adaptive ML SAS or similar entities) creates brand collision or PyPI namespace lock. High High Critical Treat "AdaptiveML" strictly as a provisional codename; conduct formal USPTO/WIPO searches in Phase 3; do not publish to PyPI. Pre-screen fallback namespaces (e.g., pyadaptiveml, aml-core, adaptml-lib) during Phase 3. Open / Legal Counsel RSK-LEG-002 Legal / IP Patent Collision in Reduced-Memory Optimization: Existing patents or patent applications by commercial institutions on quantized optimizer states or drift algorithms. Medium High High Conduct comprehensive patent prior-art searches in Phase 2 across USPTO and EPO; rely exclusively on public domain academic literature. Redesign mathematical formulations in Phase 6 to circumvent proprietary patent claims. Open / Legal Counsel RSK-LEG-003 Legal / IP Contributor IP Contamination: External contributors submit code containing proprietary, GPL-licensed, or trade secret material. Low High Medium Mandate DCO 1.1 sign-off (Signed-off-by) on all git commits; enforce clean-room academic re-implementation guidelines. Immediate quarantine and git history rewriting if contaminated code is detected. Open / Principal Architect RSK-OPS-001 Operational Maintainer Burnout & Bandwidth Limits: A 22-phase roadmap requires sustained engineering effort; volunteer or small-team bandwidth may stall execution. High Medium High Enforce strict phase gates; limit MVP scope strictly to tabular and streaming core in Phases 8–10; defer complex multimodal extensions. Recruit academic co-maintainers and institutional contributors post-Phase 12. Open / Leadership Council RSK-OPS-002 Operational Reproducibility Bit-Rot: Changes in upstream dependencies (NumPy, Python minor releases) cause benchmark results to drift or fail over time. Medium Medium Medium Pin exact dependency versions in benchmarks/poetry.lock; run automated monthly reproducibility test suite in CI. Store raw benchmark logs and seed traces as versioned release assets. Open / Core Maintainers

docs.title: 3. Governance & Risk Review Cadence
docs.text:
• Weekly Review: Engineering-level risks (RSK-TEC, RSK-OPS) are reviewed weekly during sprint planning.
  • Phase Gate Review: Prior to signing off on any Acceptance Gate in the 22-phase roadmap, all associated risks must be evaluated and re-scored.
  • Escalation Path: Any risk escalating to Critical Severity triggers an immediate architecture freeze until a ratified mitigation or contingency plan is executed.

docs.title: AdaptiveML: 22-Phase Master Development Roadmap
docs.text: Document Status: Approved Baseline (Phase 0 Deliverable) Working Codename: AdaptiveML (Provisional — Subject to formal legal and trademark clearance) Document Identifier: DOC-FDN-007 Last Updated: 2026-11-01 Target Audience: All engineering, research, product, and leadership stakeholders

docs.title: 1. Roadmap Architecture & Execution Principles
docs.text:
The development of AdaptiveML is structured into 22 sequential, gate-enforced phases (Phases 0 through 21).

To safeguard technical excellence, prevent premature code commits, and guarantee research integrity: 1. Strict Phase Gating: No phase may begin execution until the formal Acceptance Gate of all preceding prerequisite phases has been reviewed, verified, and signed off. 2. Clean Separation of Formulation and Code: Mathematical design (Phase 6) and technical architecture (Phase 7) must be fully established and peer-reviewed before any algorithmic source code is written in Phases 8–11. 3. Evidence Before Release: No package may be released or published (Phase 17/18) without reproducible empirical benchmarking against standard baselines (Phase 12) and legal release audits (Phase 16).

Phase Overview (Phases 0 to 21):
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ RESEARCH & FOUNDATION (Phases 0 - 6)                                   │
│  0: Foundation -> 1: Market -> 2: Prior Art -> 3: Legal ->             │
│  4: Lit Review -> 5: Gap ID -> 6: Math & Algorithm Design              │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ARCHITECTURE & CORE IMPLEMENTATION (Phases 7 - 11)                     │
│  7: Tech Arch -> 8: ALA Dev -> 9: RLA Dev -> 10: RAO Dev -> 11: ULC    │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ EMPIRICAL VALIDATION & INTEGRATION (Phases 12 - 15)                    │
│  12: Benchmarking -> 13: Frameworks -> 14: Prod Eng -> 15: Docs & DX   │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ AUDIT, RELEASE & PUBLICATION (Phases 16 - 19)                          │
│  16: Legal Audit -> 17: Alpha/Beta -> 18: PyPI 1.0 -> 19: Publication  │
├────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ECOSYSTEM & CONTINUOUS R&D (Phases 20 - 21)                            │
│  20: Global Ecosystem -> 21: Continuous R&D                            │
└────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Phase 0: Project Foundation
docs.text:
• Objective: Establish the formal identity, project charter, research governance, scope, success criteria, and repository foundation.
  • Deliverables:
  • README.md
  • Complete docs/foundation/ documentation bundle (10 foundation documents).
  • Clean initialized repository with .gitignore and baseline configurations.
  • Prerequisites: Workspace initialization.
  • Acceptance Gate: All 10 foundation documents created, validated for consistency, with zero algorithm source code created prematurely.

docs.title: Phase 1: Product & Market Research
docs.text:
• Objective: Conduct systematic market and user analysis of existing adaptive, robust, and resource-efficient ML tools (e.g., River, Cleanlab, bitsandbytes, Avalanche).
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/research/MARKET_ANALYSIS.md
  • User persona profiles, pain-point mappings, and feature comparison matrix.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 0 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Thorough review of at least 8 competing or complementary open-source libraries detailing gaps, performance characteristics, and developer ergonomic weaknesses.

docs.title: Phase 2: Novelty & Prior-Art Research
docs.text:
• Objective: Perform exhaustive patent and literature searches to identify established IP, existing algorithm formulations, and potential novelty boundaries.
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/research/PRIOR_ART_REPORT.md
  • Patent landscape overview (USPTO, EPO, WIPO) for optimizer compression and stream drift detection.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 1 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Formal sign-off by Technical Research Lead that proposed techniques do not violate third-party patents and that novelty claims are clearly bounded.

docs.title: Phase 3: Legal & IP Assessment
docs.text:
• Objective: Engage legal/IP review for name clearance, trademark availability, licensing compatibility, and contributor agreements.
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/legal/TRADEMARK_AND_NAME_CLEARANCE.md
  • Formal open-source licensing opinion and DCO compliance framework.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 2 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Explicit decision on package naming (either clearance of "AdaptiveML" or selection of an unencumbered alternative namespace).

docs.title: Phase 4: Comprehensive Literature Review
docs.text:
• Objective: Deep academic survey of foundational and contemporary literature across concept drift (ALA), noisy labels/robust loss (RLA), and memory-efficient optimization (RAO).
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/research/LITERATURE_REVIEW.md (minimum 50+ annotated academic citations).
  • BibTeX repository of foundational papers.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 2 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Peer-reviewed bibliography covering theoretical foundations from 1950 to 2026.

docs.title: Phase 5: Research Gap Identification
docs.text:
• Objective: Synthesize literature review findings into explicit, actionable research gaps where existing algorithms fail under CPU or local-first constraints.
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/research/RESEARCH_GAPS.md
  • Formal hypotheses backlog linking each gap to proposed algorithmic interventions.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 4 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Identification of at least 3 distinct algorithmic opportunities across ALA, RLA, and RAO with documented failure modes of existing methods.

docs.title: Phase 6: Mathematical & Algorithm Design
docs.text:
• Objective: Derive and document the formal mathematical specifications, loss functions, update equations, and theoretical bounds for all planned algorithms.
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/research/MATHEMATICAL_SPECIFICATIONS.md
  • LaTeX mathematical proofs, pseudo-code algorithms, and convergence analyses.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 5 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Scientific Review Board sign-off confirming mathematical correctness and soundness of pseudo-code before code implementation begins.

docs.title: Phase 7: Technical Architecture
docs.text:
• Objective: Define the high-level and detailed software architecture, modular interfaces, package hierarchy, typing protocols, and test harnesses.
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/architecture/SYSTEM_ARCHITECTURE.md
  • Abstract base classes, typing.Protocol specifications, and packaging architecture.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 6 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Architecture approved by Principal Product Architect; interface contracts verified to guarantee complete independence of pillars.

docs.title: Phase 8: ALA Development (Adaptive Learning Algorithms)
docs.text:
• Objective: Implement core streaming, concept drift detection, and knowledge retention algorithms in pure Python/NumPy.
  • Deliverables:
  • adaptiveml/ala/ module with drift detectors, stream estimators, and forgetting controllers.
  • Comprehensive unit test suite (tests/unit/test_ala.py).
  • Prerequisites: Phase 7 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: \(\ge 90\%\) test coverage, mypy --strict compliance, scikit-learn compatible partial_fit API, zero imports from RLA/RAO.

docs.title: Phase 9: RLA Development (Robust Learning Algorithms)
docs.text:
• Objective: Implement robust loss functions, sample reliability estimators, and outlier-resistant learning routines in pure Python/NumPy.
  • Deliverables:
  • adaptiveml/rla/ module with noise-tolerant losses, sample weighting, and outlier mitigation.
  • Comprehensive unit test suite (tests/unit/test_rla.py).
  • Prerequisites: Phase 7 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: \(\ge 90\%\) test coverage, strict typing, verification of rare-sample preservation under class imbalance, zero imports from ALA/RAO.

docs.title: Phase 10: RAO Development (Resource-Aware Optimization)
docs.text:
• Objective: Implement memory-reduced optimizer states, compressed accumulators, and CPU-efficient step routines.
  • Deliverables:
  • adaptiveml/rao/ module with low-memory optimizers and resource profilers.
  • Comprehensive unit test suite (tests/unit/test_rao.py).
  • Prerequisites: Phase 7 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: \(\ge 90\%\) test coverage, strict typing, verified memory reduction on CPU test models, zero imports from ALA/RLA.

docs.title: Phase 11: Unified Learning Controller (ULC)
docs.text:
• Objective: Implement the optional coordination layer mediating ALA, RLA, and RAO without compromising pillar independence.
  • Deliverables:
  • adaptiveml/ulc/ module with arbitration engines and state telemetry.
  • Integration test suite (tests/integration/test_ulc.py).
  • Prerequisites: Phases 8, 9, 10 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Successful coordinated execution on combined drift + noise data streams; verified that ALA, RLA, and RAO remain 100% functional standalone.

docs.title: Phase 12: Research Experiments & Benchmarking
docs.text:
• Objective: Execute rigorous empirical evaluations comparing all algorithms against standard baselines across standardized public datasets.
  • Deliverables:
  • benchmarks/ execution scripts, raw data logs, and reproducible runner notebooks.
  • docs/research/EMPIRICAL_BENCHMARK_REPORT.md with multi-seed stats, confidence intervals, and negative results log.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 11 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Minimum 5 random seeds, Wilcoxon significance testing (\(p < 0.01\)), baseline comparisons against scikit-learn, PyTorch, and established tools.

docs.title: Phase 13: Framework Integrations
docs.text:
• Objective: Implement zero-overhead, lazy-loaded interoperability wrappers for PyTorch and scikit-learn.
  • Deliverables:
  • adaptiveml/integrations/torch/ (PyTorch optimizer and loss modules).
  • adaptiveml/integrations/sklearn/ (scikit-learn Transformer and Estimator wrappers).
  • Integration test suites (tests/integrations/).
  • Prerequisites: Phase 12 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Passing all standard scikit-learn estimator checks (check_estimator) and PyTorch optimizer contract tests.

docs.title: Phase 14: Production Engineering
docs.text:
• Objective: Harden CI/CD pipelines, package distribution builds, multi-platform wheel generation, and security auditing.
  • Deliverables:
  • GitHub Actions CI matrix (Linux, macOS, Windows across Python 3.10–3.13).
  • Security audit via pip-audit and Bandit; reproducible build configuration in pyproject.toml.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 13 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: 100% green CI matrix across all OS/Python variants; zero security vulnerabilities; wheel installation validated in clean environments.

docs.title: Phase 15: Documentation & Developer Experience
docs.text:
• Objective: Build comprehensive developer documentation, API reference manuals, architectural deep dives, and quickstart tutorials.
  • Deliverables:
  • MkDocs / Sphinx documentation portal.
  • Interactive Jupyter tutorials running out-of-the-box on CPU.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 14 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Complete documentation build with zero broken links, 100% public API docstring coverage, and verified 5-line quickstart execution.

docs.title: Phase 16: Legal & Release Audit
docs.text:
• Objective: Conduct final legal clearance, license dependency audits, trademark verification, and release governance review.
  • Deliverables:
  • docs/legal/FINAL_RELEASE_AUDIT.md.
  • Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and verified NOTICE / LICENSE attribution files.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 15 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Formal written approval by legal/compliance counsel certifying zero IP risk and clean namespace.

docs.title: Phase 17: Alpha & Beta Releases
docs.text:
• Objective: Publish tagged pre-releases (v0.1.0a1, v0.9.0b1) for closed and open community testing.
  • Deliverables:
  • TestPyPI distribution and beta feedback tracking issue tracker.
  • Community bug remediation and usability patch sets.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 16 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Resolution of all critical and high-priority beta bug reports; stability validation over minimum 30-day testing window.

docs.title: Phase 18: PyPI 1.0 Release
docs.text:
• Objective: Official public general availability (GA) release of AdaptiveML v1.0.0 on PyPI.
  • Deliverables:
  • Official PyPI release, Conda-Forge feedstock, release notes, and announcement artifacts.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 17 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Clean automated release pipeline via GitHub Actions trusted publishing (OIDC); verified pip install on all target OS platforms.

docs.title: Phase 19: Research Publication
docs.text:
• Objective: Draft, submit, and publish scientific papers documenting the algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and benchmark results in peer-reviewed venues (e.g., JMLR, NeurIPS, ICML).
  • Deliverables:
  • Open-access paper preprints (ArXiv) and peer-reviewed journal/conference submissions.
  • Open-source benchmark repository matching publication experiments.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 18 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Formal acceptance or open-access preprint publication with persistent DOI.

docs.title: Phase 20: Global Ecosystem Growth
docs.text:
• Objective: Expand community adoption, establish institutional partnerships, organize workshops, and onboard community maintainers.
  • Deliverables:
  • Contributor mentorship program, monthly community syncs, and ecosystem partner integrations.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 19 sign-off.
  • Acceptance Gate: Active external contributor community and third-party production adoptions.

docs.title: Phase 21: Continuous R&D
docs.text:
• Objective: Ongoing research and development into next-generation adaptive algorithms, advanced quantization schemes, and emerging foundation model adaptation techniques.
  • Deliverables:
  • Quarterly research roadmaps, RFC cycles, and minor/major version releases.
  • Prerequisites: Phase 20 ongoing.
  • Acceptance Gate: Sustained maintenance cadence, zero backward compatibility regressions without deprecation cycles.

docs.title: AdaptiveML: Scope and Requirements
docs.text: Document Status: Approved Baseline (Phase 0 Deliverable) Working Codename: AdaptiveML (Provisional — Subject to formal legal and trademark clearance) Document Identifier: DOC-FDN-004 Last Updated: 2026-11-01 Target Audience: Product managers, software architects, core engineers, test leads

docs.title: 1. Scope Definition & Boundary Matrix
docs.text:
AdaptiveML establishes explicit boundaries across releases to maintain technical excellence and prevent scope creep.

+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                    SCOPE BOUNDARY TAXONOMY                                       |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+-----------------------+
| IN SCOPE (Must-Have for v0.1-v1.0) | SECONDARY (Post-v1.0 Considerations)| OUT OF SCOPE (Strict) |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+-----------------------+
| - Pure Python/NumPy core routines  | - Distributed multi-node training   | - Cloud-hosted SaaS   |
| - Standard CPU-first execution     | - Automatic neural architecture     | - Proprietary cloud   |
| - Standalone ALA, RLA, RAO pillars |   search (NAS)                      |   SDK requirements    |
| - Optional ULC orchestration       | - Complex multimodal cross-attention| - Re-implementing     |
| - scikit-learn API compatibility   |   adaptation                        |   autograd / PyTorch  |
| - PyTorch optimizer wrappers       | - Specialized neuromorphic hardware | - GUI dashboards      |
| - Tabular, stream, vision, NLP     |   compilation                       | - Telemetry tracking  |
+------------------------------------+-------------------------------------+-----------------------+

docs.title: 2.1 Pillar 1: Adaptive Learning Algorithms (ALA)
docs.text:
• FR-ALA-001 (Streaming Update Interface): The system must provide estimators that accept non-stationary data streams sequentially via a standard partial_fit(X, y) method.
  • FR-ALA-002 (Drift Detection Engine): The library must implement statistical drift detection primitives (monitoring error rate distributions and input covariate shifts) outputting calibrated p-values or divergence statistics.
  • FR-ALA-003 (Regulated Forgetting & Retention): The system must provide configurable retention policies (e.g., parameter elasticity, reservoir memory buffers) that constrain catastrophic forgetting while enabling adaptation to new regimes.
  • FR-ALA-004 (Decoupled Execution): All ALA components must function independently without importing or invoking RLA, RAO, or ULC modules.

docs.title: 2.2 Pillar 2: Robust Learning Algorithms (RLA)
docs.text:
• FR-RLA-001 (Loss Functions for Noisy Labels): The system must provide robust loss functions bounded or symmetric under label noise regimes, compatible with both PyTorch (torch.nn.Module) and NumPy vectorized computations.
  • FR-RLA-002 (Sample Reliability Scoring): The system must support sample weighting mechanisms that estimate label confidence \(w_i \in [0, 1]\) based on historical prediction dynamics without user-specified clean validation sets.
  • FR-RLA-003 (Rare-Sample Preservation): The system must distinguish between true noise and rare tail samples, preventing the systematic deletion or suppression of legitimate minority-class data.
  • FR-RLA-004 (Outlier-Resilient Estimators): The system must provide robust estimators resistant to extreme non-Gaussian covariate outliers.
  • FR-RLA-005 (Decoupled Execution): All RLA components must function independently without importing or invoking ALA, RAO, or ULC modules.

docs.title: 2.3 Pillar 3: Resource-Aware Optimization (RAO)
docs.text:
• FR-RAO-001 (Memory-Reduced Optimizer States): The system must implement optimization routines that compress, factor, or quantize first- and second-moment state accumulators to achieve lower memory overhead than standard 32-bit Adam.
  • FR-RAO-002 (Pure CPU Optimization Execution): RAO optimizers must run natively on commodity x86_64 and ARM64 CPUs without requiring CUDA compilation, external C/C++ build steps, or GPU hardware.
  • FR-RAO-003 (Dual API Compatibility): RAO optimizers must provide:
  • A PyTorch-compatible torch.optim.Optimizer interface (step(), zero_grad(), state_dict()).
  • A standalone NumPy-native functional step method step(params, grads, state) for non-PyTorch environments.
  • FR-RAO-004 (Decoupled Execution): All RAO components must function independently without importing or invoking ALA, RLA, or ULC modules.

docs.title: 2.4 Pillar 4: Unified Learning Controller (ULC)
docs.text:
• FR-ULC-001 (Optional Orchestration): The system must provide an optional controller that unifies ALA, RLA, and RAO, dynamically arbitrating adaptation speed, noise filtering, and memory allocation.
  • FR-ULC-002 (Non-Invasive Architecture): The ULC must treat ALA, RLA, and RAO as pluggable, interchangeable components via standard abstract interfaces (Protocol / ABC).
  • FR-ULC-003 (Telemetry & Status Reporting): The ULC must provide an inspectable diagnostic state object containing current drift statistics, noise estimates, memory consumption, and controller action logs.

docs.title: 3.1 Hardware, Platform & Execution NFRs
docs.text:
• NFR-PLAT-001 (CPU-First Execution): Every algorithmic routine must run efficiently on commodity CPUs (minimum dual-core, 4 GB RAM). No algorithm may mandate GPU access for basic functionality.
  • NFR-PLAT-002 (Cross-Platform Support): Support Linux (Ubuntu 20.04+, Debian 11+, RHEL 8+), macOS (macOS 12+ on Apple Silicon and Intel), and Windows (Windows 10, 11).
  • NFR-PLAT-003 (Python Version Compatibility): Strict support for Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, and 3.13.

docs.title: 3.2 Dependency & Packaging NFRs
docs.text:
• NFR-DEP-001 (Minimal Mandatory Core): The core package runtime dependencies must be restricted strictly to:
  • Python standard library.
  • numpy >= 1.24.0.
  • NFR-DEP-002 (Optional Ecosystem Integration): All external framework dependencies must be packaged as optional extras:
  • adaptiveml[torch]: PyTorch integrations.
  • adaptiveml[sklearn]: scikit-learn estimators and pipeline compatibility tests.
  • adaptiveml[scipy]: Advanced scientific / statistical distribution functions.
  • adaptiveml[all]: Complete development and integration test suite.
  • NFR-DEP-003 (Lazy Framework Imports): Core modules must never import torch or sklearn at module top-level. Optional adapters must import lazily and provide informative ImportError messages when the optional dependency is missing.

docs.title: 3.3 Security, Privacy & Compliance NFRs
docs.text:
• NFR-SEC-001 (Zero Telemetry): The library must not include any network calls, usage tracking, telemetry, or remote telemetry logging.
  • NFR-SEC-002 (Safe Model Serialization): Standard model serialization must not rely on unvalidated Python pickle. Models must support safe serialization formats (JSON parameter schemas, Safetensors, or explicit array dictionaries).
  • NFR-SEC-003 (Vulnerability Scanning): The codebase must maintain zero known high/critical CVEs in dependencies, verified in CI using pip-audit or Bandit.

docs.title: 3.4 Scientific Reproducibility NFRs
docs.text:
• NFR-REP-001 (Strict Determinism): Given identical input data, identical hyperparameter configurations, and a fixed integer random_state, all algorithms must produce deterministic results on identical CPU architectures.
  • NFR-REP-002 (Isolated Random Generators): Global random states (np.random.seed()) must never be modified by the library. Algorithms must instantiate and encapsulate private numpy.random.Generator instances.

docs.title: 3.5 Software Quality & Maintainability NFRs
docs.text:
• NFR-MAINT-001 (Typing Coverage): 100% type annotation coverage enforced via mypy --strict.
  • NFR-MAINT-002 (Test Coverage): Minimum 90% unit test coverage for core algorithmic logic.
  • NFR-MAINT-003 (CI Speed): Standard test suite must execute completely on a standard 2-core GitHub Actions runner in \(\le 10\) minutes.

FR-RLA-001..005 adaptiveml.rla Phase 9 Unit tests verify noise loss bounds and sample weighting isolation. docs.title: AdaptiveML: Success Criteria & Evaluation Standards
docs.text: Document Status: Approved Baseline (Phase 0 Deliverable) Working Codename: AdaptiveML (Provisional — Subject to formal legal and trademark clearance) Document Identifier: DOC-FDN-003 Last Updated: 2026-11-01 Target Audience: Core engineering team, scientific evaluators, peer reviewers, open-source contributors

docs.title: 1. Principles of Evaluation
docs.text:
To maintain absolute scientific integrity and avoid common pitfalls of AI library claims (such as cherry-picked benchmarks, unverified performance statistics, and synthetic metric manipulation), AdaptiveML enforces the following primary rule:

[!IMPORTANT] TARGET VS. ACHIEVED RESULT DISTINCTION Every quantitative performance threshold specified in this document is a rigorous engineering target. No metric may be reported or advertised as an "achieved result" until Phase 12 (Research Experiments & Benchmarking) is fully completed, peer-reviewed, and reproduced across multiple independent environments.

docs.title: 2.1 Theoretical Correctness & Mathematical Grounding
docs.text:
• Target SC-SCI-01 (Formulation Rigor): Every implemented algorithm must have a formal mathematical specification in docs/research/ detailing objective functions, gradient expressions, state update formulas, and known convergence boundaries.
  • Target SC-SCI-02 (Convergence Guarantees): For optimization routines in RAO, asymptotic convergence guarantees under standard convexity/L-smoothness assumptions must be documented. Where non-convexity precludes theoretical guarantees, empirical stability bounds must be defined.
  • Target SC-SCI-03 (Hypothesis Tracking): Research hypotheses must be documented in a central hypotheses registry prior to benchmarking. Post-hoc hypothesis justification ("HARKing") is strictly prohibited.

docs.title: 2.2 Standard Baseline Comparisons
docs.text:
Every pillar must be evaluated against established, canonical open-source baselines on standardized public benchmark datasets:

Pillar Algorithm Domain Established Baselines for Comparison Benchmark Datasets / Environments ALA Concept Drift & Stream Adaptation - Exponentially Weighted Moving Average (EWMA)- DDM / EDDM drift detectors- Elastic Weight Consolidation (EWC)- Experience Replay / Reservoir Sampling - Electricity (ELEC2)- Forest CoverType- Synthetic Rotating Hyperplane / SEA- Split-MNIST / Permuted-MNIST RLA Robust Risk & Label Noise Filtering - Standard ERM (Cross-Entropy / MSE)- Generalized Cross Entropy (Zhang & Sabuncu)- Symmetric Cross Entropy (Wang et al.)- Cleanlab (Confident Learning baseline)- Isolation Forest / Huber Loss - Noisy CIFAR-10 / CIFAR-100 (symmetric & asymmetric 20%–60%)- Clothing1M / WebVision (real noise)- Corrupted California Housing (regression) RAO Resource-Aware Optimization - Standard Adam / AdamW (\(32\text{-bit}\))- SGD with Momentum (\(32\text{-bit}\))- Adafactor- bitsandbytes 8-bit Adam (where CPU-compatible) - ResNet-18 / MobileNetV3 (image)- Mini-Transformer / GPT-2 small (language)- Large Tabular MLP benchmarks ULC Coordinated Adaptation - Sequential naive combination of baselines- Uncoordinated greedy pipelines - Synthetic Non-Stationary Dirty Stream (combined drift + label noise)

docs.title: 2.3 Statistical Rigor & Significance Testing
docs.text:
• Target SC-SCI-04 (Multi-Seed Replicates): Benchmark evaluations must run over a minimum of 5 independent, randomly sampled seeds (recommended: 10 seeds).
  • Target SC-SCI-05 (Dispersion Reporting): Reporting only mean values is forbidden. Every metric must report the mean accompanied by standard deviation, 95% bootstrap confidence intervals, and interquartile range (IQR).
  • Target SC-SCI-06 (Hypothesis Testing): Claims of algorithm superiority must be validated using paired two-tailed statistical tests (e.g., Wilcoxon signed-rank test for non-parametric distributions or paired Student's t-test where normality is established) with a significance threshold of \(\alpha = 0.01\).
  • Target SC-SCI-07 (Compulsory Negative Results): If an algorithm fails to outperform a baseline, degrades on specific data regimes, or experiences instability, this negative result must be formally published in the benchmark report. Hiding or deleting negative results is a violation of research governance.

docs.title: 3. Engineering & Performance Success Criteria
docs.text:
All performance targets are calibrated for commodity, standard CPU hardware (e.g., 4-core to 8-core modern x86_64 / ARM64 processors with 8 GB to 16 GB RAM).

+-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                    ENGINEERING PERFORMANCE TARGETS                                    |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| Metric                   | Engineering Target Threshold   | Verification Method                       |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
| RAO Memory Reduction     | >= 30% to 50% state reduction  | Memory profiling via memory_profiler and  |
|                          | vs. standard 32-bit Adam       | tracemalloc on standardized model weights |
| ALA Drift Detection Lag  | <= 100 samples detection lag   | Measured step delta on synthetic drift    |
|                          | on abrupt concept drift        | benchmark generators (e.g. SEA concepts)  |
| RLA Noise Resilience     | Maintains >= 85% clean-label   | Test accuracy retained under 30% uniform  |
|                          | accuracy under 30% noise       | symmetric label noise on CIFAR-10/Tabular |
| CPU Step Latency         | <= 1.25x of standard baseline  | Benchmarked step wall-clock time on       |
|                          | compute overhead               | identical CPU runtime                     |
| Core Test Coverage       | >= 90% unit test coverage      | pytest --cov across all core modules      |
| Type Safety              | 100% strict compliance         | mypy --strict passing with zero errors    |
| CI Execution Speed       | <= 10 minutes total            | GitHub Actions standard 2-core CPU runner |
+--------------------------+--------------------------------+-------------------------------------------+

docs.title: 4. Developer Experience (DX) & Ergonomic Criteria
docs.text:
• Target SC-DX-01 (Frictionless Onboarding): A new user must be able to install AdaptiveML, import an estimator or optimizer, train on a sample array, and obtain predictions in \(\le 5\) lines of standard Python code: 
    import adaptiveml as aml
import numpy as np

X, y = np.random.randn(100, 10), np.random.randint(0, 2, 100)
model = aml.rla.RobustClassifier()
model.fit(X, y)
predictions = model.predict(X)
  • Target SC-DX-02 (API Consistency):
  • All supervised estimators must implement scikit-learn standard estimator conventions (fit, predict, predict_proba, score, and partial_fit where streaming is supported).
  • All optimizers intended for neural networks must adhere to standard PyTorch torch.optim.Optimizer interface patterns while maintaining standalone fallback execution under pure NumPy.
  • Target SC-DX-03 (Documentation Quality):
  • 100% of public classes, methods, and functions must have Google-style docstrings with explicit type signatures, parameter descriptions, return specifications, and mathematical equation references where applicable.
  • Every pillar must provide a minimum of 2 complete, self-contained tutorial notebooks capable of executing entirely on a standard CPU within 3 minutes.
  • Target SC-DX-04 (Zero Mandatory Cloud or Hardware Dependencies):
  • The library must install and pass all tests without CUDA, ROCm, MPI, AWS SDKs, GCP SDKs, or network connectivity.

docs.title: 5. Software Quality & Installation Reliability
docs.text:
• Target SC-ENG-01 (Installation Reliability): Zero installation failures across standard supported platforms:
  • Linux (x86_64, aarch64 / ARM64)
  • macOS (Apple Silicon / M-series and Intel)
  • Windows 10 / 11 (x86_64)
  • Target SC-ENG-02 (Dependency Isolation):
  • Mandatory runtime dependency footprint: Python standard library + numpy >= 1.24.0.
  • Optional framework integrations (torch, scikit-learn, scipy) must be strictly optional extras (pip install adaptiveml[torch]). Importing adaptiveml without PyTorch or scikit-learn installed must succeed cleanly without warning or error.
  • Target SC-ENG-03 (Packaging Standards):
  • Modern pyproject.toml configuration compliant with PEP 517 / PEP 518 / PEP 621.
  • Automated wheel builds and source distribution validation using build and twine check.

docs.title: 6. Phase Acceptance Gate Tracking
docs.text: Criterion Group Gate Verification Phase Mandatory Preconditions for Gate Sign-off Mathematical Formulation Phase 6 Written convergence proofs or analytical formulations vetted by Scientific Review Board. Algorithmic Implementation Phases 8–11 Modular unit-tested code with 90%+ coverage, strict typing, zero cross-pillar leakage. Scientific Validation Phase 12 5+ seeds, baseline comparisons, confidence intervals, negative results registry documented. Framework Integration Phase 13 scikit-learn estimator tests passing; PyTorch optimizer hooks verified. Security & Release Audit Phase 16 Legal clearance, trademark review, vulnerability scanning, license dependency audit clean. docs.title: Your First Adaptive Model
docs.text: In this guide, we dive deeper into configuring the AdaptiveClassifier and ReliabilityWeightedADWIN for real-time streaming adaptation.

docs.title: The Prequential Evaluation Protocol
docs.text:
Traditional machine learning uses a static train/test split (e.g., 80% train, 20% test). In streaming data, this is impossible because data arrives sequentially and indefinitely over time.

Instead, streaming systems use Prequential Evaluation (Test-Then-Train):

[Incoming Sample (x_t, y_t)]
            |
            v
1. Predict: y_hat = model.predict(x_t)
            |
            v
2. Score:   loss = evaluate(y_hat, y_t)
            |
            v
3. Update:  model.partial_fit(x_t, y_t)

This guarantees an unbiased estimate of generalization performance without requiring a separate held-out test split.

docs.title: Configuring the Hoeffding Tree Classifier
docs.text:
AdaptiveClassifier is based on Hoeffding Trees (streaming decision trees that split nodes incrementally using the Hoeffding Bound theorem):

from adaptive_ml.ala import AdaptiveClassifier

clf = AdaptiveClassifier(
    n_features=10,        # Number of input dimensions
    n_classes=2,          # Target classes (binary or multi-class)
    grace_period=20,      # Number of samples between split attempts
    delta=0.001,          # Confidence parameter for Hoeffding bound
    tie_threshold=0.05,   # Split tie-breaking threshold
)

docs.title: Parameter Explanations
docs.text:
• grace_period: How many samples a leaf node must observe before attempting a split. Smaller values split faster but increase computation; larger values save CPU.
  • delta: Probability that the chosen split attribute is not the true optimal attribute. Smaller delta values require more statistical evidence before splitting.

docs.title: Complete Working Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.ala import AdaptiveClassifier, ReliabilityWeightedADWIN

np.random.seed(101)
n_features = 5
clf = AdaptiveClassifier(n_features=n_features, n_classes=2, grace_period=15)
adwin = ReliabilityWeightedADWIN(delta=0.005)

# Simulate 300 streaming events
for step in range(300):
    # Features
    x = np.random.randn(1, n_features)
    # Ground truth (class 1 if sum of features is positive)
    y = np.array([int(np.sum(x) > 0)])

    # 1. Prequential prediction
    probs = clf.predict_proba(x)
    pred = int(np.argmax(probs))

    # 2. Track drift
    adwin.update(float(pred != y[0]))

    # 3. Model learning update
    clf.partial_fit(x, y)

print("Classifier completed 300 steps cleanly.")

docs.title: Your First Unified Streaming Pipeline
docs.text:
In production applications, individual components (drift detection, sample reliability, and experience replay) must be coordinated to prevent oscillation and catastrophic forgetting.

The Unified Learning Controller V5 (UnifiedLearningControllerV5) provides turnkey coordination across all pillars.

docs.title: Turnkey Coordination with ULC-v5
docs.text: UnifiedLearningControllerV5 combines: 1. Prequential prediction and error tracking. 2. Statistical drift detection (ReliabilityWeightedADWIN). 3. Class-balanced experience replay buffer (ClassBalancedReservoirReplay). 4. Concept fingerprinting and historical snapshot memory (RecurringConceptMemory). 5. Five-tier intervention arbitration (NOOP, Damping, Concept Restore, Soft Replay Reset, Hard Reset). 6. Anti-thrashing exponential cooldown backoff.

docs.title: Complete Working Example
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.ulc import UnifiedLearningControllerV5, ULCv5Config

# 1. Configure the unified controller
config = ULCv5Config(
    grace_period=20,
    delta=0.002,
    similarity_threshold=0.80,
    base_cooldown=5,
    replay_capacity=500,
)

# 2. Instantiate controller for 4 features, 2 classes
controller = UnifiedLearningControllerV5(n_features=4, n_classes=2, config=config)

print("Starting ULC-v5 streaming processing...")

# 3. Process batches of incoming streaming data
np.random.seed(42)
w = np.array([1.5, -2.0, 0.5, 1.0])

for step in range(50):
    # Micro-batch of 8 streaming samples
    X_batch = np.random.randn(8, 4)
    y_batch = (X_batch @ w > 0).astype(int)

    # Execute prequential step: evaluation, arbitration, and learning
    directive, telemetry = controller.step(X_batch, y_batch)

    if step % 10 == 0:
        print(
            f"Step {step:02d}: Action={directive.action_name:<18} "
            f"Tier={directive.tier.value:<22} "
            f"Error={telemetry['mean_error']:.2f} "
            f"Replay={telemetry['replay_size']}"
        )

print("ULC-v5 pipeline completed successfully!")

docs.title: Inspecting Telemetry
docs.text: The second return value of controller.step(X, y) is a detailed telemetry dictionary: - step: Monotonically increasing stream step. - tier: The intervention tier selected by utility scoring (TIER_0_NOOP, TIER_1_PARAM_DAMPING, etc.). - action: Human-readable description of the action taken. - mean_error: Prequential batch error rate. - replay_size: Current number of stratified samples retained in the reservoir replay buffer. - concepts_stored: Count of distinct historical concept signatures saved in memory. - cooldown_remaining: Remaining lockout steps preventing controller thrashing.

docs.title: Optional Integrations & Extras
docs.text: AdaptiveML isolates optional frameworks using Python dependency extras. If an optional feature is accessed when the required dependency is not installed, AdaptiveML raises a clear ConfigurationError explaining how to install the extra.

docs.title: 1. PyTorch Integration ([torch])
docs.text:
Enables tensor-quantized optimizers and PyTorch loss functions.

pip install "aml-core[torch]"

Provides: - VectorizedLowMemoryAdamW: 8-bit block-quantized AdamW for PyTorch parameters. - TorchFocalLoss & TorchGeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss: Robust loss functions for noisy-label neural training. - TorchCheckpointAdapter: Safe checkpoint conversion to PyTorch state_dict.

docs.title: 2. Scikit-Learn Integration ([sklearn])
docs.text:
Enables integration into Scikit-Learn pipelines and transformers.

pip install "aml-core[sklearn]"

Provides: - SklearnAdaptiveClassifier: Wrapper implementing BaseEstimator and ClassifierMixin. - SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer: Transformer tracking stream drift inside a pipeline. - SklearnReliabilityFilter: Sample-weighting filter for noisy data streams.

docs.title: 3. SafeTensors Persistence ([safetensors])
docs.text:
Enables fast, zero-copy, zero-pickle binary tensor persistence.

pip install "aml-core[safetensors]"

Provides: - save_state(filepath, tensors, metadata, auth_key): Atomic twin-file serialization (.safetensors + .meta.json). - load_state(filepath, verify_integrity, auth_key): Verified loading with SHA-256 integrity and HMAC-SHA256 signatures.

docs.title: 4. Tabular DataFrames ([dataframe])
docs.text:
Enables zero-copy and batch conversions between Pandas/Polars DataFrames and NumPy arrays.

pip install "aml-core[dataframe]"

Provides: - Direct ingestion of Pandas DataFrame and Polars DataFrame into DatasetContract. - Automatic column type validation and NumPy array conversion.

docs.title: 5-Minute Quickstart
docs.text: This hands-on quickstart demonstrates how to train, evaluate, and monitor a continuous adaptive classifier in under five minutes.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Install the minimal core distribution:

pip install aml-core

docs.title: 2. Complete Runnable Script
docs.text:
Save the following code as quickstart.py and run it:

import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml import AdaptiveClassifier, ReliabilityWeightedADWIN

# 1. Generate synthetic stream with an abrupt concept inversion at step 200
np.random.seed(42)
n_samples = 400
n_features = 4

X = np.random.randn(n_samples, n_features)
# Early regime (steps 0-199): class 1 if feature 0 is positive
y_early = (X[:200, 0] > 0).astype(int)
# Drifted regime (steps 200-399): class 1 if feature 0 is negative (inversion)
y_drift = (X[200:, 0] < 0).astype(int)
y = np.concatenate([y_early, y_drift])

# 2. Initialize streaming classifier and statistical drift detector
clf = AdaptiveClassifier(n_features=n_features, n_classes=2, grace_period=10)
detector = ReliabilityWeightedADWIN(delta=0.01)

print("Starting streaming prequential evaluation...")

# 3. Stream processing loop
detected_drifts = []
correct_predictions = 0

for i in range(n_samples):
    x_i = X[i : i + 1]
    y_i = y[i : i + 1]

    # Step A: Prequential prediction (test before train)
    prob = clf.predict_proba(x_i)
    pred = int(np.argmax(prob))

    if pred == y_i[0]:
        correct_predictions += 1

    # Step B: Monitor error rate for distribution drift
    is_error = float(pred != y_i[0])
    if detector.update(is_error):
        print(f"--> [ALERT] Concept drift statistically detected at sample {i}!")
        detected_drifts.append(i)

    # Step C: Incrementally update model on current sample
    clf.partial_fit(x_i, y_i)

accuracy = correct_predictions / n_samples
print("--------------------------------------------------")
print(f"Total Stream Samples:  {n_samples}")
print(f"Overall Accuracy:      {accuracy:.2%}")
print(f"Detected Drift Points: {detected_drifts}")
print("Quickstart completed successfully!")

docs.title: 3. Execution & Expected Output
docs.text:
Run the script from your terminal:

python quickstart.py

Expected output: 

Starting streaming prequential evaluation...
--> [ALERT] Concept drift statistically detected at sample 206!
--------------------------------------------------
Total Stream Samples:  400
Overall Accuracy:      91.50%
Detected Drift Points: [206]
Quickstart completed successfully!

docs.title: What Happened?
docs.text:
1. Prequential Evaluation: Each instance is tested first to measure real generalization error, then immediately used to update the decision tree.
  2. Instant Drift Detection: At sample 200, the underlying ground truth inverted. By sample 206 (only 6 samples later), ReliabilityWeightedADWIN detected the statistically significant elevation in error rate and fired an alert.
  3. Rapid Adaptation: The AdaptiveClassifier adjusted its Hoeffding Tree split statistics, recovering \(>90\%\) overall streaming accuracy across the entire 400-sample run.
