docs.text:
Analytical logit gradients derived in Phase 6 were validated against two-sided finite difference approximations: $\(\nabla_{\mathbf{z}}^{\text{num}} = \frac{\mathcal{L}(\mathbf{z} + \epsilon \mathbf{e}_{ij}) - \mathcal{L}(\mathbf{z} - \epsilon \mathbf{e}_{ij})}{2 \epsilon}, \quad \epsilon = 10^{-6}\)$

Loss Function Maximum Gradient Error Tolerance Threshold Result SymmetricCrossEntropyLoss (SCE) \(3.21 \times 10^{-7}\) \(1.0 \times 10^{-5}\) PASS GeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss (GCE) \(4.18 \times 10^{-7}\) \(1.0 \times 10^{-5}\) PASS

docs.title: 2. Gradient Boundedness Under Adversarial Noise
docs.text: Under extreme label corruption with confident incorrect predictions (\(z_{\text{correct}} = -50.0, z_{\text{corrupt}} = +50.0\)): - Standard Cross-Entropy gradients explode or saturate. - SCE analytical gradient Frobenius norm evaluated to \(0.0988 \le 20.0\), strictly satisfying Theorem 2 boundedness guarantees.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
AdaptiveML provides a unified foundation for continual learning, concept drift adaptation, robust noise handling, and resource-bounded optimization. Rather than attempting to replace established deep learning and machine learning libraries, AdaptiveML is designed from the ground up to complement them.

AdaptiveML adheres to a strict modular dependency contract: - Core Engine: Built on pure, vectorized NumPy (numpy>=1.24.0). Installs with zero C++ compilation or heavy dependencies. - Opt-In Framework Bridges: Specialized adapters located in adaptive_ml.integrations connect AdaptiveML to external ecosystems: - scikit-learn: Native estimator and transformer interfaces (BaseEstimator, ClassifierMixin, TransformerMixin). - PyTorch: Custom autograd loss modules (nn.Module), 8-bit quantized optimizers, runtime budget hooks, and SafeTensors checkpoint adapters. - Tabular DataFrames: Zero-copy and view-based data conversion across pandas and Polars. - Serialization: Cryptographically safe tensor serialization via SafeTensors, eliminating pickle CVE vulnerabilities.

docs.title: Cross-Framework Safe Checkpointing Architecture
docs.text: AdaptiveML eliminates Python pickle deserialization vulnerabilities by separating neural model parameter tensors from orchestration metadata.

docs.title: 1. Security Architecture & Threat Model
docs.text:
Standard machine learning frameworks commonly persist models using Python pickle (e.g., torch.save, scikit-learn joblib.dump). However, pickle executes arbitrary Python bytecode during deserialization, creating severe Remote Code Execution (RCE) vulnerabilities when loading checkpoints from public repositories or external services.

AdaptiveML adopts a strict two-plane state persistence model:

Model Checkpoint
  ├── Model Parameters (.safetensors)  -> Memory-mapped, zero-copy, raw binary tensor buffers
  └── Execution Metadata (.json)       -> Human-readable architecture, optimizer, and controller state
Security Property Standard pickle / torch.save AdaptiveML TorchCheckpointAdapter Arbitrary Code Execution High Risk (Unsafe deserializer) Zero Risk (Strictly forbidden) Header Validation Basic Cryptographic header bounds Deserialization Speed \(0.77\text{ ms}\) (Interpreted) \(0.49\text{ ms}\) (\(36\%\) faster, zero-copy memory map) Inspection Without Code Impossible Immediate JSON inspection

docs.title: 2. API Usage
docs.text:
Save and restore hybrid checkpoints with TorchCheckpointAdapter:

from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_callback import TorchCheckpointAdapter

# 1. Save hybrid checkpoint
saved_path = TorchCheckpointAdapter.save_hybrid_checkpoint(
    model=model,
    optimizer=optimizer,
    controller=ulc_controller,
    filepath="checkpoints/production_v1.safetensors",
)

# 2. Restore hybrid checkpoint
TorchCheckpointAdapter.load_hybrid_checkpoint(
    model=fresh_model,
    optimizer=fresh_optimizer,
    controller=fresh_ulc_controller,
    filepath="checkpoints/production_v1.safetensors",
)

docs.title: Data Interoperability & Array Contracts
docs.text: AdaptiveML provides high-performance data conversion utilities in adaptive_ml.integrations.data designed for zero-copy views, memory alignment, and robust numerical validation across tabular and deep learning frameworks.

docs.title: 1. Supported Data Representations

docs.title: 2.1 to_numpy(data, dtype=None, ensure_2d=False, ensure_1d=False, copy=False, name="data")
docs.text:
Standardizes arbitrary inputs into a clean, validated np.ndarray:

from adaptive_ml.integrations.data import to_numpy
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0], "y": [3.0, 4.0]})
arr = to_numpy(df, ensure_2d=True, dtype=np.float32)

Guarantees & Validation: - Zero-Copy Where Possible: If the input is already contiguous and matches target dtype, returns a view without duplicating RAM. - Dimensionality Enforcement: - ensure_2d=True: Expands 1D vectors \((N,)\) to \((N, 1)\). - ensure_1d=True: Flattens single-column matrices \((N, 1)\) to \((N,)\); raises typed ValidationError on multi-column matrices. - Strict Non-Finite Validation: Automatically scans floating-point buffers for NaN and Inf, raising ValidationError with informative diagnostic messages.

docs.title: 2.2 to_tensor(data, dtype=None, device=None, copy=False, name="data")

Converts arbitrary inputs into a PyTorch torch.Tensor on the designated compute device (cpu, cuda, mps):

from adaptive_ml.integrations.data import to_tensor
import polars as pl

pldf = pl.DataFrame({"sensor_1": [12.4, 15.8], "sensor_2": [89.1, 91.2]})
tensor = to_tensor(pldf, device="cpu")

Polars pl.DataFrame, pl.Series Apache Arrow memory slice via .to_numpy() Columnar-to-row layout conversion with strict SIMD alignment.

docs.title: 2. Ingesting Pandas DataFrames
docs.text:
Pandas DataFrames can be passed directly to to_numpy() or to DatasetContract inspection:

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.integrations import to_numpy, inspect_dataset_contract
from adaptive_ml.ala import ALA30AdaptiveLearner

# Construct sample DataFrame
df = pd.DataFrame({
    "feature_0": np.random.randn(100),
    "feature_1": np.random.randn(100),
    "target": np.random.randint(0, 2, size=100)
})

# Inspect contract
contract = inspect_dataset_contract(df[["feature_0", "feature_1"]])
print(f"Detected framework: {contract.source_framework}, shape: ({contract.n_samples}, {contract.n_features})")

# Convert to validated numpy array
X = to_numpy(df[["feature_0", "feature_1"]], ensure_2d=True, dtype=np.float64)
y = to_numpy(df["target"], ensure_1d=True, dtype=np.int64)

# Stream to AdaptiveML learner
learner = ALA30AdaptiveLearner(n_features=2, n_classes=2)
res = learner.fit_batch(X, y)
print(f"Accuracy: {res['accuracy'] * 100:.2f}%")

docs.title: 3. Ingesting Polars DataFrames
docs.text:
Polars provides high-speed columnar data processing. AdaptiveML converts Polars Arrow chunks into C-contiguous NumPy arrays without intermediary Python objects:

import polars as pl
import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.integrations import to_numpy, inspect_dataset_contract

# Construct sample Polars DataFrame
pldf = pl.DataFrame({
    "x0": np.random.randn(100).tolist(),
    "x1": np.random.randn(100).tolist(),
})

contract = inspect_dataset_contract(pldf)
print(f"Polars Contract: samples={contract.n_samples}, features={contract.n_features}")

X_polars = to_numpy(pldf, ensure_2d=True, dtype=np.float64)
print(f"Converted shape: {X_polars.shape}, is_contiguous: {X_polars.flags['C_CONTIGUOUS']}")

docs.title: 4. Automatic Non-Finite & Dimension Validation
docs.text: When converting DataFrames, to_numpy automatically performs safety checks: - NaN / Inf Detection: Floating-point matrices with missing or non-finite values raise a typed ValidationError with informative diagnostic messages. - Dimensionality Enforcement: Single-column Series/DataFrames can be forced to 1D (ensure_1d=True) or 2D (ensure_2d=True). - Contiguity Guarantee: Ensures arrays are memory-contiguous for optimal SIMD and cache locality during Hoeffding tree updates and block quantization.

docs.title: Deferred Framework Integrations & Roadmap
docs.text: AdaptiveML has conducted exhaustive architectural and runtime evaluations regarding deep integrations with TensorFlow 2.x, Keras 3, and other third-party frameworks.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Status Matrix
docs.text: Framework Status Primary Decision Drivers Recommended Interoperability Path TensorFlow 2.x Deferred Python 3.14 binary wheel unavailability, static graph compilation vs dynamic quantization mismatch, dependency bloat (>550 MB). Zero-copy NumPy buffer ingestion via to_numpy(). Keras 3 Deferred Dynamic block-quantization custom call instability across multiple backends. PyTorch backend native integration or NumPy bridge. JAX / Flax Roadmap Strong functional fit; under active architectural evaluation for Q2 2027. Functional array transformations via NumPy/DLPack.

docs.title: 2.1 Python 3.14 Binary Wheel Availability
docs.text: As of Q4 2026, the official TensorFlow distribution does not distribute pre-compiled binary wheels for Python 3.14 on Windows or Linux. Attempting to mandate TensorFlow support would immediately break installation environments on modern Python releases.

docs.title: 2.2 Static Graph Compilation vs. Dynamic Block Quantization
docs.text: AdaptiveML's RAO algorithms (such as 8-bit block-quantized AdamW) rely on dynamic per-block scale normalization: $\(q_i = \text{clip}\left(\left\lfloor \frac{w_i}{\text{scale}_b} \times 127 \right\rceil, -127, 127\right)\)$ Under tf.function XLA graph compilation, variable dynamic block allocation triggers trace recompilations, neutralizing quantization throughput gains.

docs.title: 2.3 Dependency Footprint Inflation
docs.text: aml-core adheres to a lightweight footprint philosophy (\(\approx 35\text{ MB}\) uncompressed). Introducing TensorFlow pulls in \(> 550\text{ MB}\) of binaries (including CUDA dependencies, Abseil, FlatBuffers, and Protobuf), violating local-first and CPU-efficient design tenets.

docs.title: 3. Supported Interoperability Workflow
docs.text:
TensorFlow/Keras practitioners can interoperate with AdaptiveML seamlessly using the native NumPy tensor conversion bridge:

import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.ala import ALA30AdaptiveLearner
from adaptive_ml.integrations import to_numpy

# 1. Feature extraction from Keras model in streaming pipeline
# (Assuming features extracted as numpy array or tensor)
features_np = np.random.randn(100, 32).astype(np.float32)
labels_np = np.random.randint(0, 2, size=100)

# 2. Convert to validated C-contiguous numpy array
X_clean = to_numpy(features_np, ensure_2d=True, dtype=np.float64)
y_clean = to_numpy(labels_np, ensure_1d=True, dtype=np.int64)

# 3. Stream through AdaptiveML streaming learner
learner = ALA30AdaptiveLearner(n_features=32, n_classes=2)
metrics = learner.fit_batch(X_clean, y_clean)
print(f"Incremental streaming accuracy: {metrics['accuracy'] * 100:.2f}%")

docs.title: 4. Re-evaluation Criteria
docs.text: Native adapters for deferred frameworks will be formally re-evaluated when: 1. Official binary wheels for current Python versions (Python 3.14+) are published upstream. 2. Stable C++ / XLA custom call APIs allow dynamic block quantization without graph recompilation overhead. 3. Decoupled distribution wheels allow optional installation without inflating the core package footprint.

docs.title: Pure NumPy Backend Integration
docs.text: AdaptiveML's default execution engine is built natively on top of NumPy, requiring zero external C++ extensions or GPU runtimes.

docs.title: 1. Native Vectorization
docs.text: All core operations in adaptive_ml.ala, adaptive_ml.rla, and adaptive_ml.rao operate directly on contiguous NumPy ndarray buffers: - Matrix Vectorization: Tree split information gain evaluated via SIMD matrix reductions. - Quantization: Block-wise quantization performed via np.clip and vectorized scaling. - Memory Contiguity: Buffer copies minimized via in-place views (np.ndarray.view).

docs.title: 2. Example: Standalone NumPy Optimization
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.rao import LowMemoryAdamW

# Optimize arbitrary NumPy parameter arrays
w = np.zeros(100, dtype=np.float32)

class SimpleParam:
    def __init__(self, data):
        self.data = data
        self.grad = np.zeros_like(data)

param = SimpleParam(w)
opt = LowMemoryAdamW([param], lr=0.01)

# Optimization step
param.grad = np.random.randn(100).astype(np.float32)
opt.step()

docs.title: PyTorch Framework Integration Guide
docs.text: AdaptiveML provides native PyTorch modules, robust autograd loss functions, memory-efficient optimizers, runtime resource budget hooks, and cryptographic safe checkpointing.

docs.title: 1. Overview of PyTorch Components
docs.text:
Exported from adaptive_ml.integrations:

Component Type Primary Purpose TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss nn.Module Noise-tolerant loss combining Cross-Entropy and Reverse Cross-Entropy (\(\alpha, \beta\)). TorchGeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss nn.Module Bounded loss interpolating between MAE and CCE via parameter \(q \in (0.0, 1.0]\). create_torch_low_memory_adamw Optimizer Factory 8-bit block-quantized AdamW achieving \(75\%\) reduction in optimizer state RAM. TorchTrainingBudgetHook Training Callback Tracks per-step latency and physical RSS RAM; dynamically adapts batch size. TorchCheckpointAdapter State Serializer Safe checkpointing separating neural weights (SafeTensors) from metadata (JSON).

docs.title: 2. Robust Loss Functions for Corrupted Labels
docs.text: Standard neural networks quickly memorize noisy or mislabeled data. AdaptiveML provides two mathematically principled robust loss functions:

docs.title: 2.1 Symmetric Cross-Entropy Loss
docs.text:
Combines standard Cross-Entropy \(H(p, q)\) with Reverse Cross-Entropy \(H(q, p)\): $\(\mathcal{L}_{SCE} = \alpha \cdot \mathcal{L}_{CE} + \beta \cdot \mathcal{L}_{RCE}\)$

import torch
from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_module import TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss

criterion = TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss(alpha=1.0, beta=0.8)

logits = model(inputs)
loss = criterion(logits, targets)
loss.backward()

docs.title: 2.2 Generalized Cross-Entropy Loss
docs.text:
Applies a negative Box-Cox transformation bounding gradients on hard, ambiguous, or corrupted instances: $\(\mathcal{L}_{GCE} = \frac{1 - p_y^q}{q}, \quad q \in (0.0, 1.0]\)$

from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_module import TorchGeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss

# q=0.7 is recommended for moderate label corruption
criterion = TorchGeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss(q=0.7)
loss = criterion(logits, targets)

docs.title: 3. 8-Bit Quantized AdamW (create_torch_low_memory_adamw)
docs.text:
Standard fp32 AdamW stores two state moments (\(m_t, v_t\)) per parameter, requiring \(8\text{ bytes}\) of optimizer state per parameter (e.g., 800MB for a 100M parameter model). LowMemoryAdamW quantizes states into 8-bit dynamic blocks (\(B=2048\)):

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_optim import create_torch_low_memory_adamw

model = nn.Sequential(
    nn.Linear(128, 256),
    nn.ReLU(),
    nn.Linear(256, 10),
)

optimizer = create_torch_low_memory_adamw(
    model.parameters(),
    lr=1e-3,
    weight_decay=1e-2,
)

# Standard training step
optimizer.zero_grad()
loss = criterion(model(x), y)
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()

docs.title: 4. Runtime Budget Management (TorchTrainingBudgetHook)
docs.text:
Detect physical RAM pressure and execution latency bottlenecks during neural training:

from adaptive_ml.rao.budget import DynamicResourceBudgetManager
from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_callback import TorchTrainingBudgetHook

budget_mgr = DynamicResourceBudgetManager(
    max_step_time_ms=50.0,
    max_memory_mb=4096.0,
    min_batch_size=16,
    max_batch_size=128,
)
budget_hook = TorchTrainingBudgetHook(budget_mgr)

for epoch in range(10):
    for batch_idx in range(num_batches):
        curr_batch_size = budget_hook.recommended_batch_size
        x_batch, y_batch = get_batch(curr_batch_size)

        budget_hook.on_step_begin()
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss = criterion(model(x_batch), y_batch)
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
        state = budget_hook.on_step_end()

        if state == "PRESSURE_WARNING":
            print("System approaching memory ceiling; batch size throttled automatically.")

docs.title: 5. Safe Checkpointing (TorchCheckpointAdapter)
docs.text:
Standard torch.save(model) relies on Python pickle, introducing arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities. TorchCheckpointAdapter serializes tensor weights using HuggingFace safetensors and saves controller and optimizer states as readable JSON:

from pathlib import Path
from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_callback import TorchCheckpointAdapter

# Save checkpoint safely
saved_file = TorchCheckpointAdapter.save_hybrid_checkpoint(
    model=model,
    optimizer=optimizer,
    controller=None,
    filepath="checkpoints/model.safetensors",
)

# Restore checkpoint safely
TorchCheckpointAdapter.load_hybrid_checkpoint(
    model=restored_model,
    optimizer=restored_optimizer,
    controller=None,
    filepath="checkpoints/model.safetensors",
)

docs.title: Classical Batch Pipeline
docs.text:
SklearnAdaptiveClassifier can be dropped directly into any standard scikit-learn pipeline or cross-validation routine:

import numpy as np
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
from adaptive_ml.integrations import SklearnAdaptiveClassifier

# Synthetic classification dataset
np.random.seed(42)
X_train = np.random.randn(200, 10)
y_train = (X_train[:, 0] + X_train[:, 1] > 0.0).astype(int)

pipe = Pipeline([
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("classifier", SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(
        n_features=10,
        n_classes=2,
        grace_period=50,
        delta=1e-4,
        random_state=42,
    )),
])

# Fit and cross-validate
scores = cross_val_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv=5)
print(f"5-Fold CV Mean Accuracy: {scores.mean() * 100:.2f}%")

docs.title: Incremental Streaming with partial_fit
docs.text:
In production stream pipelines, use partial_fit to continuously update tree splits:

import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.integrations import SklearnAdaptiveClassifier

clf = SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(n_features=10, n_classes=2, grace_period=20)

# Simulate 5 micro-batches of streaming data
for batch_idx in range(5):
    X_batch = np.random.randn(50, 10)
    y_batch = (X_batch[:, 0] > 0.0).astype(int)
    clf.partial_fit(X_batch, y_batch, classes=[0, 1])

y_pred = clf.predict(X_batch[:5])
print("Batch predictions:", y_pred)

docs.title: 3. Detecting Distribution Shifts with SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer
docs.text:
Insert SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer into your scikit-learn pipeline to automatically track concept drift on critical features without interrupting data flow:

import numpy as np
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from adaptive_ml.integrations import (
    SklearnAdaptiveClassifier,
    SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer,
)

stream_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("drift_monitor", SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer(delta=0.001, monitored_feature_index=0)),
    ("classifier", SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(n_features=4, n_classes=2)),
])

# Process streaming batches
for step in range(5):
    X_batch = np.random.randn(40, 4)
    y_batch = (X_batch[:, 0] > 0.0).astype(int)

    X_proc = stream_pipe.named_steps["scaler"].partial_fit(X_batch).transform(X_batch)
    X_mon = stream_pipe.named_steps["drift_monitor"].transform(X_proc)
    stream_pipe.named_steps["classifier"].partial_fit(X_mon, y_batch, classes=[0, 1])

    if stream_pipe.named_steps["drift_monitor"].last_drift_detected_:
        print(f"ALERT: Drift detected at batch {step}!")

docs.title: 4. Filtering Label Noise with SklearnReliabilityFilter
docs.text:
SklearnReliabilityFilter uses spatial \(k\)-nearest neighbors and prediction margin reliability to drop corrupted observations:

import numpy as np
from adaptive_ml.integrations import SklearnReliabilityFilter

filter_step = SklearnReliabilityFilter(n_classes=2, min_reliability=0.35)
X_batch = np.random.randn(50, 4)
y_batch = (X_batch[:, 0] > 0.0).astype(int)

# In streaming scenarios, compute model probabilities or pass initial estimates
probas = np.column_stack([
    1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(X_batch[:, 0])),
    1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-X_batch[:, 0])),
])

# Filter low-reliability noisy samples
X_clean, y_clean, weights_clean = filter_step.filter_batch(X_batch, y_batch, probas)
print(f"Clean samples retained: {len(y_clean)} of {len(y_batch)}")

docs.title: Classical Batch Pipeline
docs.text:
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
from sklearn.model_selection import cross_val_score
from adaptive_ml.integrations.sklearn import SklearnAdaptiveClassifier

pipe = Pipeline([
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("classifier", SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(
        n_features=10,
        n_classes=2,
        grace_period=50,
        delta=1e-4,
        random_state=42,
    )),
])

# Fit and cross-validate
scores = cross_val_score(pipe, X_train, y_train, cv=5)
print(f"5-Fold CV Mean Accuracy: {scores.mean() * 100:.2f}%")

docs.title: Incremental Streaming with partial_fit
docs.text:
clf = SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(n_features=8, n_classes=3, grace_period=20)

for X_batch, y_batch in stream_generator():
    # Update model incrementally with incoming batch
    clf.partial_fit(X_batch, y_batch, classes=[0, 1, 2])
    print(f"Processed: {clf.samples_seen_} samples | Drifts adapted: {clf.drift_count_}")

docs.title: 3. Detecting Distribution Shifts with SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer
docs.text:
Insert SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer into your scikit-learn pipeline to automatically track concept drift on critical features without interrupting data flow:

from adaptive_ml.integrations.sklearn import SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer

stream_pipe = Pipeline([
    ("scaler", StandardScaler()),
    ("drift_monitor", SklearnDriftDetectorTransformer(delta=0.001, monitored_feature_index=0)),
    ("classifier", SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(n_features=4, n_classes=2)),
])

for X_batch, y_batch in stream:
    # Transform scales and checks drift
    X_proc = stream_pipe.named_steps["scaler"].partial_fit(X_batch).transform(X_batch)
    X_mon = stream_pipe.named_steps["drift_monitor"].transform(X_proc)
    stream_pipe.named_steps["classifier"].partial_fit(X_mon, y_batch, classes=[0, 1])

    if stream_pipe.named_steps["drift_monitor"].last_drift_detected_:
        print(f"ALERT: Drift detected at batch! Total events: {stream_pipe.named_steps['drift_monitor'].drift_count_}")

docs.title: 4. Hyperparameter Tuning and Cloning
docs.text:
SklearnAdaptiveClassifier implements full parameter introspection via get_params() and set_params():

from sklearn.base import clone
from sklearn.model_selection import GridSearchCV

param_grid = {
    "classifier__grace_period": [20, 50, 100],
    "classifier__delta": [1e-3, 1e-4, 1e-5],
}

search = GridSearchCV(pipe, param_grid, cv=3)
search.fit(X, y)
print("Best Parameters:", search.best_params_)

# Cloned instances maintain parameters with freshly initialized weights
cloned_model = clone(search.best_estimator_)

docs.title: TensorFlow / Keras Integration Assessment & Roadmap
docs.text: AdaptiveML has conducted an exhaustive architectural and runtime assessment regarding deep integration with TensorFlow 2.x and Keras 3.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Status
docs.text: Category Assessment Status Primary Decision Formal Deferral of Native TensorFlow Adapters Deferred Interim Path Zero-Copy NumPy Array Ingestion (to_numpy, to_tensor) Available & Supported Root Drivers Python 3.14 ABI Incompatibility, Graph Compilation Mismatch, Heavy Footprint Verified

docs.title: 2. Technical Evaluation & Rationale
docs.text:
1. Python 3.14 Wheel Availability: As of Q4 2026, the official TensorFlow distribution does not distribute pre-compiled AMD64 binary wheels for Python 3.14 on Windows or Linux. Attempting to mandate TensorFlow support would break environment installation on modern Python runtimes.

  2. Static Graph Compilation vs Dynamic Quantization: AdaptiveML's RAO algorithms (e.g., 8-bit block-quantized AdamW) rely on dynamic per-block scale normalization. Under tf.function XLA graph compilation, variable dynamic block allocation triggers trace recompilations, neutralizing quantization throughput gains.

  3. Dependency Footprint Inflation: aml-core adheres to a lightweight footprint philosophy (\(\approx 35\text{ MB}\)). Introducing TensorFlow pulls in \(> 550\text{ MB}\) of binaries (including CUDA dependencies, Abseil, FlatBuffers, and Protobuf), violating local-first design tenets.

docs.title: 3. Supported Interoperability Workflow
docs.text:
TensorFlow/Keras practitioners can interoperate with AdaptiveML seamlessly using the native NumPy tensor conversion bridge:

import numpy as np
import tensorflow as tf
from adaptive_ml.ala.classifier import AdaptiveClassifier
from adaptive_ml.integrations.data import to_numpy

# 1. Extract feature representations from Keras backbone
feature_extractor = tf.keras.applications.MobileNetV2(include_top=False, pooling="avg")
tf_tensor = feature_extractor(images)

# 2. Convert to NumPy without serialization
np_features = to_numpy(tf_tensor.numpy())

# 3. Stream through AdaptiveML streaming tree
clf = AdaptiveClassifier(n_features=np_features.shape[1], n_classes=10)
clf.partial_fit(np_features, labels)

docs.title: 4. Future Roadmap
docs.text: Native Keras 3 multi-backend adapters will be evaluated once TensorFlow publishes official Python 3.14+ binary wheels and stable XLA custom call bindings for dynamic block quantization.

docs.title: Framework Integrations Troubleshooting & Diagnostics Guide
docs.text: Common diagnostic procedures, error messages, and remediation steps when interfacing AdaptiveML with third-party frameworks.

docs.title: 1. Missing Optional Dependency Errors
docs.text: AdaptiveML keeps its core lightweight and requires optional dependency extras to be installed explicitly.

docs.title: Error: scikit-learn is required for SklearnAdaptiveClassifier
docs.text:
Cause: sklearn is not installed in the active Python environment. Solution: 

pip install "aml-core[sklearn]"

docs.title: Error: PyTorch is required for TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss
docs.text:
Cause: torch is not installed in the active Python environment. Solution: 

pip install "aml-core[torch]"

docs.title: Error: safetensors is required for fast zero-copy state loading
docs.text:
Cause: HuggingFace safetensors package is missing. Solution: 

pip install "aml-core[safetensors]"

docs.title: Error: pandas or polars is required for DataFrame conversion
docs.text:
Cause: Tabular data extras have not been installed. Solution: 

pip install "aml-core[dataframe]"

docs.title: Error: ValidationError: X contains non-finite values (NaN or Inf)
docs.text:
Cause: AdaptiveML decision trees and online drift detectors require valid finite real numbers. Solution: - For scikit-learn pipelines, insert SimpleImputer(strategy='mean') prior to the classifier: 

from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline

pipe = Pipeline([
    ("imputer", SimpleImputer(strategy="mean")),
    ("clf", SklearnAdaptiveClassifier(n_features=10, n_classes=2)),
])
- In pandas/Polars, clean data using .fillna() or .drop_nulls() before passing to to_numpy().

docs.title: Error: ValidationError: y must be a 1D vector, got 2D shape (N, 2)
docs.text: Cause: Target label vectors must have shape (N,) or single-column (N, 1). Multi-column one-hot encoded targets are not accepted directly by decision trees. Solution: - Convert one-hot vectors to class index integers using np.argmax(y_onehot, axis=1).

docs.title: State: PRESSURE_WARNING or THROTTLED
docs.text:
Symptom: TorchTrainingBudgetHook reports throttled state or decreases recommended batch size. Cause: Process RSS memory footprint exceeded warning_threshold (default 80%) of max_memory_mb, or per-step latency exceeded max_step_time_ms. Remediation: 1. Dynamically read budget_hook.recommended_batch_size in the training loop: 

batch_size = budget_hook.recommended_batch_size
2. Enable 8-bit block-quantized optimizer via create_torch_low_memory_adamw to cut optimizer state memory by \(75\%\). 3. Increase memory budget if host RAM permits: 
budget_mgr = DynamicResourceBudgetManager(max_memory_mb=8192.0)

docs.title: Error: SerializationError: Checkpoint file not found: ...
docs.text: Cause: Checkpoint file path does not exist, or the .meta.json companion file is missing. Remediation: Ensure both the binary tensor file (<name>.safetensors) and the metadata JSON file (<name>.meta.json) are located in the same directory.

docs.title: PyTorch Integration Specification
docs.text: Document ID: DOC-INT-P13-003 Phase: Phase 13 — Framework Integrations Status: READY FOR REVIEW Module: adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_optim, adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_module

docs.title: 1.1 Architecture & Subclassing
docs.text:
• Inherits from torch.optim.Optimizer when PyTorch is installed and parameters are instances of torch.nn.Parameter or torch.Tensor.
  • State tensors:
  • First moment \(m_t\): Stored as quantized torch.int8 tensor on active device.
  • Second moment \(v_t\): Stored as quantized torch.uint8 tensor on active device.
  • Scale vectors \(s_m, s_v\): Stored as torch.float32 tensors (\(B=64\) parameter blocks).
  • Total State Footprint: \(2.125\text{ bytes/parameter}\) vs \(8.00\text{ bytes/parameter}\) standard FP32 AdamW (\(73.44\%\) memory reduction).

docs.title: 1.2 Usage Syntax
docs.text:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from adaptive_ml.integrations.torch_optim import create_torch_low_memory_adamw

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10, 32), nn.ReLU(), nn.Linear(32, 2))
optimizer = create_torch_low_memory_adamw(model.parameters(), lr=1e-3, block_size=64)

# Standard training step
optimizer.zero_grad()
loss.backward()
optimizer.step()

docs.title: 2. PyTorch Native Robust Loss (TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss)
docs.text:
• Inherits from torch.nn.Module.
  • Combines standard Cross-Entropy with Reverse Cross-Entropy: $\(\mathcal{L}_{\text{SCE}} = \alpha \cdot \mathcal{L}_{\text{CE}} + \beta \cdot \mathcal{L}_{\text{RCE}}\)$
  • Strictly bounds gradients against corrupted labels while autograd handles backpropagation.

docs.title: 1. Estimator Contract Compliance
docs.text: SklearnAdaptiveClassifier implements the scikit-learn Estimator and Classifier specification:

docs.title: 1.1 Constructor & Parameter Immutability
docs.text:
• All hyperparameters are defined as explicit keyword arguments with default values in __init__.
  • No input data validation, fitting logic, or state mutation occurs inside __init__.
  • Parameters are assigned unmodified to identically named attributes on self, ensuring \(100\%\) compatibility with sklearn.base.clone().

docs.title: 1.2 Required Methods
docs.text:
• fit(X, y): Initializes internal estimator state and trains on initial batch. Sets self.classes_.
  • partial_fit(X, y, classes=None, sample_weight=None): Online streaming incremental update.
  • predict(X): Returns class label predictions of shape (n_samples,).
  • predict_proba(X): Returns normalized probability estimates of shape (n_samples, n_classes) on the simplex \(\Delta^{C-1}\).
  • score(X, y): Returns classification accuracy.

pipe = Pipeline([

predictions = pipe.predict(X)

docs.text: Document ID: DOC-INT-P13-004 Phase: Phase 13 — Framework Integrations Status: READY FOR REVIEW

docs.title: 1. Technical Evaluation
docs.text: In accordance with Phase 13 guidelines and Phase 7 Architecture Decision Records (ADR-005), the engineering team conducted a formal feasibility evaluation for TensorFlow/Keras integration:

docs.title: 1.1 Evaluated Factors
docs.text:
1. Dependency Footprint: tensorflow introduces \(>500\text{ MB}\) of binary dependencies, complex C++ ABIs, and frequent wheel installation challenges on modern Python versions (e.g., Python 3.12, 3.13, 3.14).
  2. Ecosystem & Persona Demand: Phase 1 market research established that \(>85\%\) of research and production practitioners working on concept drift, continual learning, and memory optimization utilize PyTorch or scikit-learn.
  3. Core Philosophy Conflict: AdaptiveML is committed to being lightweight, local-first, and CPU-first. A heavyweight TensorFlow dependency would compromise this philosophy without proportional adoption benefits.

docs.title: 2. Decision & Recommendation
docs.text:
• Verdict: DEFERRED.
  • Alternative: Developers working with TensorFlow can utilize AdaptiveML's core NumPy backend directly via standard tf.numpy_function or array casting (tensor.numpy()).
  • Re-evaluation trigger: Community demand exceeding 50 GitHub upvotes following Phase 18 release.

docs.title: Architectural Overview & Pillar Coordination
docs.text:
AdaptiveML is structured around five independently usable algorithmic pillars coordinated by the Unified Learning Controller:

flowchart TD
    subgraph DataStream ["Incoming Streaming Data (X_t, y_t)"]
        StreamIn["Stream Samples"]
    end

    subgraph Pillars ["Algorithmic Pillars"]
        ALA["ALA 3.0: Adaptive Learning<br/>(ADWIN + Hoeffding Tree + Concept Memory)"]
        RLA["RLA 3.0: Robust Learning<br/>(Multi-Signal Reliability Engine)"]
        MIN["Minority Intelligence 2.0<br/>(Beta-Binomial Prior + Dynamic FP Budget)"]
        RAO["RAO 2.0: Resource Optimization<br/>(Vectorized 8-Bit AdamW + Checkpoints)"]
    end

    subgraph Controller ["Coordination Layer"]
        ULC["ULC-v5: Unified Learning Controller<br/>(Five-Tier Hierarchy + Utility Arbitration)"]
    end

    StreamIn --> ULC
    ULC --> ALA
    ULC --> RLA
    ULC --> MIN
    ULC --> RAO

docs.title: 1. ALA — Adaptive Learning Algorithms
docs.text:
• Primary Class: AdaptiveClassifier, ReliabilityWeightedADWIN, RecurringConceptMemory.
  • Functionality: Bounded-memory prequential stream classification, statistical drift detection, and automated restoration of historical concept models without costly retraining.

docs.title: 2. RLA — Robust Learning Algorithms
docs.text:
• Primary Class: MultiSignalReliabilityEngine, RLA30RobustLearner.
  • Functionality: Multi-signal estimation of label veracity combining margin confidence, spatial \(k\)-NN consensus, and temporal consistency. Dynamically downweights or cleans corrupted labels.

docs.title: 3. Adaptive Minority Intelligence
docs.text:
• Primary Class: MinorityIntelligence20Learner, BetaBinomialPriorTracker, DynamicFPBudgetThresholdManager.
  • Functionality: Bayesian tracking of streaming class priors and dynamic calibration of decision thresholds to preserve minority recall under severe class imbalance (\(<1\%\)).

docs.title: 4. RAO — Resource-Aware Optimization
docs.text:
• Primary Class: VectorizedLowMemoryAdamW, LowMemoryAdamW, ResilientCheckpointManager.
  • Functionality: 8-bit dynamic block quantization of optimizer moments, cutting state RAM by \(>71\%\) while preserving full 32-bit precision on 1D biases and normalization scales.

docs.title: 5. ULC — Unified Learning Controller
docs.text:
• Primary Class: UnifiedLearningControllerV5.
  • Functionality: Synthesizes cross-pillar signals into a calibrated expected utility score: $\(U = (\text{Confidence} \times \text{Benefit}) - \text{Operational Cost}\)$ Arbitrates interventions across a Five-Tier Hierarchy (NOOP, Parameter Damping, Concept Restore, Soft Replay Reset, Hard Reset) with exponential cooldown backoff to suppress thrashing.

docs.title: Core Design Principles
docs.text: AdaptiveML adheres to seven strict engineering and architectural principles:

docs.title: 1. Local-First & Cloud-Agnostic
docs.text:
• No Mandatory Network Connection: The library runs completely offline. It never dials out to external license servers, telemetry endpoints, or cloud backends.
  • Embedded & Edge Ready: Designed to run inside resource-constrained Docker containers, Kubernetes sidecars, edge gateways, or local developer workstations.

docs.title: 2. CPU-First Execution Efficiency
docs.text:
• Microsecond Latency: Streaming inference (\(5.06\ \mu\text{s}\)) and prequential updates (\(<320\ \mu\text{s}\)) execute natively on standard x86_64 and ARM64 CPUs.
  • Zero Mandatory GPU/CUDA Dependencies: GPU acceleration is optional via PyTorch; all core functionality runs on commodity CPU cores.

docs.title: 3. Minimal Mandatory Dependencies
docs.text:
• Strictly Minimal Core: import adaptive_ml requires exclusively numpy>=1.24.0.
  • Decoupled Extras: PyTorch, Scikit-Learn, SciPy, Pandas, Polars, and Safetensors are optional extras installed only when required (pip install 'aml-core[torch]').

docs.title: 4. Strict \(O(1)\) Memory Invariance
docs.text:
• No Unbounded Buffers: All historical buffers, sliding windows, queues, and concept stores enforce deterministic upper bounds via reservoir replacement, FIFO eviction, or LRU pruning.
  • Infinite Streaming Stability: Tested across \(100,000+\) consecutive samples; resident memory remains strictly sub-\(50\text{ MB}\).

docs.title: 5. Security by Default & Zero-Pickle Architecture
docs.text:
• Immune to Deserialization Exploits: Python pickle is strictly forbidden across the codebase.
  • SafeTensors Persistence: All model weights are serialized via binary SafeTensors.
  • HMAC-SHA256 Authenticity: Optional keyed HMAC-SHA256 signatures with constant-time verification protect state files against tampering.

docs.title: 6. Stable, Scikit-Learn Compatible APIs
docs.text:
• Protocol Compliance: Core classifiers implement fit, partial_fit, predict, predict_proba, get_params, set_params.
  • PEP 561 Typing: All public functions and classes are fully typed and ship with py.typed.

docs.title: 7. Zero Telemetry & Privacy Preservation
docs.text:
• NullHandler Logging: Root logger attaches logging.NullHandler() by default, emitting zero noise unless explicitly configured by the host application.
  • Zero PII: Diagnostic events record purely numeric telemetry (loss, error rate, RSS memory). Customer feature payloads and labels are never logged.

docs.title: What is AdaptiveML?
docs.text:
AdaptiveML (distribution package: aml-core) is a production-grade Python library providing algorithms for Adaptive, Robust, and Resource-Efficient Learning.

Modern machine learning systems deployed in production environments operate in fundamentally non-stationary conditions. While traditional machine learning assumes identically and independently distributed (i.i.d.) data drawn from a static distribution, real-world data pipelines face: - Shifts in user behavior, market regimes, or seasonal trends (concept drift). - Imperfect human annotations, sensor degradation, and delayed labels (noisy data). - Stringent memory ceilings on edge gateways or microservice pods (computational constraints).

AdaptiveML provides native streaming algorithms, statistical drift detectors, label reliability estimators, memory-quantized optimizers, and unified controllers to address these challenges.

docs.title: Complement, Not Replace
docs.text:
AdaptiveML is designed to complement existing industry frameworks: - NumPy: AdaptiveML uses pure NumPy arrays as its primary data structure. Core algorithms execute without external overhead. - Scikit-Learn: AdaptiveML estimators (AdaptiveClassifier, etc.) implement standard Scikit-Learn protocols (fit, partial_fit, predict, predict_proba, get_params, set_params) and integrate into Scikit-Learn pipelines. - PyTorch: For deep neural architectures, AdaptiveML provides VectorizedLowMemoryAdamW (reducing optimizer state memory by \(>71\%\)) and custom loss functions (TorchFocalLoss, TorchGeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss).

AdaptiveML does not replace Scikit-Learn or PyTorch; it extends them into continuous, resource-constrained streaming domains.

docs.title: When to Use AdaptiveML
docs.text: Scenario Suitable? Recommended Approach Continuous Streaming Pipelines Yes Use AdaptiveClassifier with ReliabilityWeightedADWIN or UnifiedLearningControllerV5. Severe Label Noise & Adversarial Inputs Yes Use MultiSignalReliabilityEngine or RLA30RobustLearner to filter/downweight corrupt labels. Extreme Class Imbalance (<1% minority) Yes Use MinorityIntelligence20Learner with dynamic false-positive budget thresholding. Large Neural Network Optimizer Memory Bottlenecks Yes Replace torch.optim.AdamW with VectorizedLowMemoryAdamW for 73% RAM reduction. Static Offline Training on Clean Datasets No Standard Scikit-Learn or PyTorch is simpler and fully sufficient. Distributed Multi-GPU Clusters (Megatron/FSDP) No AdaptiveML is CPU-first and local-first; use specialized distributed frameworks.

docs.title: The Three Research & Engineering Challenges
docs.text: Production machine learning differs from textbook benchmarks in three critical dimensions:

docs.title: 1. Non-Stationary Environments & Concept Drift
docs.text:
In textbook machine learning, training and test datasets are assumed to be drawn from identical distributions \(P_{\text{train}}(X, Y) = P_{\text{test}}(X, Y)\).

In continuous operational systems: - Abrupt Drift: Sudden external shocks (e.g., regulatory changes, pandemic lockdowns, system updates) abruptly alter feature-label mappings: $\(P_{t}(Y \mid X) \neq P_{t-1}(Y \mid X)\)$ - Gradual Drift: Gradual macroeconomic shifts, sensor aging, or creeping user preference shifts slowly erode model accuracy. - Recurring Concepts: Seasonal patterns (holiday shopping, diurnal cycles, financial market sessions) cause historical distributions to re-emerge periodically.

Standard static models degrade silently under drift. Retraining from scratch is computationally expensive and discards valuable historical knowledge.

docs.title: 2. Imperfect, Delayed & Asymmetric Feedback
docs.text: Real-world feedback signals are rarely pristine ground truth: - Label Noise: Crowd-sourced annotators, automated heuristics, and sensor noise introduce mislabeled instances. - Asymmetric Corruption: Certain classes are systematically mislabeled more frequently than others (e.g., fraudulent transactions mislabeled as legitimate, but rarely vice versa). - Delayed Feedback: Ground truth \(y_t\) arrives with a variable latency \(\Delta t\) after inference \(x_t\), requiring asynchronous matching queues. - Extreme Class Imbalance: In fraud, threat detection, and disease diagnosis, critical minority classes represent \(<0.1\%\) of the stream, causing standard classifiers to collapse into majority-class trivial predictors.

docs.title: 3. Computational, Latency & Memory Constraints
docs.text:
Deploying continuous adaptation systems encounters severe infrastructure bottlenecks: - Unbounded Memory Growth: Retaining raw historical stream logs \(T\) causes \(O(T)\) memory growth, eventually triggering Out-Of-Memory (OOM) fatal crashes. - Optimizer State Bloat: Standard AdamW maintains two 32-bit floating point moments (\(m_t, v_t\)) per parameter, requiring \(8\text{ bytes}\) of optimizer state per weight and causing OOM on edge hardware. - Strict Latency SLAs: Real-time stream processing engines (Kafka, Flink, WebSocket microservices) require sub-millisecond per-sample processing latency (\(<1,000\ \mu\text{s}\)).

AdaptiveML is designed specifically to resolve these three structural challenges simultaneously.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Production Operations — Checkpoint and Recovery Guide
1. Overview and Invariants
docs.text:
AdaptiveML provides enterprise-grade, cryptographically verified checkpoint serialization and disaster recovery for both streaming algorithms and deep learning models.

Key invariants: 1. Zero-Bytecode Serialization: Uses the HuggingFace safetensors standard. Pickling of executable Python code is strictly prohibited. 2. Atomic Two-Phase Commits: Checkpoint files are written to staging files (.<name>.tmp.safetensors) and verified before atomic OS-level file replacement (os.replace). 3. Cryptographic SHA-256 Verification: Checkpoints calculate a cryptographic SHA-256 hash on write, stored in <name>.meta.json. On load, the file digest is recomputed and compared before memory allocation. 4. File Size Hard Limits: Defaults to a maximum checkpoint file size of \(5\text{ GB}\) to prevent memory exhaustion attacks.

docs.title: 2. Checkpointing Streaming Controllers
docs.text:
The UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1 supports full state persistence and restoration:

from adaptive_ml.state.serializer import save_state, load_state

# 1. Export controller state dictionary
state = controller.state_dict()

# 2. Persist with atomic write and SHA-256 checksum
save_state(
    "checkpoints/production_ulc.safetensors",
    state,
    metadata={"version": "1.0", "step": controller.total_steps},
)

# 3. Reload state with integrity verification
restored_state, metadata = load_state("checkpoints/production_ulc.safetensors")
controller.load_state_dict(restored_state)

docs.title: 3. Checkpointing PyTorch Integration Models
docs.text:
For PyTorch models running within AdaptiveML pipelines, use TorchCheckpointAdapter:

from adaptive_ml.integrations import TorchCheckpointAdapter

adapter = TorchCheckpointAdapter(
    checkpoint_dir="checkpoints/torch_model",
    save_best_only=True,
    monitor="val_loss",
    mode="min",
)

# Save checkpoint
adapter.save(model, optimizer=optimizer, epoch=10, metrics={"val_loss": 0.245})

# Restore best checkpoint
checkpoint_info = adapter.load_best(model, optimizer=optimizer)

docs.title: 4.1 Checkpoint Integrity Verification Failure
docs.text:
If load_state raises: 

SerializationError: Checkpoint integrity verification failed for ...: computed SHA-256 does not match metadata digest
Cause: The .safetensors binary file has experienced bit-rot, incomplete network transfer, or unauthorized file alteration. Action: 1. Do not load corrupted state into running pipelines. 2. Revert to the previous verified checkpoint (e.g. <name>_prev.safetensors). 3. If using distributed storage, re-download the checkpoint from primary storage.

docs.title: 4.2 Missing Metadata File
docs.text: If load_state finds .safetensors but the .meta.json file is missing: - A SerializationWarning is emitted to the diagnostic registry. - Loading proceeds only if verify_integrity=False is explicitly passed; otherwise load_state rejects unauthenticated checkpoints.

docs.title: 4.3 In-Flight Process Termination During Save
docs.text: Because writes are staged to temporary files (.model.tmp.safetensors) and replaced atomically, a process crash during save_state leaves the previous valid checkpoint completely intact.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Production Operations — Dependency Management Guide
1. Minimal-Core Philosophy
docs.text: AdaptiveML adheres to a strict minimal-core architecture: - Core Runtime Dependency: Only numpy>=1.24.0 is required. - Optional Extras: Deep learning, traditional machine learning, DataFrame adapters, and serialization formats are strictly isolated into optional extras. - CPU-First Architecture: The entire core runs seamlessly on standard x86_64 and ARM64 CPUs without CUDA or GPU dependencies.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Production Operations — Logging and Diagnostics Guide
1. Observability Architecture
docs.text:
AdaptiveML provides comprehensive zero-overhead observability for production streaming machine learning pipelines. Observability in AdaptiveML adheres to the following production principles:

  1. Local-Only by Default: Zero mandatory telemetry, zero network sockets opened, zero outbound phone-home analytics.
  2. Deterministic Bounded Ring Buffers: Diagnostic events are stored in a fixed-size ring buffer (\(O(N)\) with default capacity \(N=1,000\)), guaranteeing that event logging cannot cause memory leaks or OOM crashes.
  3. Structured Event Data: All diagnostic records are emitted as structured JSON-serializable dictionaries containing timestamp, component, level, message, and contextual metadata.
  4. Integration with Standard Python Logging: Emits events to Python's standard logging library hierarchy (adaptive_ml.*), enabling seamless ingestion into OpenTelemetry, Prometheus, Datadog, or Grafana Loki.

docs.title: 2. Configuring Production Logging
docs.text:
To configure structured logging with customized log levels and handlers, use configure_logging:

import logging
from adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics import configure_logging

# Enable INFO logging for AdaptiveML with custom format
configure_logging(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format_string="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(name)s: %(message)s",
)

docs.title: 3. Using the Diagnostic Event Registry
docs.text:
The DiagnosticRegistry singleton records anomalies, budget breaches, concept drift events, and automaton state transitions:

from adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics import (
    record_diagnostic_event,
    get_diagnostic_events,
    clear_diagnostic_events,
)

# Ingest or query events
events = get_diagnostic_events(component="ulc", min_level="WARNING")
for event in events:
    print(f"[{event['timestamp']}] {event['message']} (data: {event['metadata']})")

docs.title: Filtering Events Programmatically
docs.text: get_diagnostic_events() supports filtering by: - component: e.g. "ulc", "ala", "rla", "rao", "state" - min_level: "DEBUG", "INFO", "WARNING", "ERROR", "CRITICAL"

docs.title: 4. Monitoring Streaming Controller Telemetry
docs.text:
On every batch step, UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1.step() returns a real-time telemetry dictionary:

directive, telemetry = controller.step(X, y)

print(f"Step: {telemetry['step']}")
print(f"Automaton State: {telemetry['state']}")
print(f"Active Scenario: {telemetry['scenario']}")
print(f"Mean Sample Reliability: {telemetry['mean_reliability']:.3f}")
print(f"Retained Training Samples: {telemetry['n_retained_samples']}/{telemetry['n_input_samples']}")

docs.title: Recommended Alerting Rules
docs.text: Metric Trigger Condition Severity Recommended Action mean_reliability \(< 0.35\) for \(> 5\) steps WARNING Investigate data stream for sensor corruption or adversarial injection. n_retained_samples \(0\) for \(> 10\) steps ERROR Pipeline is discarding all data. Check filter threshold or recalibrate reliability scorer. state == NOISE_BURST \(> 12\) consecutive steps WARNING Dwell timeout will trigger escape to STABLE at step 15. Check upstream label quality. step_time_ms \(> \text{max\_step\_time\_ms}\) WARNING Budget manager will throttle tree split evaluations. Inspect CPU load.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Production Operations — Performance Tuning Guide
1. Streaming Latency and Throughput Architecture
docs.text: AdaptiveML is engineered for low-latency, CPU-first streaming environments. Empirical benchmarks demonstrate: - Single-Sample Inference: \(4.70\,\mu\text{s}\) P50 latency (\(209,000\text{ samples/s}\)). - Batch Inference (\(B=64\)): \(154.40\,\mu\text{s}\) P50 latency (\(409,000\text{ samples/s}\)). - Integrated ULC-v4.1 Pipeline (\(B=16\)): \(1.56\text{ ms}\) P50 latency (\(10,500\text{ samples/s}\)).

docs.title: 2. Ingestion Batch Sizing Guidelines
docs.text:
In streaming deployments, selecting an appropriate ingestion micro-batch size (\(B\)) balances throughput against end-to-end pipeline latency:

Ingestion Batch Size (\(B\)) Pipeline Latency (P50) Throughput (samples/s) Best Suited For \(B=1\) (Pure Online) \(252\,\mu\text{s}\) \(3,660\text{ samples/s}\) Hard real-time fraud detection, sub-millisecond trading triggers. \(B=16\) (Recommended) \(1,558\,\mu\text{s}\) \(10,560\text{ samples/s}\) High-throughput sensor streams, edge gateway aggregators. \(B=64\) (High-Throughput) \(5,099\,\mu\text{s}\) \(12,460\text{ samples/s}\) Near real-time log ingestion, network packet classification. \(B \ge 256\) \(> 20,000\,\mu\text{s}\) \(\approx 12,500\text{ samples/s}\) CPU cache thrashing observed; diminishing throughput returns.

[!TIP] For most production streaming deployments, a micro-batch size between \(16\) and \(64\) samples delivers the optimal balance of high throughput (\(>10,000\text{ samples/s}\)) and sub-\(5\text{ ms}\) latency.

docs.title: 3.1 AdaptiveClassifier Grace Period
docs.text:
The grace_period controls how many streaming samples a leaf must observe before computing Hoeffding bounds for splitting: 

clf = AdaptiveClassifier(grace_period=50, delta=1e-4)
- Low grace_period (e.g. 10–20): Rapid tree growth, adapts quickly to changing distributions, but higher CPU overhead during continuous split re-evaluation. - High grace_period (e.g. 50–200): Maximizes training throughput (\(>20,000\text{ samples/s}\)), ideal for stable or slowly drifting regimes.

docs.title: 3.2 Reliability Engine Spatial Buffer & Neighborhood
docs.text:
In MultiSignalReliabilityEngine: 

engine = MultiSignalReliabilityEngine(k_neighbors=5, buffer_size=300)
- buffer_size=300: Keeps pairwise distance matrix computation small (\(N \times 300\)). Increasing beyond \(1,000\) increases step latency without meaningful accuracy improvements. - k_neighbors=5: Provides optimal noise filtering without susceptibility to local cluster sparsity.

docs.title: 3.3 Reliability-Weighted ADWIN Delta
docs.text:
In ReliabilityWeightedADWIN: 

adwin = ReliabilityWeightedADWIN(delta=0.002)
- Lower \(\delta\) (e.g. \(10^{-4}\)): Decreases false positive drift detections in noisy streams. - Higher \(\delta\) (e.g. \(10^{-2}\)): Faster reaction to subtle or gradual concept drift.

docs.title: 4. Zero-Copy and Memory Alignment Tuning
docs.text:
1. Ensure C-Contiguity: Ensure feature matrices are contiguous in memory (np.ascontiguousarray(X, dtype=np.float32)).
  2. Avoid Type Casting in Streaming Loops: Pass float32 features and int64 labels to eliminate runtime type promotion overhead.
  3. PyTorch Tensor Sharing: On CPU, torch.from_numpy() creates a zero-copy tensor sharing underlying memory with NumPy. Avoid .clone() unless independent mutation is required.

docs.title: 1. Overview and Invariants
docs.text:
AdaptiveML is architected for continuous 24/7 streaming machine learning operations in non-stationary and adversarial environments. The system provides zero-crash guarantees for streaming pipelines under the following invariants:

  1. Deterministic Bounded Memory: Asymptotic memory complexity is \(O(1)\) relative to total streaming time. All history buffers, replay memories, and diagnostic logs are bounded by hard maximum capacities.
  2. Crash-Free Degradation: Transient numerical anomalies (NaNs, Infs, zero-variance batches, degenerate class distributions) trigger graceful degradation rather than unhandled process termination.
  3. Automaton Non-Locking: The 12-state arbitration automaton in ULC-v4.1 cannot become permanently trapped in absorbing noise or conflict states due to explicit maximum dwell timeouts (\(\tau_{\text{dwell}} \le 15\) steps).
  4. Reversible Arbitration: All intervention directives (learning rate adjustments, tree splits, replay buffer purges) are scoped, tracked in historical telemetry, and can be rolled back.

docs.title: 3.1 Streaming Step Health Checks
docs.text: Monitor the telemetry dict returned by UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1.step(): - state: Ensure state transitions dynamically across STABLE, DRIFT_DETECTED, NOISE_BURST, and ELEVATED_VARIANCE. A state locked in NOISE_BURST for \(>15\) steps indicates improper dwell configuration. - mean_reliability: Drops below \(0.30\) signal severe upstream data corruption or adversarial label injection. - n_retained_samples: If zero samples are retained across \(>10\) consecutive batches, inspect sample filter threshold.

docs.title: 3.2 Resetting Controller State
docs.text:
In case of catastrophic environmental corruption, invoke the safe reset method: 

controller.reset()
This resets the arbitration automaton to STABLE, clears dwell and cooldown counters, and purges transient error accumulators while preserving model weights and replay buffers.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Production Operations — Resource Management Guide
1. Principles of Resource-Aware Optimization (RAO)
docs.text:
In high-throughput edge, on-premise, or cloud streaming ML deployments, memory consumption and latency variance must remain strictly bounded. Unchecked memory growth leads to OS out-of-memory (OOM) killer terminations, while latency spikes breach production service level agreements (SLAs).

AdaptiveML enforces resource predictability through four core mechanisms: 1. Dynamic Resource Budgeting: Real-time latency and memory utilization monitoring. 2. Quantized Optimizer States: \(75\%\) reduction in AdamW optimizer memory via 64-block quantization. 3. Adaptive Gradient Accumulation: Dynamic scaling of micro-batch execution under tight memory ceilings. 4. Stratified Reservoir Memory: Class-balanced rehearsal buffers with hard capacity ceilings.

docs.title: 2. Dynamic Resource Budget Manager
docs.text:
The DynamicResourceBudgetManager monitors wall-clock execution time and RSS footprint:

from adaptive_ml.rao.budget import DynamicResourceBudgetManager

budget_mgr = DynamicResourceBudgetManager(
    max_step_time_ms=50.0,    # SLA step latency ceiling
    max_memory_mb=2048.0,     # Physical memory allocation ceiling
    throttle_factor=0.5,      # Back-off multiplier on breach
)

docs.title: Utilization Evaluation
docs.text: During each step, the budget manager evaluates resource state: - If step_time_ms > max_step_time_ms: Emits THROTTLE_COMPUTATION directive, scaling down batch size or disabling optional tree split evaluations. - If current_memory_mb > max_memory_mb: Emits PURGE_REPLAY or SHRINK_BUFFERS directive to reclaim heap space.

docs.title: 3. Low-Memory Optimizer Deployment
docs.text:
Standard AdamW stores first (\(m\)) and second (\(v\)) moment vectors in 32-bit floating point, tripling model parameter memory overhead. In contrast, LowMemoryAdamW segments tensors into 64-element blocks and applies dynamic 8-bit quantization:

from adaptive_ml.integrations import create_torch_low_memory_adamw

# Drop-in replacement for torch.optim.AdamW
optimizer = create_torch_low_memory_adamw(
    model.parameters(),
    lr=1e-3,
    weight_decay=1e-4,
    block_size=64,
)

docs.title: Memory Footprint Comparison
docs.text: Parameter Count Standard AdamW State LowMemoryAdamW State Memory Reduction \(10\text{ Million}\) \(80.0\text{ MB}\) \(20.3\text{ MB}\) \(-74.6\%\) \(100\text{ Million}\) \(800.0\text{ MB}\) \(203.1\text{ MB}\) \(-74.6\%\) \(1\text{ Billion}\) \(8.0\text{ GB}\) \(2.03\text{ GB}\) \(-74.6\%\)

docs.title: 4. Rehearsal Buffer Capacity Limits
docs.text:
To prevent infinite memory growth during continual learning, the ClassBalancedReservoirReplay enforces a strict sample ceiling:

from adaptive_ml.ala.replay import ClassBalancedReservoirReplay

# Bounded capacity of 2,000 samples across 5 classes
replay = ClassBalancedReservoirReplay(capacity=2000, n_classes=5)
  • When the buffer reaches 2,000 samples, incoming instances replace existing instances using Vitter's Algorithm \(R\).
  • Majority-class samples are preferentially replaced to safeguard minority class representation.
  • Absolute heap memory remains constant at \(O(\text{capacity} \times \text{features})\).

docs.title: 1. Threat Model & Security Posture
docs.text:
Streaming ML pipelines operate in production environments exposed to untrusted user input, external network streams, and remote distributed storage. AdaptiveML enforces a comprehensive defensive security posture addressing four primary threat vectors:

  1. Arbitrary Code Execution via Deserialization: Standard Python serialization (pickle) allows arbitrary remote code execution via object reduction payloads. AdaptiveML prohibits pickle in favor of SafeTensors.
  2. Checkpoint Tampering and Bit-Rot: Binary weights stored in distributed object stores (S3, GCS) or shared filesystems can be maliciously modified or corrupted during transit.
  3. Denial-of-Service via Resource Exhaustion: Maliciously oversized checkpoint payloads or unvalidated infinite input dimensions can trigger out-of-memory (OOM) crashes.
  4. Adversarial Label Poisoning: Coordinated label inversion attacks attempt to degrade model accuracy and force controller state trapping.

docs.title: 2.1 SafeTensors-First Format
docs.text: All model parameters and arrays are serialized using the HuggingFace safetensors standard: - No executable bytecode: SafeTensors files contain only a JSON header with tensor shapes/dtypes and raw contiguous binary buffer slices. - Zero-copy memory mapping: Tensors can be memory-mapped directly without running arbitrary Python deserialization code.

docs.title: 2.2 SHA-256 Cryptographic Digest Verification
docs.text:
Every checkpoint saved through save_state generates a cryptographic SHA-256 digest stored in an adjacent .meta.json file: 

from adaptive_ml.state.serializer import save_state, load_state

# Saves: model.safetensors and model.meta.json (containing _sha256 digest)
save_state("checkpoints/model.safetensors", state_dict)

# Validates: computes SHA-256 on load, raises SerializationError on bit mismatch
loaded_state, metadata = load_state("checkpoints/model.safetensors")
If an adversary or bit-rot alters even a single byte of model.safetensors, load_state immediately rejects the file with: 
SerializationError: Checkpoint integrity verification failed for ...: computed SHA-256 does not match metadata digest

docs.title: 2.3 Atomic Two-Phase Commits
docs.text: To prevent corrupt checkpoints resulting from power failure, SIGKILL, or network disconnection mid-write: 1. Files are written to hidden temporary files: .<name>.tmp.safetensors and .<name>.tmp.meta.json. 2. Both files are flushed and synced to disk. 3. Files are atomically renamed into place using OS-level atomic filesystem primitives (os.replace).

docs.title: 2.4 File Size Ceiling Limits
docs.text:
To guard against disk exhaustion and memory ballooning attacks, load_state strictly enforces a maximum file size limit (default: \(5\text{ GB}\)): 

if file_size > max_file_size_bytes:
    raise SerializationError(f"Checkpoint file size ({file_size} bytes) exceeds safety limit")

docs.title: 3. Input Validation Boundaries
docs.text:
All public entrypoints in AdaptiveML validate external inputs using defensive utilities in adaptive_ml/core/validation.py:

Function Validation Enforced Exception Raised check_array_2d Ensures 2D NumPy array, converts from array-like, rejects NaN / Inf, checks minimum rows ValidationError check_labels_1d Ensures 1D integer labels, validates range \(0 \le y_i < K\), checks length match ValidationError check_probabilities Ensures valid probability range \([0, 1]\), validates row sums equal \(1.0 \pm 10^{-3}\) ValidationError check_non_negative_finite Enforces finite real numbers \(\ge 0\) for time/memory budgets ValidationError

docs.title: 4. Supply Chain & Dependency Invariants
docs.text:
• Core library depends only on numpy>=1.24.0.
  • Zero mandatory network access, zero outbound telemetry, zero background phone-home threads.
  • All optional dependencies (PyTorch, scikit-learn, SafeTensors, pandas, Polars) use permissive open-source licenses (Apache-2.0, BSD-3-Clause, MIT).
  • Automated dependency vulnerability scanning is integrated via pip check.

docs.title: 1. Quick Diagnostics Cheat Sheet
docs.text:
When diagnosing unexpected pipeline behavior, inspect the diagnostic log and controller state: 

from adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics import get_diagnostic_events

# Print last 10 warnings or errors
for event in get_diagnostic_events(min_level="WARNING")[-10:]:
    print(f"[{event['timestamp']}] {event['component'].upper()} {event['level']}: {event['message']}")

docs.title: 2.1 Issue: ValidationError: X must be a 2-dimensional array
docs.text:
• Symptom: Single streaming sample raises ValidationError: X must be a 2-dimensional array, got shape (8,).
  • Root Cause: Passing a 1D feature vector directly to step(), predict_proba(), or score_reliability().
  • Resolution: Reshape input to 2D before ingestion: 
    X_sample = x.reshape(1, -1)  # shape becomes (1, D)
controller.step(X_sample, np.array([y]))

docs.title: 2.2 Issue: SerializationError: Checkpoint integrity verification failed
docs.text:
• Symptom: Checkpoint loading fails during start-up or container restart.
  • Root Cause: Bit-rot, truncated file write, or manual edits to .safetensors without updating .meta.json.
  • Resolution:
  • Restore checkpoint from backup or upstream object storage (S3/GCS).
  • If manually inspecting weights, do not edit binary files with text editors.
  • If unauthenticated recovery is explicitly required, pass verify_integrity=False to load_state.

docs.title: 2.3 Issue: SerializationError: State serialization requires the optional 'safetensors' dependency
docs.text:
• Symptom: Calling save_state raises SerializationError.
  • Root Cause: Environment was installed with bare pip install aml-core without the serialization extra.
  • Resolution: Install the extra: 
    pip install 'aml-core[safetensors]'

docs.title: 2.4 Issue: Controller State Stuck in NOISE_BURST
docs.text:
• Symptom: Telemetry reports state: NOISE_BURST for dozens of consecutive batches.
  • Root Cause: Upstream sensor failure or adversarial stream where \(>40\%\) of labels are corrupted.
  • Resolution:
  • The controller will automatically escape to STABLE after max_noise_dwell steps (default: 15).
  • Check controller.config.max_noise_dwell.
  • Inspect upstream data ingestion quality.
  • If necessary, call controller.reset() to force immediate recovery to STABLE.

docs.title: 2.5 Issue: n_retained_samples == 0 Across Consecutive Batches
docs.text:
• Symptom: No training updates occur because all incoming samples are filtered out.
  • Root Cause: Directive sample_filter_threshold is higher than the reliability scores assigned by RLA.
  • Resolution:
  • Inspect telemetry['mean_reliability']. If very low (\(<0.20\)), labels do not match feature spatial neighborhoods.
  • Tune weight_margin vs weight_neighbor in MultiSignalReliabilityEngine.
  • Reset the reliability search index via engine.clear().

docs.title: 2.6 Issue: Memory Creep in Custom Integration Scripts
docs.text:
• Symptom: Process RSS steadily increases over hours of streaming.
  • Root Cause: Accumulating references to telemetry dicts or tensors in an unbounded Python list inside user training loops.
  • Resolution:
  • Do not store full telemetry dictionaries in unbounded lists.
  • Use collections.deque(maxlen=1000) for application-level metric history.
  • Delete intermediate PyTorch tensors or detach them from computation graphs (t.detach().cpu().numpy()).

docs.title: 2.7 Issue: PyTorch Memory Leak During Training
docs.text:
• Symptom: GPU/CPU memory climbs during iterative training with TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss.
  • Root Cause: Storing computation graphs across steps by holding references to loss rather than loss.item().
  • Resolution: 
    # Bad: holds reference to computation graph
loss_history.append(loss)

# Good: extracts raw float value
loss_history.append(loss.item())

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This report establishes the formal milestone completion for Stages 4, 5, and 6 (Phases 12 through 16) of the AdaptiveML project.

Across these five phases, the multidisciplinary engineering, research, and release team has: 1. Empirically Proven Core Mathematical Hypotheses: Conducted multi-seed benchmarking on physical host hardware. Proved Theorem 2 (minority recall preserved at \(60.0\%\) under 100:1 severe imbalance vs. \(0.0\%\) total failure for standard Cross-Entropy), demonstrated an exact \(73.44\%\) optimizer state RAM reduction (\(2.125\text{ B/param}\) vs. \(8.00\text{ B/param}\)) without sacrificing convex convergence, and eliminated \(100\%\) of catastrophic retraining wipes under high-noise bursts via dual-evidence arbitration. 2. Engineered Seamless Framework Adapters: Delivered zero-overhead scikit-learn estimators (SklearnAdaptiveClassifier) compatible with Pipeline, clone(), and partial_fit(), alongside PyTorch autograd loss functions (TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss) and native optimizer wrappers (create_torch_low_memory_adamw), while preserving strict zero-dependency core isolation. 3. Delivered Developer Experience & Tutorials: Authored an instant 5-minute executable quickstart (examples/quickstart.py, running in \(0.18\text{s}\)) and 7 step-by-step developer tutorials in docs/tutorials/. 5. Cleared Legal, IP, and Security Audits: Audited wheel artifacts (35 clean files, zero leaked secrets or tests), generated CycloneDX/SPDX Software Bills of Materials (SBOM), adopted DCO 1.1 sign-off, and enforced namespace protection under aml-core.

All 44 automated tests pass with a 100% pass rate in \(<3.0\) seconds on Python 3.14.

docs.title: 2.1 Research Experiments & Benchmarking (Phase 12)
docs.text:

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Audit Mandate
docs.text:
This document provides the authoritative, multi-disciplinary cross-phase quality, scientific reproducibility, and release clearance audit for Stages 4, 5, and 6 of the AdaptiveML open-source project.

The scope of this audit encompasses: 1. Phase 12 (Research Experiments & Benchmarking): Verification that all empirical claims are substantiated by reproducible multi-seed code, real execution telemetry, and rigorous statistical baselines without manufactured results. 2. Phase 13 (Framework Integrations): Verification that integrations with scikit-learn and PyTorch strictly preserve the core architectural invariant: zero mandatory framework dependencies and lazy runtime resolution. 3. Phase 14 (Production Engineering): Verification of PEP 517/621 packaging, multi-platform CI/CD automation, Bandit AST security analysis, pip-audit supply-chain verification, and CPU SIMD memory efficiency. 4. Phase 15 (Documentation & Developer Experience): Verification that all quickstart scripts, API reference docstrings, and 7 step-by-step tutorials execute to completion with zero errors. 5. Phase 16 (Legal & Release Audit): Verification of distribution artifacts, clean-room Apache-2.0 licensing, DCO 1.1 sign-off, SBOM generation, and trademark isolation via the provisional package namespace aml-core.

docs.title: 3. Phase 12 Verification: Empirical Evidence & Scientific Hypotheses
docs.text: All experimental claims were audited against raw execution telemetry recorded in benchmarks/phase-12/results/benchmark_results.json run on host hardware (AMD Ryzen 9 7945HX, 32 logical cores, 15.71 GB RAM, Windows 11).

docs.title: 3.1 Verification of Hypothesis \(H_1\) (ALA: Concept Drift Adaptation)
docs.text:
• Claim: Reliability-Weighted ADWIN detects concept transitions without triggering false drift alarms during high-entropy noise bursts.
  • Empirical Result: On the SEA concept stream (\(N=2000\)), AdaptiveClassifier maintained \(92.35\%\) mean accuracy across concept transitions, successfully triggering adaptation at drift boundaries (\(t=500, 1000, 1500\)) while filtering random label noise bursts.
  • Verdict: VERIFIED.

docs.title: 3.2 Verification of Hypothesis \(H_2\) (RLA: Theorem 2 Minority Preservation)
docs.text:
• Claim: Density-aware margin scoring preserves valid minority instances under severe class imbalance and label corruption, whereas standard empirical risk minimization (Cross-Entropy) discards or misclassifies them.
  • Empirical Result: On a synthetic stream with \(100:1\) class imbalance (\(990\) majority samples, \(10\) minority samples) and \(20\%\) noise corruption: $\(\text{Minority Recall}_{\text{ERM (Cross-Entropy)}} = 0.00\% \quad (\text{Complete minority failure})\)$ $\(\text{Minority Recall}_{\text{AdaptiveML (RLA)}} = 60.00\% \quad (\text{Theorem 2 verified})\)$ $\(\text{Macro } F_1\text{ Score elevated from } 0.6591 \rightarrow 0.8207 \quad (+24.5\%)\)$
  • Verdict: VERIFIED.

docs.title: 3.3 Verification of Hypothesis \(H_3\) (RAO: Optimizer State Memory Savings)
docs.text:
• Claim: 8-bit dynamic block quantization reduces AdamW optimizer state memory consumption by \(>70\%\) with zero degradation in convex convergence.
  • Empirical Result: Measured across parameter scales \(P \in [10^3, 10^4, 10^5, 10^6]\): $\(\text{Standard FP32 AdamW State Memory} = 8.000\text{ bytes/parameter}\)$ $\(\text{AdaptiveML LowMemoryAdamW State Memory} = 2.125\text{ bytes/parameter}\)$ $\(\text{Exact State RAM Reduction} = 73.44\% \quad (\text{Target } \ge 70\% \text{ exceeded})\)$ $\(\text{Convex Optimization Error on 2D Quadratic Bowl} = 0.033 \quad (\text{Clean convergence})\)$
  • Verdict: VERIFIED.

docs.title: 3.4 Verification of Hypothesis \(H_4\) (ULC: Dual-Evidence Dynamic Arbitration)
docs.text:
• Claim: In-loop dual-evidence arbitration resolves the drift vs. noise dilemma, preventing catastrophic forgetting caused by erroneous model resets.
  • Empirical Result: Under an 85% label noise burst: $\(\text{Uncoordinated Drift Detection} \rightarrow 10 \text{ false model resets (Catastrophic Forget)}\)$ $\(\text{AdaptiveML ULC Arbitration} \rightarrow 0 \text{ false model resets (100\% protected)}\)$ $\(\text{Corrupted Noise Samples Filtered by RLA Pipeline} = 83.2\%\)$
  • Verdict: VERIFIED.

docs.title: 4. Phase 13 Verification: Framework Compatibility & Decoupling Invariants
docs.text: The Phase 13 architecture was audited to ensure strict adherence to ecosystem conventions while upholding core isolation:

docs.title: 4.1 Scikit-Learn Compatibility
docs.text:
• Audited Component: SklearnAdaptiveClassifier
  • Protocol Adherence:
  • Inherits from sklearn.base.BaseEstimator and sklearn.base.ClassifierMixin.
  • Complies with scikit-learn constructor conventions (no *args or **kwargs, parameters assigned without mutation).
  • Full compatibility with sklearn.base.clone().
  • Full integration with sklearn.pipeline.Pipeline (verified via examples/integrations/sklearn_pipeline_example.py).
  • Implements partial_fit(X, y, classes=...) for out-of-core streaming pipelines.
  • Test Coverage: 3/3 dedicated integration tests passed in tests/integration/test_sklearn_integration.py.

docs.title: 4.2 PyTorch Compatibility
docs.text:
• Audited Components:
  • create_torch_low_memory_adamw: Seamless drop-in optimizer for PyTorch neural network parameters.
  • TorchSymmetricCrossEntropyLoss: Native torch.nn.Module computing bounded reverse cross-entropy with analytical autograd compatibility.
  • Test Coverage: 2/2 dedicated integration tests passed in tests/integration/test_torch_integration.py.
  • Runtime Verification: examples/integrations/torch_training_example.py executed successfully, training a 2-layer MLP while verifying 2.12 bytes/param optimizer state memory.

docs.title: 4.3 Zero Core Pollution Invariant
docs.text:
• Audit Check: Inspect adaptive_ml/core/, adaptive_ml/ala/, adaptive_ml/rla/, adaptive_ml/rao/, adaptive_ml/ulc/.
  • Result: Core components import strictly from standard library and numpy. No import statements for torch or sklearn exist outside adaptive_ml/integrations/ and optional backend wrappers. All integration imports are lazily executed and guarded by try...except ImportError.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Audit Mandate
docs.text:
This cross-phase consistency audit evaluates the alignment, stability, security, and release readiness across Phases 14, 15, and 16 of the AdaptiveML open-source project.

The audit team verified fifteen strict production invariants to ensure that: 1. The codebase is packaged cleanly into standard PEP 517 / PEP 621 distribution artifacts without leaked secrets, test fixtures, or temporary files. 2. The documentation matches the real Python source code, docstrings, and verified benchmark metrics. 3. Legal, licensing, IP, and supply-chain requirements are completely fulfilled under Apache-2.0 and DCO 1.1 governance.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Policy Mandate
docs.text:
This report evaluates all datasets, generators, and data streams utilized across benchmarks, unit tests, integration tests, and tutorials in AdaptiveML.

Per Phase 0 and Phase 3 Research Governance: 1. Zero Proprietary Data Vendoring: The repository and distribution packages must never bundle proprietary, restricted, or unverified third-party datasets. 2. Zero Personally Identifiable Information (PII): All training streams must be devoid of individual personal data, GDPR/CCPA regulated identifiers, or biometric attributes. 3. Synthetic Generator Priority: Benchmarks and tutorials must prioritize mathematically specified synthetic data generators that execute in-memory with deterministic random seeds.
