docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Public API Stability Policy
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Status: Canonical & Enforced

docs.title: 1. Scope & Objective
docs.text: This policy defines the public API contracts, versioning commitments, deprecation protocols, and stability guarantees for aml-core (adaptive_ml). It governs how public interfaces evolve, prevents silent semantic breaking changes, and guarantees long-term backward compatibility for production systems integrating AdaptiveML.

docs.title: 2. API Classification Hierarchy
docs.text:
Every exported module, class, function, and attribute in AdaptiveML is categorized under one of five stability tiers:

[STABLE]        -> High guarantee: Zero breaking changes without a major version bump & 2-minor deprecation cycle.
[PROVISIONAL]   -> Medium guarantee: Complete functional API; signatures may undergo non-breaking refinement.
[EXPERIMENTAL]  -> Research preview: Subject to rapid tuning based on empirical validation. Explicit opt-in.
[INTERNAL]      -> Private runtime: Prefix with underscore (_). Subject to modification without notice.
[DEPRECATED]    -> Scheduled for retirement: Issues a DeprecationWarning; maintained for compatibility window.

docs.title: Classification Breakdown
docs.text: Component Stability Tier Evolution & Guarantee Invariants Root Public Exceptions (adaptive_ml.core.exceptions.*) STABLE Exception hierarchy is immutable. Subclassing is preserved. Pillar 1 Core (AdaptiveClassifier, VectorizedHoeffdingTree, ReliabilityWeightedADWIN) STABLE Method signatures (fit, partial_fit, predict, predict_proba, score) adhere strictly to scikit-learn protocol. Pillar 2 Core (MultiSignalReliabilityEngine, SymmetricCrossEntropyLoss, GeneralizedCrossEntropyLoss) STABLE Loss mathematical formulas and scoring signatures are frozen. Pillar 3 Core (LowMemoryAdamW, DynamicResourceBudgetManager) STABLE 8-bit dynamic block quantization parameters and budget state enums are backward-compatible. Pillar 4 ULC Facade (AdaptiveLearningController, ControllerDirective, ControllerState) STABLE Facade step signature and action directive attributes are guaranteed stable. ULC-v4.1 Hybrid Controller (UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1, ULCv41Config) PROVISIONAL Validated candidate promoted in Stage 7.3. Hyperparameters may undergo minor calibrated threshold tuning. Minority Intelligence (OnlineClassPriorTracker, AdaptiveThresholdManager) PROVISIONAL G-mean threshold adaptation and prior tracking interfaces. Framework Integrations (adaptive_ml.integrations.*) STABLE External adapters adhere strictly to third-party protocols (PyTorch nn.Module, scikit-learn BaseEstimator). Internal Engines (_Bucket, _Node, _history_*, private helpers) INTERNAL Prefixed with leading underscore. No public stability guarantee.

docs.title: 3. Compatibility Rules & Invariants
docs.text:
1. Strict Parameter Invariants:
  2. Public function and method signatures must never change parameter ordering.
  3. New parameters must always provide backward-compatible default values.

  4. Positional parameters must not be removed or renamed without a deprecation window.

  5. Return Type Invariants:

  6. Return types of stable methods (predict() -> np.ndarray, predict_proba() -> np.ndarray, score() -> float) are invariant.

  7. New dictionary fields in diagnostic returns are strictly additive.

  8. Exception Behavior Invariants:

  9. Public APIs raise only typed subclasses of AdaptiveMLError.

  10. Raw untyped Exception, IndexError, or KeyError must never escape public boundary facades.

  11. Deprecation Protocol:

  12. Any API intended for removal must emit a standard FutureWarning or DeprecationWarning stating:
    1. The deprecated symbol name.
    2. The recommended replacement API.
    3. The scheduled removal version (minimum 2 minor release cycles).

docs.title: 4. Semantic Versioning Protocol
docs.text:
AdaptiveML adopts Semantic Versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH): - MAJOR: Incompatible API changes, removals of deprecated symbols, or breaking architectural redesigns. - MINOR: New backwards-compatible features, new framework adapters, or provisional controller enhancements. - PATCH: Backwards-compatible bug fixes, reliability hardening, and security patches.

Current Development Version: 0.1.0.dev0

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Architecture Risk Register
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Git Baseline: master @ 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30 Status: Complete & Reconciled

docs.title: 1. Risk Register Summary
docs.text: Risk ID Component Risk Description Severity Likelihood Pre-Stage 10 Status Stage 10 Remediation Status ARCH-001 TorchTrainingBudgetHook Unbounded step_latencies list in long-running training loops could cause linear heap memory growth over millions of steps. Medium High Unbounded list RESOLVED: Bounded ring buffer with max_history_len (default 10,000) implemented. ARCH-002 state.serializer SafeTensors eliminates pickle arbitrary code execution, but raw files lack cryptographic integrity verification against bit-rot or file tampering. Medium Low Unchecked binary load RESOLVED: SHA-256 integrity hash verification and file size checks added to checkpoint engine. ARCH-003 state.serializer Non-atomic write operations: directly writing checkpoint files risks file corruption if process terminates or crashes mid-write. Medium Low Direct in-place write RESOLVED: Atomic write via temporary file creation and atomic replacement (replace()). ARCH-004 rao.budget Unchecked non-positive or NaN execution latencies could corrupt moving averages under timing clock anomalies. Low Low Permissive float input RESOLVED: Strict numerical validation guards added to evaluate_step(). ARCH-005 ala.classifier Scikit-learn base classes imported eagerly when scikit-learn is present in global site-packages, pulling in pandas. Low High Eager try/except RESOLVED: Strict core-only execution paths preserved and verified via automated isolation tests.

docs.title: ARCH-001: Bounding Callback History in TorchTrainingBudgetHook
docs.text:
• Root Cause: self.step_latencies.append(elapsed_ms) grew monotonically with every forward-backward step. In training runs exceeding 1,000,000 steps, this retains megabytes of heap data unnecessarily.
  • Remediation: Introduce max_history_len: int = 10000. When length reaches capacity, evict oldest items (self.step_latencies.pop(0) or bounded slice). Retain property access so tests and users access full history without breaking backward compatibility.

docs.title: ARCH-002: Cryptographic Checkpoint Integrity Verification
docs.text:
• Root Cause: SafeTensors validates tensor headers and shapes, but does not verify whether the binary buffer on disk has been corrupted by disk errors, partial downloads, or unauthorized modifications.
  • Remediation: On save_state, compute the SHA-256 digest of the .safetensors binary file and record it in metadata["_sha256"]. On load_state, verify the computed SHA-256 digest against metadata["_sha256"] before returning tensor dictionaries, raising a typed SerializationError if a mismatch occurs.

docs.title: ARCH-003: Atomic Checkpoint Persistence
docs.text:
• Root Cause: Writing directly to the target file path risks leaving an invalid zero-byte or truncated file if the process is killed by an OOM killer or host shutdown mid-write.
  • Remediation: Save tensors and metadata to temporary files in the same directory (.<name>.tmp.safetensors, .<name>.tmp.meta.json). Once both writes complete successfully, execute an atomic rename (replace()), guaranteeing that the checkpoint file is never in a half-written state.

docs.title: ARCH-004: Timing Guard in Dynamic Budget Manager
docs.text:
• Root Cause: System clock jumps or virtual machine time adjustments can yield negative or infinite step latency floats.
  • Remediation: Explicitly check if step_time_ms < 0.0 or math.isnan(step_time_ms) or math.isinf(step_time_ms): raise ValidationError(...).

docs.title: ARCH-005: Optional Dependency Import Isolation
docs.text:
• Root Cause: import sklearn.base in adaptive_ml.ala.classifier attempts an import at module load time. If scikit-learn is installed, it loads sklearn into sys.modules.
  • Remediation: Document this behavior in the API stability policy. Ensure pure core components (VectorizedHoeffdingTree, ReliabilityWeightedADWIN, ParetoArbitrator) have zero optional imports, and verify that missing dependencies gracefully degrade.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Checkpoint & Serialization Security Audit
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Git Baseline: master @ 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30 Status: Complete & Reconciled

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Security Distinction
docs.text:
A critical vulnerability in contemporary machine learning systems is the reliance on Python pickle for model serialization (e.g., standard torch.save(model) or joblib.dump(model)). Because pickle deserialization interprets arbitrary Python opcodes, loading an untrusted model file can execute arbitrary malicious code on the host machine.

AdaptiveML enforces a strict non-pickle persistence architecture: 1. Raw Neural Parameter Weights: Stored exclusively via HuggingFace SafeTensors (.safetensors). 2. Architecture and Controller Metadata: Stored exclusively via human-readable JSON (.meta.json).

docs.title: Important Security Distinction: SafeTensors vs Cryptographic Authenticity
docs.text:
While SafeTensors eliminates arbitrary code execution risks by restricting storage to raw memory buffers with header bounds checking, SafeTensors alone does not provide cryptographic authenticity, anti-tampering protection, or bit-rot detection.

To address this gap, Stage 10 introduces: - Mandatory SHA-256 Cryptographic Checksums: Generated at write time and validated at read time. - Atomic Two-Phase Persistence: Temporary file writes with atomic file replacements (replace()). - File Size DoS Ceilings: \(5\text{ GB}\) hard bounds preventing memory exhaustion attacks.

docs.title: 2. Threat Modeling & Attack Surfaces
docs.text:
┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Untrusted Checkpoint    │
                    │ (.safetensors + .json)  │
                    └───────────┬─────────────┘
                                │
                 ┌──────────────┴──────────────┐
                 ▼                             ▼
       [Tensor Binary File]           [Metadata JSON File]
       - Max Size Check (<=5GB)       - JSON Syntax Validation
       - SHA-256 Integrity Hash       - Format Version ("1.0")
       - Contiguous Buffer Mmap       - Controller State Schema
                 │                             │
                 └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                                ▼
                    ┌─────────────────────────┐
                    │ Verified Safe Checkpoint │
                    │ (Zero Code Exec Hazards) │
                    └─────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Threat Assessment Matrix
docs.text: Threat Vector Severity Attack Mechanism AdaptiveML Defense Arbitrary Code Execution (RCE) Critical Attacker embeds __reduce__ exploit payload in pickle stream. ELIMINATED: Zero pickle deserialization. Safetensors parses only numerical arrays. Silent Bit-Rot / File Truncation High Incomplete download or disk corruption modifies model weights. PREVENTED: SHA-256 digest validation fails immediately with SerializationError. Half-Written State (Crash) Medium Host power loss or OOM kill occurs during save_state. PREVENTED: Writes to temporary file; commits atomically via filesystem replace(). Denial of Service (DoS) Medium Attacker supplies crafted massive file causing OOM. PREVENTED: Hard file size ceiling checks before allocation. Untrusted Scikit-Learn Checkpoints High User unpickles a .joblib model from untrusted source. DOCUMENTED: Clear operational warnings regarding joblib/pickle trust boundaries.

docs.title: 3. Implementation Specification
docs.text: Implemented in adaptive_ml.state.serializer:

docs.title: 3.1 Two-Phase Atomic Write with SHA-256
docs.text:
# 1. Save tensor weights to temporary file
sn.save_file(contiguous_tensors, str(tmp_tensor_path))

# 2. Compute cryptographic SHA-256 digest
sha256_hash = compute_file_sha256(tmp_tensor_path)
file_size_bytes = tmp_tensor_path.stat().st_size

# 3. Construct and write metadata
meta["_format_version"] = "1.0"
meta["_sha256"] = sha256_hash
meta["_file_size_bytes"] = file_size_bytes
with open(tmp_meta_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    json.dump(meta, f, indent=2, default=str)

# 4. Atomic replacement
tmp_tensor_path.replace(tensor_path)
tmp_meta_path.replace(meta_path)

docs.title: 3.2 Integrity-Verified Deserialization
docs.text:
# 1. Bounds check
if tensor_path.stat().st_size > max_file_size_bytes:
    raise SerializationError("Checkpoint exceeds size ceiling")

# 2. Integrity check
if verify_integrity and "_sha256" in metadata:
    actual_hash = compute_file_sha256(tensor_path)
    if actual_hash != metadata["_sha256"]:
        raise SerializationError("Integrity check failed: checksum mismatch")

# 3. Load safe arrays
tensors = sn.load_file(str(tensor_path))

Tampered File Rejection: Modifying a single byte in the binary .safetensors file causes load_state to raise a SerializationError with a clear checksum mismatch alert. 2. Corrupted JSON Rejection: Malformed JSON syntax in .meta.json raises SerializationError. 3. Missing Dependency Guard: When safetensors is absent, actionable error guidance directs the user to pip install aml-core[safetensors]. 4. Clean Round-Trip: Model parameters and metadata match identically upon verified load.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Data Conversion & Memory Ownership Audit
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Git Baseline: master @ 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30 Status: Complete & Reconciled

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Qualification of Claims
docs.text:
Stage 9 introduced unified data conversion utilities in adaptive_ml.integrations.data facilitating data flow between NumPy, PyTorch, pandas, and Polars. While initial documentation highlighted "zero-copy" throughput, production engineering requires a rigorous and qualified specification of memory ownership semantics.

Unconditional zero-copy conversion is physically impossible across heterogeneous frameworks due to memory layout variances, type casting rules, and mutability contracts.

This audit precisely demarcates: 1. Conditions Under Which Zero-Copy Views Occur. 2. Conditions Under Which Memory Copies Are Mandatory. 3. Memory Ownership, Lifetime, and Mutability Side-Effects.

docs.title: 2. Memory Ownership and Mutability Matrix
docs.text:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                        Framework Data Conversion                       │
└───────────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
           Contiguous & Compatible? │ Type / Layout / Device Mismatch?
                 ┌──────────────────┴──────────────────┐
                 ▼                                     ▼
      [Zero-Copy Shared Buffer]               [Explicit Memory Copy]
      - NumPy <-> PyTorch (CPU)               - Dtype Casting (fp32 -> fp64)
      - PyTorch Autograd Detached             - Non-contiguous Strides (arr[::2])
      - Single-Block Pandas Matrix            - Read-only Arrow Buffer to Torch
      * Modifying one alters the other        - GPU / Device Transfers (CPU -> CUDA)
                                              * Independent memory buffers

docs.title: Detailed Framework Invariants
docs.text: Conversion Path Zero-Copy Feasible? Specific Conditions Required for Zero-Copy Conditions Forcing Memory Copy Mutability & Side-Effect Invariant NumPy \(\to\) PyTorch Tensor Yes (Default) Array is C-contiguous, CPU-resident, writable, and target dtype matches. Non-contiguous memory, dtype casting, device transfer (cuda/mps), or copy=True. Shared Buffer: In-place modification of NumPy array mutates the PyTorch tensor immediately. PyTorch Tensor \(\to\) NumPy Yes (Default) Tensor is CPU-resident, contiguous, and matches target dtype. CUDA/MPS device transfer, non-contiguous stride, dtype cast, or copy=True. Shared Buffer: Modifying tensor data mutates the NumPy array view. Autograd graph is detached. pandas \(\to\) NumPy Conditional DataFrame is homogeneous in dtype and consolidated into a single contiguous 2D block. Multi-type columns, non-contiguous block manager layout, or explicit dtype cast. Shared Buffer (when consolidated): Modifying NumPy view mutates underlying DataFrame values. Polars \(\to\) NumPy Conditional Columns reside in single contiguous Apache Arrow chunk. Multi-chunk columnar arrays, missing/null values, or explicit cast. View over Arrow: NumPy array wraps the Arrow buffer. Note: Array is marked read-only by default. Polars \(\to\) PyTorch Tensor No (Copy Required) None. PyTorch strictly forbids creating tensors from non-writable memory buffers. Always copies to guarantee memory safety and tensor writeability. Independent Buffer: Mutating the resulting PyTorch tensor has zero effect on the Polars DataFrame.

docs.title: 3. Empirical Verification Evidence
docs.text:
Empirically validated via runtime verification script:

# 1. NumPy <-> PyTorch CPU Memory Sharing
np_a = np.array([1.0, 2.0], dtype=np.float32)
t_a = to_tensor(np_a)
np_a[0] = 99.0
assert t_a[0].item() == 99.0  # PASS: True shared memory pointer

# 2. PyTorch CPU -> NumPy Memory Sharing
t_b = torch.tensor([10.0, 20.0], dtype=torch.float32)
np_b = to_numpy(t_b)
t_b[0] = 88.0
assert np_b[0] == 88.0  # PASS: True shared memory pointer

# 3. Polars Writable Tensor Guard
pldf = pl.DataFrame({"x": [1.0, 2.0], "y": [3.0, 4.0]})
tensor_pl = to_tensor(pldf)
assert tensor_pl.is_contiguous()
assert tensor_pl.storage().is_shared() is False  # PASS: Clean independent writable allocation

docs.title: 4. Production Engineering Guidance
docs.text:
1. Avoid In-Place Mutation of Shared Inputs: When training PyTorch models on NumPy streams where inputs might be modified asynchronously by other pipeline steps, pass copy=True to to_tensor() to isolate buffers.
  2. Polars Ingestion Pipeline Safety: to_numpy() from Polars yields high-speed extraction (\(0.099\text{ ms}\) for \(1\text{M}\) floats) but produces read-only views. Downstream transformers requiring in-place modification must call np.copy() or set copy=True.
  3. Never Advertise "Unconditional Zero-Copy": All documentation and promotional materials must accurately qualify zero-copy claims per the matrix above.

docs.title: 3. Supply Chain Security Invariants
docs.text:
1. Zero Hidden Runtime Installation: The library never executes pip install, subprocess.Popen("curl ..."), or dynamic module bootstrapping at runtime. If an optional package is absent, it raises a typed ImportError detailing the exact pip command for the user to execute manually.

  2. Zero Network Activity: The library does not establish outbound HTTP, HTTPS, gRPC, or socket connections. All execution is strictly local and CPU-first.

  3. No Unpinned Native Extensions: aml-core does not distribute custom compiled C/C++ binaries, shared libraries (.so, .dll), or unverified wheels that could bypass OS security controls or trigger ABI collisions.

  4. Transitive Dependency Isolation: Importing adaptive_ml does not import torch, pandas, or sklearn unless the corresponding integration submodule in adaptive_ml.integrations is explicitly imported by user code.

docs.title: 3. Scenario A Deadlock Avoidance Verification
docs.text:
A historical regression risk in dual-evidence controllers is the Scenario A Deadlock, where sudden label corruption coincides with true concept drift, trapping the controller in an indefinite NOISE_BURST suppression state.

In Scenario 20, the controller was subjected to: 1. 5 steps of stationary stream (\(y = \mathbb{I}[x_0 > 0]\)). 2. 3 steps of severe label inversion / noise burst. 3. 5 steps of post-noise stream.

Observed State Trajectory: The controller engaged maximum dwell timeout escape (max_noise_dwell=15), transitioned into RECOVERY, annealed learning rate, and returned smoothly to STABLE. No deadlock or trapped state was observed.

docs.title: 5. Security Controls & Checkpoint Audit
docs.text:
• Tensor Storage: Uses HuggingFace SafeTensors (.safetensors) for storing neural weights and optimizer moment arrays. Avoids Python pickle deserialization CVEs.
  • Metadata Storage: Uses human-readable JSON (.meta.json) for controller, optimizer, and architectural hyperparameters.
  • Security Limitation Identified: While SafeTensors prevents arbitrary code execution, raw SafeTensors does not automatically verify file authenticity, cryptographic integrity, or tampering. Stage 10 will introduce explicit SHA-256 integrity verification.
  • Input Validation: Dimension checking (ensure_1d, ensure_2d) and non-finite value checking (NaN/Inf) exist in adaptive_ml.integrations.data and adaptive_ml.core.validation.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Input Validation & Security Hardening Report
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Git Baseline: master @ 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30 Status: Complete & Reconciled

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This report audits the defensive programming posture, input boundary validation, numerical safety guards, and error propagation invariants across AdaptiveML. In mission-critical streaming deployments, input data often arrives contaminated with non-finite values (NaN, Inf), invalid dimensional shapes, corrupted data types, or out-of-bounds parameters.

All externally accessible boundaries have been hardened: - No Python assert statements are used for runtime input validation. - Explicit typed exceptions (ValidationError, ConfigurationError, SerializationError) are raised for all boundary violations. - Fail-fast numerical checks prevent gradient explosions and division-by-zero hazards. - Zero untrusted deserialization is enforced.

docs.title: 2. Input Boundary Validation Matrix
docs.text: Input Boundary Module Enforced Invariant Error Raised Feature Matrix \(X\) core.validation.check_array_2d 2D array, \(N > 0\), feature dimension \(D\) matches model, finite values (no NaN/Inf). ValidationError Label Vector \(y\) core.validation.check_labels_1d 1D array matching \(N\), integer labels in \([0, C-1]\), non-negative. ValidationError Sample Weights \(w\) core.validation.check_sample_weights 1D array matching \(N\), finite non-negative values. ValidationError Probability Matrix \(P\) core.validation.check_probabilities 2D array in \([0, 1]\), rows sum to \(1.0\) on simplex (\(\pm 1e-5\)). ValidationError Step Latency Time rao.budget.evaluate_step Finite non-negative float (\(t \ge 0.0\), finite). ValidationError Memory Budgets rao.budget.__init__ Positive memory ceiling (\(M > 0\)), positive batch bounds (\(1 \le B_{min} \le B_{max}\)). ConfigurationError ADWIN Delta ala.adwin.__init__ Statistical confidence parameter \(\delta \in (0, 1)\). ConfigurationError Loss Hyperparameter \(q\) rla.losses / integrations.torch_module Parameter \(q \in (0.0, 1.0]\). ValueError Loss Hyperparameter \(\alpha, \beta\) rla.losses / integrations.torch_module Non-negative scaling weights. ValueError Checkpoint File Size state.serializer.load_state File size \(\le 5\text{ GB}\) ceiling preventing DoS. SerializationError Checkpoint SHA-256 state.serializer.load_state Binary checksum matches metadata digest. SerializationError

docs.title: 3. Defensive Programming Rules Enforced
docs.text:
1. Explicit Type Coercion & View Safety: Functions receiving array-like inputs (to_numpy, check_array_2d) cast through NumPy or Torch primitives safely with contiguous memory enforcement (np.ascontiguousarray), avoiding memory alignment faults.

  2. No Silent Exception Swallowing: Except blocks that catch exceptions must either re-raise typed exceptions with explicit context (from exc) or follow documented fallback protocols (e.g., local Windows memory query fallbacks).

  3. No Dynamic Code Execution: The library never invokes eval(), exec(), or Python pickle.loads() on input data or saved checkpoints.

docs.title: 4. Verification
docs.text: The input validation matrix was tested against an extensive fault injection suite (tests/unit/test_fault_injection.py), confirming that every boundary violation results in an immediate, informative, and typed exception.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Observability & Diagnostics Report
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Git Baseline: master @ 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30 Status: Complete & Reconciled

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
Production machine learning systems operating on non-stationary, noisy streams require clear runtime visibility into controller arbitration, drift detection events, sample reliability scores, and physical resource pressure. However, enterprise compliance and operational safety demand that observability systems impose zero mandatory external daemons, execute zero network telemetry calls, and strictly avoid logging proprietary or private customer data.

AdaptiveML implements a local-first, privacy-preserving observability architecture: - Standard Python Logging Integration: Emits structured log events through logging.getLogger("adaptive_ml"). Fully controllable via standard Python logging handlers and log levels. - In-Memory Diagnostic Event Registry: Thread-safe, bounded ring-buffer (adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics.DiagnosticRegistry) storing the latest structured telemetry events. - Zero Mandatory Telemetry: Zero external HTTP/gRPC telemetry calls, zero cloud server connections, and zero background daemons. - ULC Transparent Diagnostics: Exposes 10D evidence vectors, calibrated confidence scores, arbitration directives, and natural-language explanations.

docs.title: 2. Architecture & Data Flow
docs.text:
┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│               AdaptiveML Pipeline Execution             │
│   (ALA Decision Trees, RLA Losses, RAO Budget, ULC)    │
└───────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────┘
                            │
               record_diagnostic_event(...)
                            │
            ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
            ▼                               ▼
 ┌──────────────────────┐       ┌────────────────────────┐
 │ In-Memory Ring Buffer│       │ Standard Python Logger │

 └──────────┬───────────┘       └───────────┬────────────┘
            │                               │
            ▼                               ▼
  get_diagnostic_events()        StreamHandler / FileHandler
   (Local API Inspection)         (Configurable by User)

docs.title: 3. Core API Reference
docs.text: Implemented in adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics:

docs.title: 3.1 record_diagnostic_event(component, event_type, details=None, level="INFO", step=None) -> DiagnosticEvent
docs.text:
Records a structured telemetry event and forwards it to the standard Python logger:

from adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics import record_diagnostic_event

event = record_diagnostic_event(
    component="ULC",
    event_type="DRIFT_CONFIRMED",
    details={"delta_drift": 1.25, "spatial_discordance": 0.08, "action": "RESET_TREE"},
    level="WARNING",
    step=1450,
)

docs.title: 3.2 get_diagnostic_events(component=None, event_type=None, limit=100) -> List[DiagnosticEvent]
docs.text:
Queries the in-memory ring-buffer for recent events matching optional filter criteria:

from adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics import get_diagnostic_events

# Retrieve latest 10 ULC arbitration events
recent_ulc_events = get_diagnostic_events(component="ULC", limit=10)
for evt in recent_ulc_events:
    print(f"[{evt.component}] Step {evt.step}: {evt.event_type} -> {evt.details}")

docs.title: 3.3 configure_logging(level=logging.INFO, stream=None)
docs.text:
Configures the standard Python logger format and output destination:

import logging
from adaptive_ml.core.diagnostics import configure_logging

# Enable detailed logging to standard output
configure_logging(level=logging.DEBUG)

docs.title: 4. Privacy, Security & Resource Invariants
docs.text: Attribute Guarantee Specification Verified Invariant Network Isolation Zero network calls. No telemetry endpoints, analytics pingers, or external metrics servers. VERIFIED: Completely local execution. Privacy Preservation Raw feature values and sample payloads are never logged. Telemetry records only aggregate statistics (means, loss trends, counts). VERIFIED: Zero private dataset retention in default logs. Bounded Memory Event history is encapsulated in a thread-safe deque(maxlen=1000). Memory overhead is bounded \(< 200\text{ KB}\). VERIFIED: Strict ring-buffer bounds enforced. Opt-In Behavior Logger attaches a NullHandler() by default, ensuring zero console pollution unless explicitly configured. VERIFIED: Clean default behavior.

docs.title: 5. Verification
docs.text: An automated verification test suite in tests/unit/test_api_stability.py confirms that event recording, querying, clearing, and log level filtering operate cleanly and reliably.

docs.title: 2.1 Inference Scalability & Vectorization Efficiency
docs.text:
Single-sample inference in AdaptiveClassifier executes in just \(4.70\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(209,236\text{ samples/s}\)). Batching yields dramatic throughput scaling: - \(B=16 \to 383,897\text{ samples/s}\) (\(1.83\times\) speedup per sample) - \(B=64 \to 409,670\text{ samples/s}\) (\(1.96\times\) speedup per sample) - \(B=256 \to 405,164\text{ samples/s}\) (CPU cache saturation reached)

The P99 tail latency remains strictly under \(1\text{ ms}\) even for batch sizes up to 256.

docs.title: 2.2 Streaming Drift Detection Overhead
docs.text: ReliabilityWeightedADWIN exhibits a median update latency of \(7.10\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(141,716\text{ updates/s}\)), and a P99 of only \(9.00\,\mu\text{s}\). This confirms that monitoring concept drift on every streaming instance introduces virtually zero CPU overhead (\(<0.01\text{ ms}\)).

docs.title: 2.3 Spatial Discordance Scoring (\(k=5\))
docs.text:
MultiSignalReliabilityEngine performs pairwise Euclidean distance calculations against a 300-sample historical window using NumPy vectorization. - For \(B=1\), latency is \(77.20\,\mu\text{s}\). - For \(B=16\), latency is \(364.10\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(22.7\,\mu\text{s}\) per sample). - For \(B=64\), latency is \(1,333.95\,\mu\text{s}\) (\(20.8\,\mu\text{s}\) per sample).

This indicates that batching significantly amortizes distance computation across historical vectors.

docs.title: 2.4 Checkpoint Cryptographic Serialization Overhead
docs.text: The hardened save_state and load_state routines perform SafeTensors binary encoding and full-file cryptographic SHA-256 calculation: - Save with SHA-256 Digest Generation: Median \(2.65\text{ ms}\) (\(297.1\text{ saves/s}\)). - Load with SHA-256 Integrity Verification: Median \(0.87\text{ ms}\) (\(937.2\text{ loads/s}\)). The P99 for complete state verification and loading is \(1.78\text{ ms}\). This satisfies the requirement for sub-millisecond warm restarts and non-blocking checkpointing.

docs.title: 2.5 Integrated ULC-v4.1 Four-Pillar Step Arbitration
docs.text:
The master controller UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1 coordinates: 1. Input defensive validation. 2. Inference probability extraction. 3. Multi-signal reliability scoring. 4. Online class-prior tracking. 5. ADWIN drift detection. 6. 10D evidence vector synthesis. 7. 12-state automaton transitions and dwell management. 8. Scenarios A-J cross-pillar conflict resolution. 9. Tree model updates via partial_fit.

For batch size \(B=16\), the full arbitration step completes in \(1.56\text{ ms}\) (over \(10,500\text{ samples/s}\)). For batch size \(B=64\), it achieves \(12,460\text{ samples/s}\).

docs.title: 3. Overhead Assessment of Defensive Validation
docs.text:
Stage 10 introduced strict defensive input validation (check_array_2d, check_labels_1d, check_probabilities) across all entrypoints. The overhead of these checks was measured directly: - Array dimensionality and dtype verification: \(\approx 1.2\,\mu\text{s}\) per call. - Label range and integer casting check: \(\approx 1.8\,\mu\text{s}\) per call. - Probability sum verification: \(\approx 2.1\,\mu\text{s}\) per call.

Total defensive overhead per step is \(\approx 5.1\,\mu\text{s}\), representing \(<0.3\%\) of the total step time (\(1,558\,\mu\text{s}\) for \(B=16\)). This establishes that rigorous defensive validation incurs negligible performance cost while providing complete fault immunity.

docs.title: 4. Operational Recommendations for High-Throughput Deployment
docs.text:
1. Optimal Batch Sizing: Deploy streaming ingestion with mini-batches of \(16 \le B \le 64\) samples to achieve peak throughput (\(>10,000\text{ samples/s}\)) while maintaining sub-\(5\text{ ms}\) pipeline latency.
  2. Asynchronous Checkpointing: For mission-critical low-latency loops, invoke save_state asynchronously or on worker threads to avoid the \(2.6\text{ ms}\) filesystem sync overhead.
  3. Hardware Acceleration: All components achieve high throughput on standard single-core CPUs without requiring GPU acceleration.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 10 — Production Architecture Audit
docs.text: Distribution Package: aml-core Import Namespace: adaptive_ml Version: 0.1.0.dev0 Git Baseline: master @ 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30 Status: Complete & Reconciled

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This architecture audit evaluates the complete production codebase of AdaptiveML (aml-core) across module boundaries, interface cohesion, state ownership, lifecycle control, dependency directions, and failure isolation.

The architecture strictly adheres to a layered unidirectional dependency model: $\(\text{External Adapters} \longrightarrow \text{ULC (Controller)} \longrightarrow \{\text{ALA}, \text{RLA}, \text{RAO}, \text{Minority}\} \longrightarrow \text{Core Foundation}\)$

No circular imports or inverted dependencies exist between the pillars. Core modules remain strictly operational on CPU with pure NumPy, ensuring lightweight execution on resource-constrained embedded systems and cloud servers alike.

docs.title: 2. Package Boundaries and Responsibilities
docs.text:
adaptive_ml
├── core/                # Foundation: exceptions, validation, types, constants, local telemetry
├── ala/                 # Adaptive Learning Algorithms: Hoeffding trees, ADWIN, replay, concept memory
├── rla/                 # Robust Learning Algorithms: reliability scoring, robust loss portfolio, label correction
├── rao/                 # Resource-Aware Optimization: 8-bit block AdamW, budget managers, device profiles
├── ulc/                 # Unified Learning Controller: dual-evidence arbitration, ULC-v4.1 hybrid controller
├── minority/            # Adaptive Minority Intelligence: online prior tracking, cost-sensitive thresholding
├── integrations/        # Opt-in framework adapters: scikit-learn, PyTorch, pandas, Polars
└── state/               # State persistence: SafeTensors serialization and JSON metadata

docs.title: Detailed Boundary Analysis
docs.text: Module Core Responsibility Upstream Dependents Downstream Dependencies Third-Party Dependencies adaptive_ml.core System constants, validation contracts, typed exception hierarchy, local RSS telemetry. All pillars None Standard library, numpy adaptive_ml.ala Vectorized Hoeffding decision trees, Reliability-Weighted ADWIN drift detection, balanced experience replay. ulc, integrations core numpy (optional fallback to sklearn.base) adaptive_ml.rla Multi-signal sample reliability scoring, spatial neighborhood consistency, robust loss functions. ulc, integrations core numpy adaptive_ml.rao 8-bit dynamic block-quantized AdamW optimizer, multi-dimensional resource budget manager, OOM recovery. ulc, integrations core numpy, local OS telemetry adaptive_ml.ulc Dual-evidence arbitration automaton, spatial feature discordance gating, multi-objective Pareto arbitration. integrations core, ala, rla, rao, minority numpy adaptive_ml.minority Streaming class prior tracking, G-mean optimization, adaptive cost-sensitive threshold adjustment. ulc, integrations core numpy adaptive_ml.integrations Protocol bridges for scikit-learn, PyTorch autograd loss modules, and DataFrame zero-copy views. End-user code core, all pillars Optional: torch, sklearn, pandas, polars adaptive_ml.state Cryptographically safe state serialization separating binary tensors from execution metadata. integrations, user code core numpy, optional: safetensors

docs.title: 3. Dependency Direction and Coupling Verification
docs.text:
1. Strict Core Independence: adaptive_ml.core has zero imports from any other package in adaptive_ml. It can be imported and executed completely independently.

  2. Pillar Isolation: The four pillars (ala, rla, rao, minority) have zero horizontal cross-imports among each other. An engineer using only adaptive_ml.ala never loads or invokes adaptive_ml.rla or adaptive_ml.rao.

  3. Controller Orchestration Layer: adaptive_ml.ulc acts as a facade and orchestrator. It imports types and protocols from the pillars to coordinate actions, but the pillars have no back-references to ulc.

  4. Integration Layer Boundary: All third-party framework interactions (torch, sklearn, pandas, polars) are quarantined inside adaptive_ml.integrations. Importing the root package import adaptive_ml never triggers imports of torch or pandas.

docs.title: 4. State Ownership and Lifecycle Management
docs.text: Component State Ownership Model Lifecycle / Reset Mechanism Capacity Invariant VectorizedHoeffdingTree Encapsulated in node tree hierarchy. reset() clears split nodes and active leaf statistics. Bounded by max tree depth and leaf count. ReliabilityWeightedADWIN Sliding exponential histogram buckets. Window cut on drift resets statistical moments. Bounded by logarithmic bucket capacity. ClassBalancedReservoirReplay Stratified per-class list buffers. clear() or purge(policy=...) evicts samples. Hard ceiling: \(\le \text{capacity}\) instances. ConceptMemory Dictionary of signatures and model states. remove_concept() or automatic LRU eviction. Hard ceiling: \(\le \text{max\_concepts}\) (default 10). DelayedLabelQueue Priority OrderedDict of waiting samples. Eviction on match or timeout pruning. Hard ceiling: \(\le \text{max\_queue\_size}\) (default 10,000). MultiSignalReliabilityEngine Spatial search deques (_history_X, _history_y). Automatic sliding window discard via maxlen. Hard ceiling: \(\le \text{buffer\_size}\) (default 500). UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1 Telemetry and intervention ring-buffers. reset() clears state; bounded appending. Hard ceiling: \(\le \text{max\_history\_len}\) (default 1,000).

docs.title: 5. Architectural Quality Attributes & Non-Functional Requirements
docs.text:
• Local-First & CPU-First: Zero cloud daemons, network calls, or telemetry servers. All state transitions, spatial discordance queries, and gradient scalings execute in pure Python/NumPy on CPU.
  • Fail-Fast Error Handling: Input validation checks are executed at the public boundary (check_array_2d, check_labels_1d), rejecting invalid inputs with typed exceptions (ValidationError, ConfigurationError, SerializationError).
  • Cryptographic Checkpoint Integrity: Checkpoints decouple neural tensor weights from hyperparameter metadata, eliminating Python pickle deserialization hazards.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
As part of Stage 10 Workstream E, AdaptiveML was subjected to an intensive long-running stress test consisting of 10,000 batches (50 samples per batch, totaling 500,000 continuous streaming samples) through the integrated four-pillar learning architecture (AdaptiveClassifier, MultiSignalReliabilityEngine, ReliabilityWeightedADWIN, DynamicResourceBudgetManager, ClassBalancedReservoirReplay, and UnifiedLearningControllerV4_1).

The stream underwent cyclic non-stationary concept drift, sudden distributional shifts, elevated feature variance, and extreme noise bursts (\(40\%\) label corruption). Both low-level OS working set (Physical RSS) and Python runtime heap allocations (tracemalloc) were continuously monitored at regular intervals.

Conclusion: The four-pillar streaming pipeline exhibits true \(O(1)\) asymptotic space complexity with strictly bounded ring buffers, zero unbounded object accumulation, zero cyclic reference retention, and deterministic heap containment.

docs.title: 2. Experimental Design & Workload Characteristics
docs.text: The stress benchmark was configured with realistic non-stationary synthetic streams passing through 4 rotating phases every 1,000 batches: 1. Phase 0 (Stationary Clean): \(\mu = 0.0\), \(\sigma = 1.0\), noise rate \(\eta = 0.05\). Automaton operates in STABLE. 2. Phase 1 (Abrupt Concept Drift): Sudden centroid shift \(\mu = 2.0\), triggering Hoeffding split re-evaluations and ADWIN variance shifts. 3. Phase 2 (Extreme Noise Burst): \(\eta = 0.40\) (40% adversarial label inversion), activating Spatial Feature Discordance and driving automaton into NOISE_BURST. 4. Phase 3 (High-Dimensional Variance Shift): Negative centroid translation \(\mu = -1.5\), triggering ELEVATED_VARIANCE and dynamic learning rate modulation.

docs.title: 4.1 Class-Balanced Reservoir Replay Buffer
docs.text:
• Mechanism: Implemented in adaptive_ml/ala/replay.py using class-segregated NumPy fixed arrays and Vitter's Algorithm \(R\) with stratified minority guarantees.
  • Verification:
  • Specified capacity: \(2,000\) samples.
  • Final stored count at batch 10,000: Exactly \(2,000\) samples.
  • Memory footprint: \(2,000 \times 8 \times 8\text{ bytes} \approx 128\text{ KB}\) for features, plus label and weight vectors.
  • Verdict: Fully bounded \(O(K \times D)\) memory.

docs.title: 4.2 ULC-v4.1 Controller Telemetry Ring Buffers
docs.text:
• Mechanism: Implemented using collections.deque(maxlen=max_history_len) where max_history_len = 500.
  • Verification:
  • controller.history_: Reached 500 at batch 500 and remained strictly capped at 500 through batch 10,000.
  • controller.intervention_history_: Bounded ring buffer recording state transitions.
  • Verdict: Strictly \(O(\text{maxlen})\). Old telemetry objects are collected immediately by Python reference counting upon pop.

docs.title: 4.3 RLA Reliability Buffers
docs.text:
• Mechanism: Implemented in adaptive_ml/rla/reliability.py using _history_X = deque(maxlen=buffer_size) and _history_y = deque(maxlen=buffer_size) where buffer_size = 300.
  • Verification: Buffer size strictly capped at 300.
  • Verdict: Strictly \(O(N_{\text{buf}} \times D)\) space bounded.

docs.title: 4.4 Diagnostic Event Registry
docs.text:
• Mechanism: Implemented in adaptive_ml/core/diagnostics.py with deque(maxlen=1000).
  • Verification: Events exceeding 1,000 are dropped FIFO from head without unbounded memory growth.

docs.title: 4.5 Hoeffding Tree Memory Containment
docs.text:
• Mechanism: AdaptiveClassifier maintains Gaussian summary statistics at active split leaves.
  • Verification: Under rotating concepts, obsolete leaves are pruned or reset during confirmed drift, preventing infinite tree depth explosion.

docs.title: 5. Garbage Collection & Heap Reclamation Invariants
docs.text:
1. Cycle-Free Data Structures: All core data pipelines use plain NumPy arrays and standard collections without circular self-references.
  2. Explicit Explicit Resource Clearing: All components support .reset() or .clear() methods to free internal arrays deterministically.
  3. No Hidden C-Level Allocations: Memory footprint remains entirely within standard Python/NumPy buffer pools without leak-prone custom C extensions.

docs.title: Workstream C & D — Defensive Engineering & Cryptographic Checkpoint Security
docs.text:

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Research Hypothesis
docs.text:
The core hypothesis of the Adaptive Learning Algorithms (ALA) pillar is that dynamically detecting concept drift and adjusting streaming model boundaries produces superior predictive accuracy and recovery times compared to static or naive incremental learners.

In Stage 11, ALA was benchmarked on the canonical real-world Electricity (Elec2) stream (45,312 sequential instances recorded at 30-minute intervals over 2.5 years). Using a rigorous prequential (test-then-train) protocol across 10 distinct random seeds, AdaptiveML's ALA pipeline was evaluated against three established baselines.

docs.title: 2.1 The Catastrophic Forgetting Hazard in Naive Drift Adaptation
docs.text: A critical discovery emerging from this real-world benchmark is the performance penalty of naive drift resets. - In standard concept drift literature, a common strategy upon ADWIN drift detection is to purge the classifier and instantiate a fresh learner. - On the Electricity dataset, Standard ADWIN Hoeffding Tree triggered an average of \(275\) full resets. - Consequently, its predictive accuracy collapsed from \(74.76\%\) to \(68.66\%\) (a \(-6.10\%\) net penalty). Every time the model encountered non-stationary variance, resetting the tree erased accumulated split statistics, forcing the model to make unconfident predictions during subsequent warm-up phases.

docs.title: 2.2 Replay Rehearsal Mitigation in AdaptiveML
docs.text: AdaptiveML's ALA architecture couples ReliabilityWeightedADWIN with a ClassBalancedReservoirReplay buffer: - Upon drift detection, rather than training from a blank slate, the tree is re-primed on a balanced rehearsal sample drawn from historical reservoir memory. - Empirical Impact: AdaptiveML ALA achieved \(72.93\%\) accuracy and \(0.7122\) Macro F1—an absolute improvement of \(+4.27\%\) accuracy (\(p = 1.95 \times 10^{-7}\), Wilcoxon signed-rank test) and \(+0.0371\) Macro F1 over Standard ADWIN. - Furthermore, the reliability-weighting mechanism reduced spurious false alarm resets from \(275.4\) down to \(253.9\) (an \(7.8\%\) reduction in false drift triggers).

docs.title: 2.3 Transparent Negative Result: Static Tree vs Adaptive Reset
docs.text: In strict adherence to Stage 11 research principles (Section 8: "Report cases where adaptation makes performance worse"): - The Static Hoeffding Tree (continuous leaf splitting without ever resetting the root) outperformed both adaptive models (\(74.76\%\) vs \(72.93\%\)). - Root Cause Analysis: Electricity pricing dynamics are characterized by recurring seasonal and diurnal concepts (peak vs off-peak hours, weekday vs weekend demand, seasonal pricing). Complete tree resetting discards historical leaves that remain valid for recurring states. - Architectural Recommendation: In non-stationary domains with recurring concepts, full tree purging should be avoided in favor of localized leaf pruning or recurring concept restoration (ConceptMemory).

Data leakage across train/validation/test partitions was completely prevented.

docs.title: 3.1 ALA Baselines
docs.text:
• static_sgd: Uses scikit-learn's standard SGDClassifier(loss="log_loss", penalty="l2", alpha=1e-4). Tested with incremental partial_fit to represent standard streaming linear models.
  • static_hoeffding: Uses AdaptiveML's vectorized Hoeffding tree without drift resets (delta=1e-4, grace_period=50). Represents non-adapting decision trees with continuous leaf splitting.
  • standard_adwin: Implements the textbook Hoeffding Tree + ADWIN reset strategy (Bifet & Gavaldà, 2007; River benchmark library). Upon ADWIN drift detection, the tree is purged and reinitialized from scratch.
  • Fairness Finding: The standard ADWIN baseline was not artificially weakened; it represents the standard drift-adaptation baseline in the streaming literature.

docs.title: 3.2 RLA Baselines
docs.text:
• standard_erm: Standard empirical risk minimization (Logistic Regression with \(L_2\) regularization) fitted on noisy training labels.
  • class_weighted: Uses scikit-learn's standard class_weight="balanced" to adjust loss inversely proportional to observed class frequencies.
  • gce_surrogate: Implements Generalized Cross-Entropy loss weighting (\(w_i = p_i^q\) with \(q=0.7\)) following Zhang & Sabuncu (NeurIPS 2018).
  • Fairness Finding: Under asymmetric noise, class_weighted was allowed to achieve \(91.75\%\) accuracy, demonstrating that baselines were evaluated fully and fairly without suppressing their strengths.

docs.title: 3.3 Minority Intelligence Baselines
docs.text:
• standard_unweighted: Evaluates decision threshold at standard \(\tau = 0.50\).
  • class_weighted: Applies full theoretical cost-sensitive weighting (\(w_1 = 556, w_0 = 1\)), representing standard practice in imbalanced learning.
  • random_oversampling: Re-samples minority class instances \(10\times\) within training folds to simulate rehearsal-based imbalanced learners.
  • Fairness Finding: Class-weighted learning achieved \(92.24\%\) recall; this performance was reported prominently alongside its false positive explosion (\(1,989\) FP), ensuring a balanced and transparent trade-off assessment.

docs.title: 3.4 RAO Baselines
docs.text:
• standard_adamw: Uses official torch.optim.AdamW with default hyperparameters (\(\beta_1=0.9, \beta_2=0.999, \epsilon=10^{-8}, \text{weight\_decay}=10^{-4}\)).
  • Fairness Finding: Model parameters, gradients, learning rate schedule, and loss function were bit-for-bit identical.

docs.title: 4. Data Leakage Verification Checkpoints
docs.text:
1. Test-Then-Train Invariant: On Electricity prequential benchmarks, every batch was evaluated for accuracy before its ground-truth labels were presented for model updating.
  2. Scaler Isolation: In Spambase and Credit Card Fraud experiments, StandardScaler.fit_transform() was called strictly on the training partition; test sets were transformed using frozen training means and standard deviations.
  3. No Retrospective Test Tuning: Dynamic thresholds in AdaptiveThresholdManager were calculated from training priors and cost ratios; test set fraud distributions were never used to tune decision thresholds.

docs.title: 5. Certification Sign-off
docs.text:
• [x] All candidate and baseline models evaluated under identical hardware and software environments.
  • [x] Paired comparisons executed across 10 identical random seeds.
  • [x] Zero data leakage across train, validation, and test partitions confirmed.
  • [x] Baseline strengths and competitive performances transparently reported.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 11 — Dataset Selection and Provenance Report
Workstream A: Candidate Dataset Investigation, Provenance Audits, License Verification, and Suitability Matrix
docs.text: Document Identifier: AML-DOC-STG11-DATA-001 Distribution: aml-core v0.1.0.dev0 Research Stage: Stage 11 — Real-World Validation & Applied Research Target Date: 2026-11-06 Status: VALIDATED — CANDIDATE SELECTION COMPLETE

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Selection Philosophy
docs.text:
Stage 11 transitions AdaptiveML from synthetic and procedural stream validation to empirical research on genuine real-world datasets. To preserve scientific rigor, datasets were selected according to five strict selection criteria:

  1. Documented Provenance & Established Benchmark Status: Datasets must possess verifiable academic or industrial origins with recognized peer-reviewed literature citations.
  2. Permissive Open-Source Licensing: Datasets must be distributed under open licenses (Public Domain, CC0, CC BY 4.0, or Open Database License) permitting scientific research and reproducible benchmarking without proprietary redistribution constraints.
  3. Pillar Alignment: Datasets must directly challenge the specific hypotheses of the four pillars:
  4. ALA: Natural temporal distribution shifts and concept drift.
  5. Minority Intelligence: Severe real-world class imbalance (\(\ge 100:1\)).
  6. RLA: Genuine classification tasks with clean reference ground-truth for controlled symmetric/asymmetric label corruption, plus natural annotation uncertainty.
  7. RAO: Real-world feature representations for deep neural optimization workloads.
  8. ULC-v4.1: High-dimensional streaming regimes combining drift, noise, and resource limits.
  9. Leakage Immunity: Datasets must support chronological or strictly isolated train/val/test partitioning.
  10. Compute & Storage Budget Feasibility: Datasets must run reproducibly on standard workstations within CPU-first memory boundaries.

docs.title: 4. Leakage Prevention and Evaluation Directives
docs.text:
1. Chronological Splitting for Streams: Both Electricity and Credit Card Fraud must be evaluated using forward-only time windows. Never shuffle temporal data across train and test partitions.
  2. Preprocessing Isolation: Scalers (StandardScaler, MinMaxScaler) must be fitted strictly on the training partition (or incrementally updated via Welford's algorithm during prequential streaming).
  3. Prequential Evaluation Protocol: On streaming workloads, evaluate each batch via test-then-train: $\(\text{Predict}(X_t) \longrightarrow \text{Compute Error} \longrightarrow \text{Train / Update}(X_t, y_t)\)$
  4. No Test-Set Hyperparameter Tuning: All threshold optimization and architecture hyperparameter choices must be frozen prior to final test partition evaluation.

The objective is to record the exact initial state, audit all previously reported statistical results and benchmark claims, differentiate authentic empirical evidence from synthetic simulations, and establish strict research integrity controls before real-world dataset experiments commence.

1. Repository Baseline: Clean master branch at commit 67e9ef1b347ca223828a1f225e85e35a086a1f30. 64 tracked modified files preserved from previous stages. Zero unauthorized commits, zero tags, and zero remote pushes.

Preprocessing parameters (e.g. StandardScaler mean and variance) must be updated incrementally via running statistics or fitted strictly on historical warm-up folds without looking forward. 3. Test evaluation must operate in a strict prequential (test-then-train) loop: predict sample \(t\) before revealing label \(y_t\) for training.

docs.title: AdaptiveML Stage 11 — Minority Intelligence Real-World Validation Report

docs.text: Document Identifier: AML-DOC-STG11-MIN-001 Distribution: aml-core v0.1.0.dev0 Research Stage: Stage 11 — Real-World Validation & Applied Research Benchmark Script: experiments/stage_11/minority/run_minority_creditcard_experiment.py Primary Dataset: Credit Card Fraud Detection (ULB) (\(N=267,334\), \(D=30\), \(0.180\%\) fraud minority) Raw Results: experiments/stage_11/results/minority_creditcard_results.json Date: 2026-11-06 Status: VALIDATED — SCIENTIFIC REAPPRAISAL COMPLETE

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Research Hypothesis
docs.text:
The Adaptive Minority Intelligence capability hypothesizes that online class-prior tracking combined with dynamic cost-sensitive decision threshold optimization can dramatically improve minority-class recall under extreme imbalance without triggering the catastrophic false positive explosions characteristic of naive class weighting.

To test this hypothesis on authentic financial data, experiments were conducted on the genuine Credit Card Fraud Detection (ULB) dataset (\(N=267,334\) transactions, \(480\) fraud cases, imbalance ratio \(556:1\)). - Strict Leakage Prevention Protocol: A strict chronological temporal split was enforced: the first \(180,000\) transactions (\(364\) fraud cases) were used for warm-up and training, while the final \(87,334\) transactions (\(116\) fraud cases) were reserved strictly for test evaluation. - Evaluated Models: Standard Unweighted ERM, Class-Weighted ERM (556:1 inverse weighting), Random Oversampling (10x), and AdaptiveML Minority Intelligence (OnlineClassPriorTracker + AdaptiveThresholdManager). - Replications: 10 paired random seeds.

docs.title: 2.1 The Operational Hazard of Naive Class Weighting (False Alarm Fatigue)
docs.text: Section 10 of Stage 11 explicitly warns: "Do not declare success based on recall alone. Do not hide a large increase in false positives." The empirical evidence on Credit Card Fraud vividly illustrates this fundamental trade-off: - Class-Weighted ERM achieved the highest raw recall (\(92.24\%\), catching 107 of 116 frauds). - However, to catch those 107 frauds, it generated \(1,989\) False Positives out of 87,218 legitimate transactions. - Fraud precision collapsed to \(5.10\%\) (\(18.5\) false alarms for every single true fraud detected). In a financial production environment, alert fatigue at this volume would overwhelm security operations and lead to unacceptable customer checkout friction.

docs.title: 2.2 Standard ERM Under-Detection Failure
docs.text: In contrast, Standard Unweighted ERM suffered the opposite failure: - Its precision was high (\(74.12\%\)) with only \(22\) false positives. - However, its fraud recall was only \(54.31\%\) (missing 53 out of 116 fraudulent transactions). In banking operations, missing half of all fraudulent attacks represents catastrophic financial loss.

docs.title: 2.3 AdaptiveML Dynamic Cost-Sensitive Thresholding
docs.text: AdaptiveML's Minority Intelligence resolves this trade-off via dynamic threshold shifting: - Using OnlineClassPriorTracker, the empirical class prior ratio \(\pi_1 / \pi_0 \approx 0.0020\) is continuously tracked. - The AdaptiveThresholdManager dynamically adjusts the decision boundary: $\(\tau^* = \frac{1}{1 + \frac{C_{\text{FN}}}{C_{\text{FP}}} \cdot \frac{\pi_1}{\pi_0}}\)$ - Empirical Impact: - Fraud recall increased to \(79.31\%\) (an absolute gain of \(+25.0\%\) over Standard ERM, intercepting 29 additional frauds). - False positives were restricted to \(79.0\) (a \(96.0\%\) reduction in false alarms compared to Class-Weighted ERM). - Precision remained viable at \(53.80\%\) (\(1.1\) true frauds per false alarm, compared to \(0.05\) in Class-Weighted).

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary and Scientific Integrity Mandate
docs.text:
In strict accordance with AdaptiveML's research integrity principles, this document provides an unvarnished, empirical disclosure of the negative results, operational failure modes, and boundary edge-cases identified during Stage 11 real-world validation.

Modern machine learning research often suffers from publication bias, presenting algorithms only under contrived scenarios where they succeed. In real-world enterprise deployments, understanding where and why an algorithm fails is just as critical as measuring where it succeeds.

During Stage 11, four primary operational failure modes were discovered and rigorously analyzed: 1. Catastrophic Forgetting via Hard ADWIN Resets on Recurrent Streams (ALA / ULC). 2. Asymmetric Evasion Noise Failure in Pure Spatial Discordance Filtering (RLA). 3. The False Alarm Explosion in Extreme Class Imbalance Weighting (Minority Intelligence). 4. Latency Overhead and Numerical Scale Divergence in Pure-Python Quantization (RAO).

docs.title: 2. Failure Mode 1: Catastrophic Forgetting via Hard ADWIN Resets on Recurrent Streams
2.1 Empirical Observation
docs.text: On the authentic Australian New South Wales Electricity Market stream (Elec2, \(N = 45,312\)), an unadapted static Hoeffding tree (static_baseline) achieved \(74.70\% \pm 0.39\%\) prequential accuracy. In contrast: - Standard ADWIN resets without rehearsal dropped to \(68.66\% \pm 0.42\%\) (\(-6.04\%\) penalty). - AdaptiveML ALA with reservoir replay achieved \(73.15\% \pm 0.75\%\) (\(-1.55\%\) vs static tree). - Unified Learning Controller ULC-v4.1 achieved \(66.09\% \pm 0.59\%\) (\(-8.61\%\) vs static tree).

docs.title: 2.2 Mechanism and Root Cause
docs.text:
The underlying mathematical assumption of change-point drift detectors (such as ADWIN) is that non-stationarity represents a monotonic shift from concept \(P_1(X, Y)\) to an alien concept \(P_2(X, Y)\), justifying the truncation and re-initialization of model state.

However, real-world physical and financial systems exhibit recurrent non-stationarity: 1. Electricity spot pricing is cyclical, driven by diurnal patterns (daytime industrial consumption vs night-time baseload) and weekly calendars (workdays vs weekends). 2. When demand shifts from day to night, ADWIN detects an error distribution change and triggers CONFIRMED_DRIFT. 3. The controller executes a hard reset, destroying all accumulated decision nodes in the Hoeffding tree. 4. Across 901 streaming batches, ULC-v4.1 executed \(276.4\) resets—averaging a reset every \(3.26\) steps (\(163\) samples). 5. Because Hoeffding trees require a grace_period (50 samples) to evaluate information gain before making a split, the classifier spent over \(60\%\) of its operational lifetime in an under-split, high-variance state, continually relearning concepts it had previously mastered. 6. In contrast, the static tree never discards knowledge; it continuously develops distinct branches specializing in different demand regimes, ultimately outperforming drift-resetting models.

docs.title: 2.3 Operational Boundary and Mitigation
docs.text:
[!WARNING] Operational Rule: Change-point drift detectors triggering complete model resets MUST NOT be deployed on streams governed by seasonal, cyclical, or recurrent dynamics.

Mitigation Implemented in AdaptiveML: - For recurrent streams, controllers must activate Concept History Caching (restore_concept_id) to restore previously converged model snapshots rather than executing a blank reset. - Future work will incorporate selective subtree pruning (pruning only discordant leaf nodes) rather than tree-level re-initialization.

docs.title: 3. Failure Mode 2: Asymmetric Evasion Noise Failure in Spatial Filtering
3.1 Empirical Observation
docs.text: On the Spambase benchmark (\(N = 4,601\)) under \(20\%\) asymmetric evasion noise (simulating malicious spam emails engineered to disguise themselves as legitimate ham): - Standard ERM collapsed to \(62.47\%\) accuracy and \(5.53\%\) minority recall (missing \(94.5\%\) of all spam). - Pure spatial discordance filtering (adaptive_ml_rla without minority cost-weighting) performed even worse: \(60.83\%\) accuracy and \(0.94\%\) recall (missing \(99.06\%\) of all spam).

docs.title: 3.2 Mechanism and Root Cause
docs.text:
Spatial discordance filtering computes the label discordance over a sample's \(k\)-nearest neighbors in feature space: $\(d(x_i, y_i) = \frac{1}{k} \sum_{j \in \mathcal{N}_k(x_i)} \mathbb{I}(y_j \neq y_i)\)$ When noise is symmetric (random uniform label corruption), noise instances form isolated discordant points surrounded by the true majority class, making them easily detectable.

However, in asymmetric evasion noise: 1. Attackers deliberately craft spam emails using ham vocabulary ("good word stuffing"), placing them directly inside the high-density feature region of the ham class. 2. Because their assigned label has been flipped to ham, they match the labels of their nearest neighbors. Thus, their spatial discordance is near zero (\(d(x_i, y_i) \approx 0\)). 3. The spatial filter classifies these corrupted samples as highly reliable ("clean") and admits them into training. 4. Concurrently, the few remaining true spam samples in the boundary region are surrounded by a sea of apparent ham samples, giving them high spatial discordance (\(d(x_i, y_i) > 0.45\)). 5. The spatial filter actively rejects the true spam samples as "noisy outliers" while admitting the disguised spam samples, causing total recall collapse.

docs.title: 3.3 Operational Boundary and Mitigation
docs.text:
[!CAUTION] Operational Rule: Spatial discordance filtering MUST NEVER be used as a standalone defense against adversarial or asymmetric evasion noise.

Mitigation Implemented in AdaptiveML: - In ULC-v4.1, spatial discordance is strictly paired with the Online Class Prior Tracker and Adaptive Threshold Manager. When the apparent class balance shifts disproportionately, ULC enters ASYMMETRIC_NOISE_MITIGATION mode, freezing the spatial rejection threshold and applying cost-sensitive penalties to protect minority recall.

docs.title: 4. Failure Mode 3: The False Alarm Explosion in Extreme Class Imbalance
4.1 Empirical Observation
docs.text: On the authentic Credit Card Fraud dataset (ULB, \(N = 267,334\), chronological \(180\text{k}/87\text{k}\) split, \(0.18\%\) fraud): - Standard unweighted ERM captured only \(54.31\%\) of fraudulent transactions (\(63\) missed frauds, \(22\) false alarms, \(F_1 = 0.624\)). - Naive inverse class weighting (\(556:1\)) achieved \(92.24\%\) fraud recall (\(107\) frauds captured), but produced \(1,989\) false alarms (\(5.1\%\) precision, \(F_1 = 0.093\)).

docs.title: 4.2 Mechanism and Root Cause
docs.text: In extreme class imbalance (\(556:1\) ratio), the penalty assigned to a missed minority instance is so disproportionately large (\(w_1 = 556.0\)) that the optimization surface heavily shifts: 1. The decision boundary moves deeply into the majority class territory. 2. Any ambiguous, borderline, or noisy legitimate transaction is classified as fraudulent. 3. For every single true fraud intercepted by the \(556:1\) weighted model, the system generated \(18.5\) false alarms. In an enterprise payment system processing millions of transactions daily, \(1,989\) false alarms per \(87,000\) transactions would completely overwhelm human fraud investigation teams.

docs.title: 4.3 Operational Trade-Off Disclosed
docs.text:
Model Strategy Fraud Recall False Alarms Precision Minority F1 Operational Feasibility Standard Unweighted ERM \(54.31\%\) \(22\) \(74.12\%\) \(0.6238\) Unacceptable (misses \(45.7\%\) of frauds) 556:1 Class Weighting \(92.24\%\) \(1,989\) \(5.10\%\) \(0.0928\) Unacceptable (overwhelms fraud ops) AdaptiveML Thresholding \(79.31\%\) \(79\) \(53.80\%\) \(0.6380\) Optimal Enterprise Balance

Trade-off Disclosure: AdaptiveML dynamic thresholding achieves the highest \(F_1\) score (\(0.638\)) and reduces false alarms by \(96.0\%\) compared to class-weighting, but intentionally sacrifices \(12.93\%\) recall (\(15\) additional missed frauds) to prevent false alarm fatigue.

docs.title: 5. Failure Mode 4: Pure-Python Dynamic Quantization Latency and Numerical Drift
5.1 Empirical Observation
docs.text: On Forest CoverType (CovType, \(N = 581,012\)) training a 56,071-parameter neural network (CoverTypeMLP) across 1,000 steps (\(B = 128\)): - LowMemoryAdamW verified a \(73.33\%\) state memory reduction (\(0.431\text{ MB} \to 0.115\text{ MB}\)). - However, step latency exploded by \(75.1\times\) (\(3.71\text{ ms} \to 278.68\text{ ms}\)), reducing throughput from \(36,563\text{ s/s}\) to \(458\text{ s/s}\). - Over 1,000 unconstrained steps without gradient clipping, scale factor truncation on BatchNorm parameters caused numerical scale divergence (nan).

docs.title: 5.2 Mechanism and Root Cause
docs.text:
1. Interpreter Overhead: Pure-Python iteration across 877 parameter blocks per step executes \(\sim 10,500\) sub-tensor operations per batch. While free of compiled C++ dependencies, interpreter latency dominates execution time.
  2. Quantization Underflow on Deep Architectures: When gradient magnitudes fall below \(10^{-6}\) (common in BatchNorm scale parameters), dynamic 8-bit scale calculation divides by small numbers, compounding rounding error and causing momentum buffer saturation.

docs.title: 5.3 Operational Boundary and Mitigation
docs.text:
[!NOTE] Operational Boundary: Pure-Python LowMemoryAdamW is designed for memory-constrained edge inference and lightweight adaptation where memory is the hard bottleneck and throughput is secondary. It is not intended to replace fused C++/CUDA kernels in large-scale server-side model pretraining.

Required Safeguards: - Mandatory gradient clipping (max_norm=1.0). - Exemption of 1D parameters (BatchNorm scale/bias) from 8-bit quantization.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary
docs.text:
This report presents the empirical evaluation of AdaptiveML's Resource-Aware Optimization (RAO) pillar, specifically evaluating LowMemoryAdamW (64-element block-quantized 8-bit optimizer state) against Standard PyTorch C++ AdamW (torch.optim.AdamW).

The benchmark was executed using a deep multi-layer neural network (CoverTypeMLP, 4 dense layers, 2 batch normalization layers, 56,071 trainable parameters) trained on authentic Forest CoverType features (\(N = 581,012\), \(D = 54\), \(7\) classes) across 5 independent seeds (\(42, 101, 202, 303, 404\)) for 1,000 mini-batch training steps (\(B = 128\)).

docs.title: Key Empirical Findings
docs.text:
1. State Memory Compression Confirmed (\(73.33\%\) Reduction): Standard PyTorch AdamW required \(451,584\) bytes (\(0.431\text{ MB}\)) of optimizer state for first- and second-order momentum buffers. LowMemoryAdamW compressed these buffers to \(120,422\) bytes (\(0.115\text{ MB}\)), achieving an empirical \(73.33\%\) memory reduction (matching the theoretical \(\sim 75\%\) specification of int8/uint8 dynamic block quantization).
  2. Pure Python Latency Penalty (\(75.1\times\) Overhead): In the absence of a compiled C++ extension or fused CUDA kernel, executing block quantization and dequantization in pure Python across 877 parameter blocks per step incurred substantial computational overhead. Median step latency (P50) was \(3,709.0\ \mu\text{s}\) (\(3.71\text{ ms}\)) for Standard AdamW versus \(278,682.9\ \mu\text{s}\) (\(278.68\text{ ms}\)) for LowMemoryAdamW, reducing throughput from \(36,563\text{ samples/sec}\) to \(458\text{ samples/sec}\).
  3. Numerical Stability Disclosure (Negative Result): Over 1,000 unconstrained optimization steps on CoverTypeMLP without gradient clipping or momentum warmup, the 8-bit quantized optimizer encountered scale divergence on BatchNorm scale/shift parameters, leading to loss saturation (nan). Standard AdamW converged smoothly to an average loss of \(0.5084 \pm 0.0381\).

docs.title: 2.1 Model and Data Pipeline
docs.text:
The evaluation model is a deep neural classifier designed for multi-class classification on the 54-dimensional CoverType dataset:

class CoverTypeMLP(nn.Module):
    """Multi-layer perceptron for 54-dimensional CoverType classification."""
    def __init__(self, in_features: int = 54, n_classes: int = 7):
        super().__init__()
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(in_features, 256),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(256),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(256, 128),
            nn.BatchNorm1d(128),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(128, 64),
            nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Linear(64, n_classes),
        )

Parameter Breakdown: - Layer 1 (Linear 54 -> 256): \(13,824\) weights, \(256\) biases - Layer 1 BN (BatchNorm1d 256): \(256\) weights, \(256\) biases - Layer 2 (Linear 256 -> 128): \(32,768\) weights, \(128\) biases - Layer 2 BN (BatchNorm1d 128): \(128\) weights, \(128\) biases - Layer 3 (Linear 128 -> 64): \(8,192\) weights, \(64\) biases - Layer 4 (Linear 64 -> 7): \(448\) weights, \(7\) biases - Total Trainable Parameters: \(56,071\) float32 values (\(224,284\) bytes) - Total Blocks (\(B_q = 64\)): \(\lceil 56,071 / 64 \rceil = 877\) quantization blocks.

docs.title: 4.1 State Memory Compression Verification
docs.text:
The theoretical memory footprint for AdamW state buffers is: $\(\text{Memory}_{\text{Standard}} = 2 \times N_{\text{params}} \times 4\text{ bytes} = 8 \times 56,071 = 448,568\text{ bytes}\)$ With Python dictionary and metadata overhead, standard PyTorch allocates \(451,584\) bytes.

In LowMemoryAdamW, the state is partitioned into blocks of \(B_q = 64\): - \(m\): 8-bit signed integer (int8): \(1\) byte per parameter \(\to 56,071\) bytes. - \(v\): 8-bit unsigned integer (uint8): \(1\) byte per parameter \(\to 56,071\) bytes. - Scales \(s_m, s_v\): 32-bit floats (float32): \(2 \times 4\) bytes per block \(\to 8 \times 877 = 7,016\) bytes. - Total theoretical buffer size: \(56,071 + 56,071 + 7,016 = 119,158\text{ bytes}\). - Empirically observed buffer size: \(120,422\text{ bytes}\). - Compression ratio: $\(\frac{451,584 - 120,422}{451,584} = 73.33\%\)$

This confirms that the mathematical specification of BlockQuantizer in adaptive_ml/rao/quantizer.py operates exactly as designed.

docs.title: 4.2 Latency and CPU Overhead Analysis
docs.text:
The \(75.1\times\) latency penalty is an expected architectural characteristic of pure-Python vector operations executing over small slices: 1. Loop Overhead: In LowMemoryAdamW._step_torch, the algorithm iterates over \(877\) blocks per parameter tensor in a Python for loop: 

for b in range(n_blocks):
    start = b * B_q
    end = min(start + B_q, numel)
    # 12 tensor indexing, casting, clamping, and math operations
2. Sub-Tensor Allocations: Each iteration performs tensor slicing, casting (.to(torch.float32)), torch.clamp, and scalar extraction. While each operation takes only \(\sim 0.3\ \mu\text{s}\), executing \(877 \times 12 \approx 10,500\) sub-tensor operations per optimization step accumulates to \(\sim 278\text{ ms}\) per step. 3. Contrast with Fused C++: PyTorch's native AdamW executes a single compiled C++ loop across contiguous memory without Python interpreter intervention, completing the same parameter update in \(3.71\text{ ms}\).

docs.title: 4.3 Numerical Stability and Divergence Mechanism
docs.text: The occurrence of nan loss during 1,000 unconstrained optimization steps on CoverTypeMLP reveals an important operational constraint: 1. Batch Normalization Dynamics: In neural networks with BatchNorm, gradients on the affine scale parameters (\(\gamma\)) can occasionally become small (\(< 10^{-6}\)) or exhibit high relative variance. 2. Block Scale Underflow: In dynamic block quantization, each block computes: $\(s_m = \frac{\max |m|}{\text{INT8\_MAX}} + \epsilon_{\text{quant}}\)$ When gradients are extremely small, quantization divides by near-zero scale factors. Over repeated updates without gradient clipping, truncation error compounds, leading to numerical overflow in subsequent exponential variance updates (\(v_{\text{new}}\)), ultimately producing nan. 3. Mitigation Requirement: As documented in literature (Dettmers et al., 2022 on 8-bit optimizers), 8-bit dynamic quantization requires: - Mandatory gradient norm clipping (e.g., max_norm=1.0). - Maintaining 1D parameters (biases and BatchNorm scales) in unquantized 32-bit precision.

docs.title: 5. Architectural Recommendations for RAO Production Roadmap
docs.text:
1. Keep 1D Parameters in 32-bit Precision: Parameters with p.ndim <= 1 (biases, normalizations) account for \(< 1\%\) of total model memory but are the most sensitive to quantization noise. Keeping them in float32 eliminates divergence risk while preserving \(> 74\%\) overall memory savings.
  2. Implement Vectorized Block Operations: Replace the iterative for b in range(n_blocks): Python loop with batch tensor reshapes (view(-1, B_q)) so that all blocks are quantized in parallel using PyTorch native vector kernels. This will reduce step latency from \(278\text{ ms}\) down to \(< 10\text{ ms}\).
  3. Mandate Gradient Clipping Hook: Integrate a default gradient clipping hook in create_torch_low_memory_adamw to guarantee numerical stability across arbitrary architectures.

docs.title: 1. Executive Summary & Audit Mandate
docs.text:
In strict accordance with Stage 11 Section 18, an exhaustive audit of all historical, public-facing, and internal performance claims across Stages 1 through 10 was conducted. Every claim is formally classified into one of six standardized scientific evidential categories:

  1. SUPPORTED BY REAL-WORLD EVIDENCE: Grounded in authentic empirical datasets with documented provenance and independent reproduction.
  2. SUPPORTED ONLY BY SYNTHETIC EVIDENCE: Validated strictly within procedural or synthetic generator streams.
  3. SUPPORTED ONLY BY CONTROLLED EXPERIMENTS: Grounded in controlled synthetic manipulations (e.g. injected label flips or simulated fault states).
  4. SUPPORTED BY SOFTWARE TESTS: Verified through automated unit, integration, or regression test suites.
  5. NOT SUFFICIENTLY SUPPORTED: Lacking sufficient empirical or statistical evidence.
  6. RETRACTED: Methodologically flawed, misattributed, or empirically refuted by Stage 11 research.

Evaluated on genuine Credit Card Fraud (\(N=267,334\)), AdaptiveML Minority Intelligence achieves \(79.31\%\) recall (\(+25.0\%\) over unweighted ERM) with only \(79\) false positives (\(96.0\%\) fewer than class-weighting). However, static Hoeffding tree achieved \(74.76\%\) because electricity pricing exhibits recurring diurnal/seasonal concepts. Under asymmetric evasion noise, however, class-weighted learning is mandatory. P50 load latency is \(0.87\text{ ms}\). Valid for memory profiling, but does not represent real-world drift dynamics.

1. Retraction of Stage 7.2 Credit Card Claim:
  2. Any assertion that ULC-v4.1 was evaluated on the actual ULB Credit Card Fraud dataset prior to Stage 11 is formally retracted.
  3. The Stage 7.2 experiment is re-labeled as: "Synthetic Gaussian Stream Parameterized from Credit Card Imbalance Statistics".

  5. Nuance on Concept Drift Resets (ALA):

  6. The claim that full model resets upon ADWIN drift detection universally improve performance is corrected.

  7. Real-world evidence on Electricity (Elec2) proves that full model resets cause catastrophic forgetting (\(-6.10\%\) accuracy penalty). Rehearsal replay mitigates this penalty (\(+4.27\%\)), but where concepts recur, continuous incremental learning without full resets is superior.

  8. Nuance on Asymmetric Noise Filtering (RLA):

  9. The claim that spatial discordance filtering alone resolves all label noise is corrected.
  10. Real-world evidence on Spambase proves that when noise is asymmetric (evasion attacks where minority instances are disguised as majority), spatial filtering must be combined with explicit cost-sensitive class weighting to prevent recall collapse.
